अर्च्या नित्यं संनिधानात्तत्र गौरी न संशयः .
अक्षारलवणं रात्रौ भुंक्ते चैव सुवाग्यता . . 12
text_mt: She should constantly worship Gaurī who is present there, without a doubt; / and restrained in speech, she eats in the night food free of alkaline matter and salt.

sanskrit_iast:
gaurī sannihitā nityaṃ bhūmau prastaraśāyinī3 .
evaṃ niyamayuktasya4 devyā yatsamudāhṛtam . . 13
meaning:
गौरी सन्निहिता नित्यं भूमौ प्रस्तरशायिनी3 .
एवं नियमयुक्तस्य4 देव्या यत्समुदाहृतम् . . 13
text_mt: Gaurī is constantly present, sleeping on the ground on a spread of grass. / What was proclaimed by the goddess for one who maintains such a discipline,

sanskrit_iast:
tacchṛṇuṣva mahābāho kathyamānaṃ mahāphalam .
bhartāraṃ tu labhetkanyā yaṃ vācchati mano'nugam . . 14
meaning:
तच्छृणुष्व महाबाहो कथ्यमानं महाफलम् .
भर्तारं तु लभेत्कन्या यं वाच्छति मनोऽनुगम् . . 14
text_mt: listen to that great fruit being described, O mighty-armed one: / an unmarried girl will obtain the husband whom she desires in accordance with her heart.

sanskrit_iast:
suciraṃ saha vai bhartrā krīḍayitvā5 ihaiva sā .
santatiṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya saha tenaiva gacchati . . 15
meaning:
सुचिरं सह वै भर्त्रा क्रीडयित्वा5 इहैव सा .
सन्ततिं च प्रतिष्ठाप्य सह तेनैव गच्छति . . 15
text_mt: Having sported for a very long time in this very world with her husband, / and having established her lineage, she departs along with him.

sanskrit_iast:
helilokaṃ candralokaṃ lokaṃ citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ .
gatvā yāti sado rājanvāmadevasya bhārata . . 16
meaning:
हेलिलोकं चन्द्रलोकं लोकं चित्रशिखण्डिनः .
गत्वा याति सदो राजन्वामदेवस्य भारत . . 16
text_mt: Having gone to the world of the sun, the world of the moon, and the world of Citraśikhaṇḍin, / she goes, O king, to the assembly of Vāmadeva, O Bhārata.

sanskrit_iast:
vidhavā tu yadā rājandevyā vrataparāyaṇā6 .
bharttāraṃ niyatā nityaṃ sadārcanaparāyaṇā . . 17
meaning:
विधवा तु यदा राजन्देव्या व्रतपरायणा6 .
भर्त्तारं नियता नित्यं सदार्चनपरायणा . . 17
text_mt: When a widow, O king, is devoted to the goddess’s votive observance, / restrained, always intent on the perpetual worship of her husband,

sanskrit_iast:
iha cotsṛjya dehaṃ svaṃ dṛṣṭvā haripure priyam .
ākṣipya yamadūtebhyaḥ saha bhartrā rameddivi . . 18
meaning:
इह चोत्सृज्य देहं स्वं दृष्ट्वा हरिपुरे प्रियम् .
आक्षिप्य यमदूतेभ्यः सह भर्त्रा रमेद्दिवि . . 18
text_mt: she leaves her body here, sees her beloved in the city of Hari, / snatches him from the messengers of Yama, and rejoices with her husband in heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
varṣakoṭiṃ daśaguṇāṃ ramitvā sā ihāgatā .
bhartrā sahaiva pūrvoktaṃ labhate phalamīpsitam . . 19
meaning:
वर्षकोटिं दशगुणां रमित्वा सा इहागता .
भर्त्रा सहैव पूर्वोक्तं लभते फलमीप्सितम् . . 19
text_mt: Having rejoiced there for a ten-fold crore of years, she comes back to this world, / and along with her husband she obtains the previously described desired fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
indrāṇyāpi vratamidaṃ putrārthinyā narādhipa .
labdhaḥ putro vratasyānte jayanto nāma nāmataḥ . . 1.21.20
meaning:
इन्द्राण्यापि व्रतमिदं पुत्रार्थिन्या नराधिप .
लब्धः पुत्रो व्रतस्यान्ते जयन्तो नाम नामतः . . 1.21.20
text_mt: This votive observance was also observed by Indrāṇī when she desired a son, O ruler of men; / at the end of the votive observance a son was obtained, named Jayanta by name.

sanskrit_iast:
arundhatyā tathā cīrṇaṃ vaśiṣṭhaṃ prati kāmataḥ .
dṛśyate divi cādyāpi vaśiṣṭhasya samīpataḥ . . 21
meaning:
अरुन्धत्या तथा चीर्णं वशिष्ठं प्रति कामतः .
दृश्यते दिवि चाद्यापि वशिष्ठस्य समीपतः . . 21
text_mt: So too it was performed by Arundhatī out of love for Vasiṣṭha; / and even today she is seen in the sky near Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit_iast:
rohiṇyā lavaṇatyāgātsapannīgaṇamardanam .
labdhaṃ devyāḥ prasādena saubhāgyamacalaṃ divi . . 22
meaning:
रोहिण्या लवणत्यागात्सपन्नीगणमर्दनम् .
लब्धं देव्याः प्रसादेन सौभाग्यमचलं दिवि . . 22
text_mt: By giving up salt, Rohiṇī obtained the subjugation of her co-wives / and unshakeable good fortune in heaven, through the grace of the goddess.

sanskrit_iast:
ityeṣā tithirityeva tṛtīyā lokapūjitā .
sadā viśeṣataḥ puṇyā vaiśākhe māsi yā bhavet . . 23
meaning:
इत्येषा तिथिरित्येव तृतीया लोकपूजिता .
सदा विशेषतः पुण्या वैशाखे मासि या भवेत् . . 23
text_mt: In this way, this third lunar day is revered by the world; / it is always especially holy when it falls in the month of Vaiśākha.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyā bhādrapade māsi māghepyevaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
māghe bhādrapade cāpi strīṇāṃ dhanyā1 pracakṣate . . 24
meaning:
पुण्या भाद्रपदे मासि माघेप्येवं न संशयः .
माघे भाद्रपदे चापि स्त्रीणां धन्या1 प्रचक्षते . . 24
text_mt: It is holy in the month of Bhādrapada, and also in Māgha, without a doubt; / in Māgha and in Bhādrapada it is proclaimed to bring good fortune to women.

sanskrit_iast:
sādhāraṇī tu vaiśākhe sarvalokasya bhārata .
māghamāse tṛtīyāyāṃ guḍasya lavaṇasya ca . .
dānaṃ śreyaskaraṃ rājanstrīṇāṃ2 ca puruṣasya ca . . 25
meaning:
साधारणी तु वैशाखे सर्वलोकस्य भारत .
माघमासे तृतीयायां गुडस्य लवणस्य च . .
दानं श्रेयस्करं राजन्स्त्रीणां2 च पुरुषस्य च . . 25
text_mt: In Vaiśākha it is common to all people, O Bhārata. / On the third lunar day in the month of Māgha, the gift of jaggery and salt / brings welfare, O king, to women and to men.

sanskrit_iast:
guḍena tuṣyate datto lavaṇena tu viśvabhūḥ .
guḍapūpāstu dātavyā māsi bhādrapade tathā . . 26
meaning:
गुडेन तुष्यते दत्तो लवणेन तु विश्वभूः .
गुडपूपास्तु दातव्या मासि भाद्रपदे तथा . . 26
text_mt: Datta is pleased with jaggery, while Viśvabhū is pleased with salt; / and cakes made of jaggery should be given likewise in the month of Bhādrapada.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tu māghasya vāmadevasya prītaye .
vāridānaṃ praśastaṃ syānmodakānāṃ ca bhārata . . 27
meaning:
तृतीयायां तु माघस्य वामदेवस्य प्रीतये .
वारिदानं प्रशस्तं स्यान्मोदकानां च भारत . . 27
text_mt: On the third lunar day of Māgha, for the pleasure of Vāmadeva, / the gift of water and sweetmeat balls is commended, O Bhārata.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśākhe māsi rājendra tṛtīyā candanasya ca .
vāriṇā tuṣyate vedhā modakairbhīma eva hi . .
dānāttu candanasyeha kañjajo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 28
meaning:
वैशाखे मासि राजेन्द्र तृतीया चन्दनस्य च .
वारिणा तुष्यते वेधा मोदकैर्भीम एव हि . .
दानात्तु चन्दनस्येह कञ्जजो नात्र संशयः . . 28
text_mt: In the month of Vaiśākha, O best of kings, on the third lunar day, / the Creator is pleased with water and sandalwood, and Bhīma indeed with sweetmeat balls; / and from the gift of sandalwood here, the Lotus-born is pleased, there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
yātveṣā kuruśārdūla vaiśākhe māsi vai tithiḥ .
tṛtīyā sā'kṣayā loke gīrvāṇairabhinanditā . . 29
meaning:
यात्वेषा कुरुशार्दूल वैशाखे मासि वै तिथिः .
तृतीया साऽक्षया लोके गीर्वाणैरभिनन्दिता . . 29
text_mt: The lunar day which falls on the third in the month of Vaiśākha, O tiger among the Kurus, / is praised in the world as Akṣayā, applauded by the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
āgateyaṃ mahābāho bhūri candraṃ vasuvratā .
kaladhautaṃ tathānnaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ cāpi viśeṣataḥ . .
yadyaddattaṃ tvakṣayaṃ syātteneyamakṣayā smṛtā . . 1.21.30
meaning:
आगतेयं महाबाहो भूरि चन्द्रं वसुव्रता .
कलधौतं तथान्नं च घृतं चापि विशेषतः . .
यद्यद्दत्तं त्वक्षयं स्यात्तेनेयमक्षया स्मृता . . 1.21.30
text_mt: When this arrives, O mighty-armed one, bringing abundant vows of wealth, / gold, food, and especially clarified butter— / whatever is given becomes imperishable; therefore it is remembered as Akṣayā.

sanskrit_iast:
yatkiñciddīyate dānaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu .
tatsarvamakṣayaṃ syādvai teneyamakṣayā smṛtā . . 31
meaning:
यत्किञ्चिद्दीयते दानं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु .
तत्सर्वमक्षयं स्याद्वै तेनेयमक्षया स्मृता . . 31
text_mt: Whatever gift is given, whether small or great, / all of that indeed becomes imperishable; therefore it is remembered as Akṣayā.

sanskrit_iast:
yo'syāṃ dadāti karakanvāribījasamanvitān .
sa yāti puruṣo vīra lokaṃ vai hemamālinaḥ . . 32
meaning:
योऽस्यां ददाति करकन्वारिबीजसमन्वितान् .
स याति पुरुषो वीर लोकं वै हेममालिनः . . 32
text_mt: The man who on this day gives water pots provided with water and seeds, / that heroic man goes to the world of the Golden-Garlanded One.

sanskrit_iast:
ityeṣā kathitā vīra tṛtīyā tithiruttamā .
yāmupoṣya naro rājannṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ bhajet . . 33
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ brāhme parvaṇi tṛtīyākalpavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 21 .
caturthītithivratamāhātmyam
meaning:
इत्येषा कथिता वीर तृतीया तिथिरुत्तमा .
यामुपोष्य नरो राजन्नृद्धिं वृद्धिं श्रियं भजेत् . . 33
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि तृतीयाकल्पविधिवर्णनं
नामैकविंशोऽध्यायः . 21 .
चतुर्थीतिथिव्रतमाहात्म्यम्
text_mt:
Thus has been declared, O hero, the supreme third lunar day, / by fasting on which a man, O king, attains prosperity, growth, and fortune.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, entitled “Description of the Rules for the Observance of the Third Lunar Day”, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Śatārdhasāhasrī [Saṃhitā] of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
The greatness of the votive observance of the fourth lunar day

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
caturthyāṃ tu sadā rājannirāhāravratānvitaḥ .
dattvā tilānnaṃ viprasya svayaṃ bhuṃkte tilaudanam . . 1
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
चतुर्थ्यां तु सदा राजन्निराहारव्रतान्वितः .
दत्त्वा तिलान्नं विप्रस्य स्वयं भुंक्ते तिलौदनम् . . 1
text_mt: Sumantu said: / On the fourth lunar day, O king, always observing a fast, / having given sesamum food to a vipra, he himself eats sesamum rice.
title: Caturthīkalpavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
varṣadvaye samāptirhi vratasya tu yadā bhavet .
vināyakastasya tuṣṭo dadāti phalamīhitam1 . . 2
meaning:
वर्षद्वये समाप्तिर्हि व्रतस्य तु यदा भवेत् .
विनायकस्तस्य तुष्टो ददाति फलमीहितम्1 . . 2
text_mt: When the completion of the votive observance takes place after two years, / Vināyaka, being pleased, bestows upon him his desired fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
yāti bhāgyanivāsaṃ hi krīḍate vibhavaiḥ saha .
iha cāgatya puṇyānte divyo divyavapuryaśāḥ . . 3
meaning:
याति भाग्यनिवासं हि क्रीडते विभवैः सह .
इह चागत्य पुण्यान्ते दिव्यो दिव्यवपुर्यशाः . . 3
text_mt: He goes to the abode of fortune and sports with riches; / and coming back to this world at the end of his merit, divine, with a divine body and fame,

sanskrit_iast:
matimāndhṛtimānvāgmī bhāgyavānkāmakāravān2 .
asādhyānyapi sādhyeha kṣaṇādeva mahāntyapi . . 4
meaning:
मतिमान्धृतिमान्वाग्मी भाग्यवान्कामकारवान्2 .
असाध्यान्यपि साध्येह क्षणादेव महान्त्यपि . . 4
text_mt: intelligent, resolute, eloquent, fortunate, acting as he desires, / accomplishing instantly even insurmountable and great tasks in this world,

sanskrit_iast:
hantyaśvarathasampannaṃ ṣalīputrasahāyavān .
rājā bhavati dīrghāyuḥ saptajanmānyasau nṛpa . .
etaddadāti santuṣṭo vighnahantā4 vināyakaḥ . . 5
meaning:
हन्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नं षलीपुत्रसहायवान् .
राजा भवति दीर्घायुः सप्तजन्मान्यसौ नृप . .
एतद्ददाति सन्तुष्टो विघ्नहन्ता4 विनायकः . . 5
text_mt: equipped with elephants, horses, and chariots, accompanied by strong sons, / he becomes a long-lived king for seven births, O king. / Pleased, the slayer of obstacles, Vināyaka, grants this.

sanskrit_iast:
śatānīka uvāca
vighnaḥ kasya kṛtastena yena vighnavināyakaḥ .
etadvadasva vighneśa vighnakāraṇamadya me . . 6
meaning:
शतानीक उवाच
विघ्नः कस्य कृतस्तेन येन विघ्नविनायकः .
एतद्वदस्व विघ्नेश विघ्नकारणमद्य मे . . 6
text_mt: Śatānīka said: / For whom was an obstacle created by him, on account of which he is the Vināyaka of obstacles? / Tell me today this cause of obstacles, O lord of obstacles.

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
kaumāre lakṣaṇe puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ ca sukṛte kṛte .
vighnaṃ cakāra vighneśo gāṅgeyasya vināyakaḥ . . 7
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
कौमारे लक्षणे पुंसां स्त्रीणां च सुकृते कृते .
विघ्नं चकार विघ्नेशो गाङ्गेयस्य विनायकः . . 7
text_mt:
Sumantu said:
When the treatise on the marks of men and women was composed by Kumāra,
Vināyaka, the lord of obstacles, caused an obstacle for the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ tu vighnaṃ viditvāsau kārttikeyo ruṣānvitaḥ .
utkṛṣya dantaṃ tasyāsyāddhantuṃ taṃ ca samudyataḥ . . 8
meaning:
तं तु विघ्नं विदित्वासौ कार्त्तिकेयो रुषान्वितः .
उत्कृष्य दन्तं तस्यास्याद्धन्तुं तं च समुद्यतः . . 8
text_mt:
Knowing of that obstacle, Kārttikeya, filled with wrath,
pulled a tusk from his mouth and prepared to slay him.

sanskrit_iast:
nivāryāpṛcchaddeveśo roṣaḥ kāryaḥ kutastvayā .
taṃ cācakhyau sa pitre vai kṛtaṃ pūruṣalakṣaṇam . .
tatra vighnakṛte mahyaṃ yoṣitā na ca lakṣaṇam . . 9
meaning:
निवार्यापृच्छद्देवेशो रोषः कार्यः कुतस्त्वया .
तं चाचख्यौ स पित्रे वै कृतं पूरुषलक्षणम् . .
तत्र विघ्नकृते मह्यं योषिता न च लक्षणम् . . 9

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca mahādevaḥ prahasantsvasutaṃ kila .
mama kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ putra paśyase tvaṃ vadasva me . . 1.22.10
meaning:
अथोवाच महादेवः प्रहसन्त्स्वसुतं किल .
मम किं लक्षणं पुत्र पश्यसे त्वं वदस्व मे . . 1.22.10
text_mt:
Then Mahādeva, laughing, said to his son:
“What mark of mine, O son, do you see? Tell me.”

sanskrit_iast:
sa covāca kare tubhyaṃ kapālaṃ dvijalakṣitam .
avicāreṇa saṃsthāpyaṃ kapālī tena cocyate . .
sa tallakṣaṇamādāya samudre prākṣipadruṣā . . 11
meaning:
स चोवाच करे तुभ्यं कपालं द्विजलक्षितम् .
अविचारेण संस्थाप्यं कपाली तेन चोच्यते . .
स तल्लक्षणमादाय समुद्रे प्राक्षिपद्रुषा . . 11
text_mt:
And he said: “In your hand a skull marked by a twice-born [Brahmin]
was placed without deliberation; therefore you are called Kapālī.”
In anger he took that treatise on marks and cast it into the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
atha devasamāje vai pravṛtte brahmarudrayoḥ .
ahaṃ jyāyānahaṃ jyāyānvivādo'bhūttayordvayoḥ . .
tava saṃbhūtyabhijño'sti māṃ tu veda na kaścana . . 12
meaning:
अथ देवसमाजे वै प्रवृत्ते ब्रह्मरुद्रयोः .
अहं ज्यायानहं ज्यायान्विवादोऽभूत्तयोर्द्वयोः . .
तव संभूत्यभिज्ञोऽस्ति मां तु वेद न कश्चन . . 12
text_mt:
Then, when an assembly of the gods had convened between Brahmā and Rudra,
a dispute arose between the two of them: “I am greater!” “I am greater!”
[Rudra said:] “There is one who knows of your birth, but no one knows of mine.”

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ śive'ti bruvati brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ .
muktāṭṭahāsaṃ provāca tvāmahaṃ veditā bhava . . 13
meaning:
एवं शिवेऽति ब्रुवति ब्रह्मणः पञ्चमं शिरः .
मुक्ताट्टहासं प्रोवाच त्वामहं वेदिता भव . . 13
text_mt:
As Śiva was saying this, the fifth head of Brahmā,
bursting into a loud laugh, said: “I know you, O Bhava!”

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ bruvantu rudreṇa brāhmaṃ hayaśiro mahat .
nakhāgreṇa nikṛttaṃ ca tasyaiva ca kare sthitam . . 14
meaning:
एवं ब्रुवन्तु रुद्रेण ब्राह्मं हयशिरो महत् .
नखाग्रेण निकृत्तं च तस्यैव च करे स्थितम् . . 14
text_mt:
As it spoke thus, the great horse-head of Brahmā
was severed by Rudra with the tip of his fingernail and remained right in his hand.

sanskrit_iast:
karasthenaiva tenāsāvāgacchadyatra vai hariḥ .
tapastepe tadā merau tatrāsau bhagavānvaśī . . 15
meaning:
करस्थेनैव तेनासावागच्छद्यत्र वै हरिः .
तपस्तेपे तदा मेरौ तत्रासौ भगवान्वशी . . 15
text_mt:
With it remaining in his hand, he went to where Hari was;
the lord, self-controlled, was then performing austerities on Mount Meru.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtte hayaśire tasminsthānāttasmāttu brahmaṇaḥ .
roṣādviniḥsṛtastvanyaḥ puruṣaḥ śvetakuṇḍalī . . 16
meaning:
कृत्ते हयशिरे तस्मिन्स्थानात्तस्मात्तु ब्रह्मणः .
रोषाद्विनिःसृतस्त्वन्यः पुरुषः श्वेतकुण्डली . . 16
text_mt:
When that horse-head was severed, from that place of Brahmā
another man wearing white earrings came forth in wrath.

sanskrit_iast:
kavacī saśiraskaśca saśaraḥ saśarāsanaḥ .
anirdeśyavapuḥ sragvī kiṃ karomi sa cābravīt . . 17
meaning:
कवची सशिरस्कश्च सशरः सशरासनः .
अनिर्देश्यवपुः स्रग्वी किं करोमि स चाब्रवीत् . . 17
text_mt:
Armoured, wearing a helmet, with arrows and a bow,
of indescribable form and wearing a garland, he said, “What shall I do?”

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca ruṣā brahmā hanyatāṃ sa sudurmatiḥ .
sa tu mārgeṇa rudrasya āgacchadroṣato drutam . . 18
meaning:
अथोवाच रुषा ब्रह्मा हन्यतां स सुदुर्मतिः .
स तु मार्गेण रुद्रस्य आगच्छद्रोषतो द्रुतम् . . 18
text_mt:
Then Brahmā said in fury, “Let that utterly wicked one be slain!”
And he went swiftly following Rudra's path in anger.

sanskrit_iast:
rudro'pi viṣṇutejobhiḥ praviṣṭaḥ sa tvadhiṣṭhitaḥ .
sa praviśya tadāpaśyattapantaṃ cottamaṃ tapaḥ . .
haro nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ vaikuṇṭhamaparājitam . . 19
meaning:
रुद्रोऽपि विष्णुतेजोभिः प्रविष्टः स त्वधिष्ठितः .
स प्रविश्य तदापश्यत्तपन्तं चोत्तमं तपः . .
हरो नारायणं देवं वैकुण्ठमपराजितम् . . 19
text_mt:
Rudra too, having entered, established himself in the splendours of Viṣṇu.
Having entered, Hara then saw the god Nārāyaṇa,
Vaikuṇṭha, the undefeated, performing supreme austerities.

sanskrit_iast:
haraṃ dṛṣṭvātha samprāptaṃ kāryaṃ cāsya vicintya ca .
uvāca śūlinaṃ devo bhindhi śūlena me bhujam . . 1.22.20
meaning:
हरं दृष्ट्वाथ सम्प्राप्तं कार्यं चास्य विचिन्त्य च .
उवाच शूलिनं देवो भिन्धि शूलेन मे भुजम् . . 1.22.20
text_mt:
Seeing Hara arrived and considering his purpose,
the god said to the trident-bearer, “Pierce my arm with your trident!”

sanskrit_iast: sa bibheda mahātejā bhujaṃ śūlena taṃ haraḥ . . 21
meaning: स बिभेद महातेजा भुजं शूलेन तं हरः . . 21
text_mt: Hara, possessing great splendour, pierced that arm with his trident.

sanskrit_iast:
śūlabhedādasṛkcordhvaṃ jagāmāvṛtya rodasī .
vinivṛtya tataḥ paścātkapāle nipapāta ha . . 22
meaning:
शूलभेदादसृक्चोर्ध्वं जगामावृत्य रोदसी .
विनिवृत्य ततः पश्चात्कपाले निपपात ह . . 22
text_mt:
From the piercing of the trident, blood went upward, covering heaven and earth;
then, turning back afterwards, it fell into the skull.

sanskrit_iast:
asṛkkapāle patitaṃ pradeśinyā vyavarddhayat .
yadā hi vinivṛttiḥ syāddevasya rudhiraṃ prati . . 23
meaning:
असृक्कपाले पतितं प्रदेशिन्या व्यवर्द्धयत् .
यदा हि विनिवृत्तिः स्याद्देवस्य रुधिरं प्रति . . 23
text_mt:
He caused the blood that had fallen into the skull to swell with his forefinger,
so that there might be a turning away of the god towards the blood.

sanskrit_iast:
tadā tu vyasṛjattoyaṃ sa kṛtvā vāruṇīṃ tanum .
toye pravṛtte'sṛgbhūte kapāle yatra tacchiraḥ . . 24
meaning:
तदा तु व्यसृजत्तोयं स कृत्वा वारुणीं तनुम् .
तोये प्रवृत्तेऽसृग्भूते कपाले यत्र तच्छिरः . . 24
text_mt:
Then, assuming a watery form, he released water.
When the water turned into blood in the skull where that head was,

sanskrit_iast:
kapāle tu pradeśinyā rudro'sau rudhire'sṛjat .
āmuktakavacaṃ raktaṃ raktakuṇḍalinaṃ naram . . 25
meaning:
कपाले तु प्रदेशिन्या रुद्रोऽसौ रुधिरेऽसृजत् .
आमुक्तकवचं रक्तं रक्तकुण्डलिनं नरम् . . 25
text_mt:
in the skull, with his forefinger, Rudra created in the blood
a man clad in armour, red, and wearing red earrings.

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca bhavaṃ devaṃ kiṃ karomīti mānada .
asāvapi sasarjātha śvetakuṇḍalinaṃ naram . . 26
meaning:
अथोवाच भवं देवं किं करोमीति मानद .
असावपि ससर्जाथ श्वेतकुण्डलिनं नरम् . . 26
text_mt:
Then he said to the god Bhava, “What shall I do, O giver of honour?”
And he too then created a man wearing white earrings.

sanskrit_iast:
tāvubhau samayudhyetāṃ dhanuṣpravaradhāriṇau .
yathā rājanbalīyāṃsau kujaketū yugātyaye . . 27
meaning:
तावुभौ समयुध्येतां धनुष्प्रवरधारिणौ .
यथा राजन्बलीयांसौ कुजकेतू युगात्यये . . 27
text_mt:
The two of them, bearing excellent bows, fought together,
just as, O king, the two mighty planets Mars and Ketu fight at the end of an aeon.

sanskrit_iast:
tayostu yudhyatorevaṃ saṃvartaścādhiko gataḥ .
na cādṛśyata vijaya ekasyāpi tadā tayoḥ . . 28
meaning:
तयोस्तु युध्यतोरेवं संवर्तश्चाधिको गतः .
न चादृश्यत विजय एकस्यापि तदा तयोः . . 28
text_mt:
As the two were fighting thus, more than a cosmic dissolution elapsed,
and yet victory was not seen for either one of the two.

sanskrit_iast:
athāntarikṣe tau dṛṣṭvā vāguvācāśarīriṇī .
avatāro'tha bhavitā yuvayorhi mayā saha . . 29
meaning:
अथान्तरिक्षे तौ दृष्ट्वा वागुवाचाशरीरिणी .
अवतारोऽथ भविता युवयोर्हि मया सह . . 29
text_mt:
Then, seeing them, a bodiless voice spoke in the sky:
“An incarnation of the two of you shall come to pass along with me.

sanskrit_iast:
bhārāpanodaḥ karttavyaḥ pṛthivyarthe suraiḥ saha .
tadāścaryo hi bhavitā devakāryārthasiddhaye . . 1.22.30
meaning:
भारापनोदः कर्त्तव्यः पृथिव्यर्थे सुरैः सह .
तदाश्चर्यो हि भविता देवकार्यार्थसिद्धये . . 1.22.30
text_mt:
The removal of the burden must be accomplished for the sake of the earth, along with the gods;
then it will indeed be miraculous for the success of the gods' purpose.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūlokabhāvaṃ nirdhūya bhūyo gantā surālayam .
evamuktvā tu vaikuṇṭho dadāvekaṃ ravestadā . . 31
meaning:
भूलोकभावं निर्धूय भूयो गन्ता सुरालयम् .
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैकुण्ठो ददावेकं रवेस्तदा . . 31
text_mt:
Having cast off worldly existence, you shall go once again to the abode of the gods.”
Having spoken thus, Vaikuṇṭha then gave one to Ravi.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetakuṇḍalinaṃ dṛptaṃ1 taṃ jagrāha ravirmudā .
indrasyāpi tataḥ paścādraktakuṇḍalinaṃ dadau ..32
meaning:
श्वेतकुण्डलिनं दृप्तं1 तं जग्राह रविर्मुदा .
इन्द्रस्यापि ततः पश्चाद्रक्तकुण्डलिनं ददौ ..32
text_mt:
Ravi joyfully received the proud one with white earrings;
then, after that, he gave the one with red earrings to Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
jagrāha ca mudā yukta indraḥ svaṃ ca puraṃ yayau .
gatau ravīndrau pragṛhya puruṣau krodhasambhavau ..3 3
athovāca tadā rudraṃ devaḥ kamalasaṃsthitaḥ .
gaccha tvamapi kāpāle kapālavratacaryayā ..
avatāro vratasyāsya martyaloke bhaviṣyati .. 34
meaning:
जग्राह च मुदा युक्त इन्द्रः स्वं च पुरं ययौ .
गतौ रवीन्द्रौ प्रगृह्य पुरुषौ क्रोधसम्भवौ ..3 3
अथोवाच तदा रुद्रं देवः कमलसंस्थितः .
गच्छ त्वमपि कापाले कपालव्रतचर्यया ..
अवतारो व्रतस्यास्य मर्त्यलोके भविष्यति .. 34
text_mt:
Filled with joy, Indra received him and went to his own city.
When Ravi and Indra had departed, taking the two men born of anger,
the god seated on the lotus then said to Rudra:
“You too, go, bearing the skull, performing the practice of the skull-observance;
there will be an incarnation of this observance in the mortal world.

sanskrit_iast:
ye ca vrataṃ tvadīyaṃ vai dhārayiṣyanti mānavāḥ .
na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ kiñcidbhaviteha paratra ca ..35
meaning:
ये च व्रतं त्वदीयं वै धारयिष्यन्ति मानवाः .
न तेषां दुर्लभं किञ्चिद्भवितेह परत्र च ..35
text_mt:
And whatever humans shall maintain this observance of yours,
nothing will be difficult for them to attain, here or in the hereafter.”

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ saṃlapya bahuśaḥ sumukhaṃ pratinandya ca .
āhūya ca samudraṃ sa pratyuvācāvicārayan ..36
meaning:
एवं संलप्य बहुशः सुमुखं प्रतिनन्द्य च .
आहूय च समुद्रं स प्रत्युवाचाविचारयन् ..36
text_mt:
Having conversed thus at length, and having cheered Sumukha,
he summoned the Ocean and replied without hesitation:

sanskrit_iast:
kuruṣvābharaṇaṃ2 strīṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yadvilakṣaṇam .
kārttikeyena yatproktaṃ tadvadasvāvicārayan .. 37
meaning:
कुरुष्वाभरणं2 स्त्रीणां लक्षणं यद्विलक्षणम् .
कार्त्तिकेयेन यत्प्रोक्तं तद्वदस्वाविचारयन् .. 37
text_mt:
“Make the marks that serve as ornaments for women, and those that are contrary;
proclaim without hesitation that which was spoken by Kārttikeya.”

sanskrit_iast:
sa cāha mama nāmnedaṃ bhavetpuruṣalakṣaṇam .
devena tatpratijñātamevametadbhaviṣyati ..38
meaning:
स चाह मम नाम्नेदं भवेत्पुरुषलक्षणम् .
देवेन तत्प्रतिज्ञातमेवमेतद्भविष्यति ..38
text_mt:
And he said: “Let this treatise on the marks of men be known by my name.”
The god agreed to that: “So shall it be!”

sanskrit_iast: kārttikeyena yatproktaṃ tadvadasvāvicārayan ..39
meaning: कार्त्तिकेयेन यत्प्रोक्तं तद्वदस्वाविचारयन् ..39
text_mt: “Proclaim without hesitation that which was spoken by Kārttikeya.

sanskrit_iast:
prayacchāsya viṣāṇaṃ vai niṣkṛṣṭaṃ yattvayā'dhunā .
avaśyameva tadbhūtaṃ bhavitavyaṃ tu kasyacit ..1.22.40
meaning:
प्रयच्छास्य विषाणं वै निष्कृष्टं यत्त्वयाऽधुना .
अवश्यमेव तद्भूतं भवितव्यं तु कस्यचित् ..1.22.40
text_mt:
Give back his tusk, which you pulled out just now;
for that must inevitably come to be for someone.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛte vināyakaṃ tadvai daivayogānna kāmataḥ .
gṛhāṇa etatsāmudraṃ yattvayā parikīrtitam ..41
meaning:
ऋते विनायकं तद्वै दैवयोगान्न कामतः .
गृहाण एतत्सामुद्रं यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम् ..41
text_mt:
Except for Vināyaka, it happened by destiny and not by desire.
Receive this Sāmudra [treatise] which was proclaimed by you.

sanskrit_iast:
strīpuṃsorlakṣaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāmudramiti viśrutama .
imaṃ ca saviṣāṇaṃ vai kuru devavināyakama ..42
meaning:
स्त्रीपुंसोर्लक्षणं श्रेष्ठं सामुद्रमिति विश्रुतम .
इमं च सविषाणं वै कुरु देवविनायकम ..42
text_mt:
The excellent treatise on the marks of men and women is renowned as Sāmudra;
and make this god Vināyaka possessed of his tusk.”

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca ca deveśaṃ bāhuleyaḥ samatsaram .
viṣāṇaṃ dadmi cāsyāhaṃ tava vākyānna saṃśayaḥ . . 43
meaning:
अथोवाच च देवेशं बाहुलेयः समत्सरम् .
विषाणं दद्मि चास्याहं तव वाक्यान्न संशयः . . 43
text_mt:
Then Bāhuleya spoke with envy to the lord of the gods:
“I give him the tusk at your command, no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā tvayaṃ viṣāṇaṃ ca muktvā tu vicariṣyati .
tadā viṣāṇamuktaḥ sanbhasma aitaṃ kariṣyati . . 44
meaning:
यदा त्वयं विषाणं च मुक्त्वा तु विचरिष्यति .
तदा विषाणमुक्तः सन्भस्म ऐतं करिष्यति . . 44
text_mt:
However, when he roams about having set aside this tusk,
then, stripped of the tusk, he shall reduce this to ashes.”

sanskrit_iast:
evamastviti taṃ coktvā viṣāṇaṃ tatkare dadau .
vināyakasya deveśaḥ kārtikeyamate sthitaḥ . . 45
meaning:
एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा विषाणं तत्करे ददौ .
विनायकस्य देवेशः कार्तिकेयमते स्थितः . . 45
text_mt:
Saying to him, “So be it,” the lord of the gods, abiding by Kārttikeya's view,
placed that tusk in the hand of Vināyaka.

sanskrit_iast:
saviṣāṇakaro'dyāpi dṛśyate pratimā nṛpa .
bhīmasūnormahābāhorvighnaṃ karttuṃ mahātmanaḥ . . 46
meaning:
सविषाणकरोऽद्यापि दृश्यते प्रतिमा नृप .
भीमसूनोर्महाबाहोर्विघ्नं कर्त्तुं महात्मनः . . 46
text_mt:
Even today an image is seen with a tusk in hand, O king,
to cause an obstacle for the mighty-armed, great-souled son of Bhīma.

sanskrit_iast:
etadrahasyaṃ devānāṃ mayā te samudāhṛtam .
yatra devo na vai veda devānāṃ bhuvi durlabham . . 47
meaning:
एतद्रहस्यं देवानां मया ते समुदाहृतम् .
यत्र देवो न वै वेद देवानां भुवि दुर्लभम् . . 47
text_mt:
This secret of the gods has been related to you by me,
which a god does not know, hard to attain in the world of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
mayā prasannena tava guhyametadudāhṛtam .
kathitaṃ tithisaṃyoge vināyakakathāmṛtam . . 48
meaning:
मया प्रसन्नेन तव गुह्यमेतदुदाहृतम् .
कथितं तिथिसंयोगे विनायककथामृतम् . . 48
text_mt:
Being pleased, I have related this secret to you;
the nectar-like tale of Vināyaka, narrated in connection with the lunar day.

sanskrit_iast:
ya idaṃ śrāvayedvidvānbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān .
kṣatriyāṃśca svavṛttisthānviṭśūdrāṃśca guṇānvitān . . 49
meaning:
य इदं श्रावयेद्विद्वान्ब्राह्मणान्वेदपारगान् .
क्षत्रियांश्च स्ववृत्तिस्थान्विट्शूद्रांश्च गुणान्वितान् . . 49
text_mt:
Whatever learned man recites this to Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas,
to Kṣatriyas abiding in their proper duties, and to Vaiśyas and Śūdras endowed with virtues,

sanskrit_iast:
na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcidiha cāmutra vidyate .
na ca durgatimāpnoti na ca yāti parābhavam . . 1.22.50
meaning:
न तस्य दुर्लभं किञ्चिदिह चामुत्र विद्यते .
न च दुर्गतिमाप्नोति न च याति पराभवम् . . 1.22.50
text_mt:
nothing is difficult for him to attain, here or in the world beyond;
he neither meets with misfortune nor suffers defeat.

sanskrit_iast:
nirvighnaṃ sarvakāryāṇi sādhayennātra saṃśayaḥ .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ cāpi vindeta bharatottama . . 51
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpavarṇanaṃ
nāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 22 .
vighna-vināyakakathāvarṇanam
meaning:
निर्विघ्नं सर्वकार्याणि साधयेन्नात्र संशयः .
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं श्रियं चापि विन्देत भरतोत्तम . . 51
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पवर्णनं
नाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः . 22 .
विघ्न-विनायककथावर्णनम्
text_mt:
He will accomplish all undertakings without hindrance, there is no doubt in this; / and he will obtain prosperity, increase, and fortune, O best of the Bharatas.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "Description of the Caturthī Rite", in the Brāhma Book of the holy and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Narrative of Vighna-Vināyaka

sanskrit_iast:
śatānīka uvāca
kenāyaṃ bhīmajo vipra pramathādhipatiḥ kṛtaḥ .
bhartṛtve cāpi vighnānāmadhikārī kathaṃ babhau . . 1
meaning:
शतानीक उवाच
केनायं भीमजो विप्र प्रमथाधिपतिः कृतः .
भर्तृत्वे चापि विघ्नानामधिकारी कथं बभौ . . 1
text_mt: Śatānīka said: / By whom was this son of Bhīmā made the lord of the Pramathas, O vipra? / And how did he become the officer presiding over obstacles?
title: Caturthīkalpavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra yadayaṃ vighnakārakaḥ .
yairvāpi vighnakaraṇairniryukto'pi vināyakaḥ . .
tatte vacmi mahābāho śṛṇuṣvaikamanādhunā . . 2
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र यदयं विघ्नकारकः .
यैर्वापि विघ्नकरणैर्निर्युक्तोऽपि विनायकः . .
तत्ते वच्मि महाबाहो शृणुष्वैकमनाधुना . . 2
text_mt: Sumantu said: / I am well questioned, O king of kings, as to why he causes obstacles, / and by what obstacle-causing acts Vināyaka was appointed. / I shall tell you that, O mighty-armed one; listen now with a single-minded focus.

sanskrit_iast:
ādye kṛtayuge vīra prajāsargamavāpa ha .
dṛṣṭvā karmāṇi siddhāni vinā vighnena bhārata . . 3
meaning:
आद्ये कृतयुगे वीर प्रजासर्गमवाप ह .
दृष्ट्वा कर्माणि सिद्धानि विना विघ्नेन भारत . . 3
text_mt: In the first Kṛtayuga, O hero, the creation of beings came about. / Seeing actions succeed without obstacle, O Bhārata,

sanskrit_iast:
agatakleśāṃ prajāṃ dṛṣṭvā garvitāṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa .
bahuśaścintayityā tu idaṃ karma mahīpate . . 4
meaning:
अगतक्लेशां प्रजां दृष्ट्वा गर्वितां कृत्स्नशो नृप .
बहुशश्चिन्तयित्या तु इदं कर्म महीपते . . 4
text_mt: and seeing beings free from distress and wholly arrogant, O king, / thinking repeatedly about this deed, O ruler of the earth,

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakaḥ samṛddhyarthaṃ prajānāṃ viniyojitaḥ .
gaṇānāṃ cādhipatye ca bhīmaḥ kañjajasāttvataiḥ . .
tatopasṛṣṭo yastasya lakṣaṇāni nibodha me . . 5
meaning:
विनायकः समृद्ध्यर्थं प्रजानां विनियोजितः .
गणानां चाधिपत्ये च भीमः कञ्जजसात्त्वतैः . .
ततोपसृष्टो यस्तस्य लक्षणानि निबोध मे . . 5
text_mt: Vināyaka was appointed for the prosperity of beings / and for the lordship over the Gaṇas—the terrible one, by Brahmā and the Sāttvatas. / Hear from me the signs of one who is possessed by him:

sanskrit_iast:
svapnevagāhate'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃśca paśyati .
kāṣāyavāsasaścaiva kravyādāṃścādhirohati . . 6
meaning:
स्वप्नेवगाहतेऽत्यर्थं जलं मुण्डांश्च पश्यति .
काषायवाससश्चैव क्रव्यादांश्चाधिरोहति . . 6
text_mt: In a dream he repeatedly plunges into water and sees shaven-headed men / and men wearing ochre garments, and he mounts carnivorous beasts.

sanskrit_iast:
antyajairgardabhairuṣṭraiḥ sahaikatrāvatiṣṭhate .
vrajamānastathātmānaṃ manyate'nugataṃ paraiḥ . . 7
meaning:
अन्त्यजैर्गर्दभैरुष्ट्रैः सहैकत्रावतिष्ठते .
व्रजमानस्तथात्मानं मन्यतेऽनुगतं परैः . . 7
text_mt: He stays in one place with outcasts, donkeys, and camels; / and as he walks, he imagines himself pursued by enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ .
karaṭārūḍhamātmānamambhasontaragaṃ tathā . . 8
meaning:
विमना विफलारम्भः संसीदत्यनिमित्ततः .
करटारूढमात्मानमम्भसोन्तरगं तथा . . 8
text_mt: Despondent, with all undertakings fruitless, he sinks down for no cause; / and in a dream he sees himself mounted on a crow, submerged in water,

sanskrit_iast:
pattibhiścāvṛtaṃ yāntaṃ saṅgamanāntikaṃ nṛpa .
paśyate kuruśārdūla svapnānte nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 9
meaning:
पत्तिभिश्चावृतं यान्तं सङ्गमनान्तिकं नृप .
पश्यते कुरुशार्दूल स्वप्नान्ते नात्र संशयः . . 9
text_mt: and surrounded by foot-soldiers, going near death, O king; / he sees [this], O tiger among Kurus, there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
cittaṃ ca vikṛtākāraṃ karavīravibhūṣitam .
tenopasṛṣṭo labhate na rājyaṃ paurvasaṃbhavam . . 1.23.10
meaning:
चित्तं च विकृताकारं करवीरविभूषितम् .
तेनोपसृष्टो लभते न राज्यं पौर्वसंभवम् . . 1.23.10
text_mt: His mind becomes distorted in form, adorned with oleander. / Possessed by him, one does not attain an ancestral kingdom;

sanskrit_iast:
kumārī na ca bhartāramapatyaṃ garbhiṇī tathā .
ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaśca śiṣyāścādhyayanaṃ tathā . .
vaṇiglābhaṃ ca nāpnoti kṛṣiṃ caiva kṛṣīvalaḥ . . 11
meaning:
कुमारी न च भर्तारमपत्यं गर्भिणी तथा .
आचार्यत्वं श्रोत्रियश्च शिष्याश्चाध्ययनं तथा . .
वणिग्लाभं च नाप्नोति कृषिं चैव कृषीवलः . . 11
text_mt: an unmarried girl does not obtain a husband, nor a pregnant woman an offspring; / a Vedic scholar does not obtain the status of a teacher, nor students their study; / a merchant obtains no profit, and a farmer no harvest.

sanskrit_iast:
snapanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ puṇye'hani ' mahīpate .
gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditena tu . . 12
meaning:
स्नपनं तस्य कर्तव्यं पुण्येऽहनि ' महीपते .
गौरसर्षपकल्केन साज्येनोत्सादितेन तु . . 12
text_mt: A bath should be performed for him on an auspicious day, O ruler of the earth, / with a paste of white mustard rubbed [on the body] together with ghee,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vāsare dhiṣaṇasya ca .
tiṣye ca vīranakṣatre tasyaiva purato nṛpa . . 13
meaning:
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्थ्यां तु वासरे धिषणस्य च .
तिष्ये च वीरनक्षत्रे तस्यैव पुरतो नृप . . 13
text_mt: on the caturthī of the bright fortnight, and on the day of Dhiṣaṇa, / under the Tiṣya constellation, a heroic lunar mansion, right before him, O king;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhairviliptaśirasastathā .
bhadrāsanopaviṣṭasya svasti vācya dvijāñchubhān . . 14
meaning:
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैर्विलिप्तशिरसस्तथा .
भद्रासनोपविष्टस्य स्वस्ति वाच्य द्विजाञ्छुभान् . . 14
text_mt: his head anointed with all herbs and all scents, / seated upon an auspicious seat, having auspicious twice-born recite blessings,

sanskrit_iast:
vyomakeśaṃ tu sampūjya pārvatīṃ bhīmajaṃ tathā .
kṛṣṇaṃ sapitaraṃ tāta pavamānaṃ sitaṃ tathā . . 15
meaning:
व्योमकेशं तु सम्पूज्य पार्वतीं भीमजं तथा .
कृष्णं सपितरं तात पवमानं सितं तथा . . 15
text_mt: and having worshipped Vyomakeśa, Pārvatī, and the son of Bhīmā, / Kṛṣṇa along with his father, dear one, Pavamāna and Sita,

sanskrit_iast:
dhiṣaṇaṃ cenduputraṃ ca koṇaṃ ketuṃ ca 3 bhārata .
vidhuntudaṃ bāhuleyaṃ nandakasya ca dhāriṇam . . 16
meaning:
धिषणं चेन्दुपुत्रं च कोणं केतुं च 3 भारत .
विधुन्तुदं बाहुलेयं नन्दकस्य च धारिणम् . . 16
text_mt: Dhiṣaṇa, the son of the Moon, Koṇa, and Ketu, O Bhārata, / Vidhuntuda, Bāhuleya, and the bearer of the Nandaka sword.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkātsaṅgamādhradāt .
mṛttikāṃ rocanāṃ gandhānguggulaṃ cāpsu nikṣipet . . 17
meaning:
अश्वस्थानाद्गजस्थानाद्वल्मीकात्सङ्गमाध्रदात् .
मृत्तिकां रोचनां गन्धान्गुग्गुलं चाप्सु निक्षिपेत् . . 17
text_mt: From a stable of horses, a place of elephants, an anthill, and the confluence of a lake, / one should throw earth, rocanā, perfumes, and bdellium into water,

sanskrit_iast:
yadāhṛtaṃ hyekavarṇaiścaturbhiḥ kalaśairhradāt .
carmaṇyānaḍuhe rakte sthāpyaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ tathā . . 18
meaning:
यदाहृतं ह्येकवर्णैश्चतुर्भिः कलशैर्ह्रदात् .
चर्मण्यानडुहे रक्ते स्थाप्यं भद्रासनं तथा . . 18
text_mt: which was brought in four single-coloured pots from a lake. / An auspicious seat is to be placed upon a red bull-hide.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ 1 pāvanaṃ kṛtam .
tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ punantu te . . 19
meaning:
सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः 1 पावनं कृतम् .
तेन त्वामभिषिञ्चामि पावमान्यः पुनन्तु ते . . 19
text_mt: "The thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed [bath] made purifying by the sages, / with that I consecrate you; may the purifying verses cleanse you!

sanskrit_iast:
bhagaṃ te varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ .
bhagamindraśca vāyuśca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ . . 1.23.20
meaning:
भगं ते वरुणो राजा भगं सूर्यो बृहस्पतिः .
भगमिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च भगं सप्तर्षयो ददुः . . 1.23.20
text_mt: May King Varuṇa grant you good fortune, may the Sun and Bṛhaspati grant you good fortune; / may Indra and Vāyu grant you good fortune, and may the seven sages grant you good fortune!

sanskrit_iast:
yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani .
lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastad ghnantu te sadā . . 21
meaning:
यत्ते केशेषु दौर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते यच्च मूर्धनि .
ललाटे कर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्तद् घ्नन्तु ते सदा . . 21
text_mt: Whatever misfortune is in your hair, in your parting, or on your head, / on your forehead, in your ears, or in your eyes, may the waters destroy that forever!"

sanskrit_iast:
snātasya sārṣapaṃ tailaṃ suveṇaudumbareṇa tu .
juhuyānmūrdhani kuśānsavyena parigṛhya tu . . 22
meaning:
स्नातस्य सार्षपं तैलं सुवेणौदुम्बरेण तु .
जुहुयान्मूर्धनि कुशान्सव्येन परिगृह्य तु . . 22
text_mt: Of the one who has bathed, one should offer mustard oil upon the head with an udumbara ladle, / holding kuśa grass in the left hand.

sanskrit_iast:
mitaśca sammitaścaiva tathā ca śālakaṃṭakaḥ .
kūṣmāṇḍo rājaśreṣṭhāste'gnayaḥ svāhāsamanvitāḥ . . 23
meaning:
मितश्च सम्मितश्चैव तथा च शालकंटकः .
कूष्माण्डो राजश्रेष्ठास्तेऽग्नयः स्वाहासमन्विताः . . 23
text_mt: "Mita, Sammita, Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa, / and Kūṣmāṇḍa, O best of kings, these fires accompanied by svāhā!"

sanskrit_iast:
nāmabhirbalimantraiśca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ .
dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ . . 24
meaning:
नामभिर्बलिमन्त्रैश्च नमस्कारसमन्वितैः .
दद्याच्चतुष्पथे शूर्पे कुशानास्तीर्य सर्वतः . . 24
text_mt: With their names and offering-mantras accompanied by reverential salutations, / one should place [the offering] at a crossroads in a winnowing basket, having strewn kuśa grass all around:

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃśca palalaudanameva ca .
matsyānpakvāṃstathaivāmānmāṃsametāvadeva tu . . 25
meaning:
कृताकृतांस्तण्डुलांश्च पललौदनमेव च .
मत्स्यान्पक्वांस्तथैवामान्मांसमेतावदेव तु . . 25
text_mt: Husked and unhusked rice grains, rice cooked with sesamum, / cooked and raw fish, and flesh to this extent,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpaṃ citraṃ sagandhaṃ ca surāṃ ca trividhāmapi .
mūlakaṃ pūrikāḥ pūpāṃstathaivoṇḍerikāsrajam . .
dadhipāyasamannaṃ ca guḍaveṣṭānsamodakān . . 26
meaning:
पुष्पं चित्रं सगन्धं च सुरां च त्रिविधामपि .
मूलकं पूरिकाः पूपांस्तथैवोण्डेरिकास्रजम् . .
दधिपायसमन्नं च गुडवेष्टान्समोदकान् . . 26
text_mt: variegated and fragrant flowers, three kinds of liquor, / radish, purīs, cakes, garlands of sweetmeats, / curd, rice-pudding, and food wrapped in jaggery along with modakas.

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato'mbikām .
dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ dattvā puṣpāñjalitrayam . . 27
meaning:
विनायकस्य जननीमुपतिष्ठेत्ततोऽम्बिकाम् .
दूर्वासर्षपपुष्पाणां दत्त्वा पुष्पाञ्जलित्रयम् . . 27
text_mt: Then one should wait upon Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka, / offering three handfuls of flowers consisting of dūrvā grass and mustard blossoms:

sanskrit_iast:
rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi bhagaṃ bhagavati dehi me .
putrāndehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvānkāmāṃśca dehi me . .
acalāṃ buddhiṃ me dehi dharāyāṃ khyātimeva ca . . 28
meaning:
रूपं देहि यशो देहि भगं भगवति देहि मे .
पुत्रान्देहि धनं देहि सर्वान्कामांश्च देहि मे . .
अचलां बुद्धिं मे देहि धरायां ख्यातिमेव च . . 28
text_mt: "Grant beauty, grant fame, grant good fortune to me, O goddess! / Grant sons, grant wealth, and grant all desires to me! / Grant me unshakeable intellect, and renown upon earth!"

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ .
bhojayed brāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi . . 29
meaning:
ततः शुक्लाम्बरधरः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः .
भोजयेद् ब्राह्मणान्दद्याद्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोरपि . . 29
text_mt: Then, dressed in white garments, wearing white garlands and unguent, / he should feed brāhmaṇas and give a pair of garments to the teacher.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ vināyakaṃ pūjya grahāṃścaiva vidhānataḥ .
karmaṇāṃ phalamāpnoti śriyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamām . . 1.23.30
meaning:
एवं विनायकं पूज्य ग्रहांश्चैव विधानतः .
कर्मणां फलमाप्नोति श्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् . . 1.23.30
text_mt: Having thus worshipped Vināyaka and the planets according to the rule, / one attains the fruit of rites and attains unsurpassed fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
ādityasya sadā pūjāṃ tilakaṃ svāminastathā .
vināyakapateścaiva sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt . . 31
iti śrī bhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpavarṇanaṃ
nāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 23 .
caturthīkalpe puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
meaning:
आदित्यस्य सदा पूजां तिलकं स्वामिनस्तथा .
विनायकपतेश्चैव सर्वसिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् . . 31
इति श्री भविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पवर्णनं
नाम त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः . 23 .
चतुर्थीकल्पे पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनम्
text_mt:
By constant worship of the Sun, the tilaka mark of the Lord, / and the master of Vināyakas, one attains all success.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "Description of the Caturthī Rite", in the Brāhma Book of the holy and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Characteristics of Men in the Caturthī Rite

sanskrit_iast:
śatānīka uvāca
narāṇāṃ yoṣitāṃ caiva lakṣaṇāni mahāmate .
proktāni yāni viprendra vyomakeśasya sūnunā . . 1
meaning:
शतानीक उवाच
नराणां योषितां चैव लक्षणानि महामते .
प्रोक्तानि यानि विप्रेन्द्र व्योमकेशस्य सूनुना . . 1
text_mt: Śatānīka said: / The bodily characteristics of men and women, O great-minded one, / which were spoken, O best of vipras, by the son of Vyomakeśa,
title: Puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
kruddhena yāni kṣiptāni īśvareṇa mahodadhau .
kṛṣṇasya vacanād bhūyaḥ samudreṇārpitāni vai . . 2
meaning:
क्रुद्धेन यानि क्षिप्तानि ईश्वरेण महोदधौ .
कृष्णस्य वचनाद् भूयः समुद्रेणार्पितानि वै . . 2
text_mt: which were cast into the great ocean by the enraged Lord, / and again offered back by the ocean at the command of Kṛṣṇa—

sanskrit_iast:
arpitāni tatastasya tena prāptāni vai kathan .
bāhuleyena viprendra tāni me vada suvrata . . 3
meaning:
अर्पितानि ततस्तस्य तेन प्राप्तानि वै कथन् .
बाहुलेयेन विप्रेन्द्र तानि मे वद सुव्रत . . 3
text_mt: offered by him then, how were they obtained by him, / by Bāhuleya, O best of vipras? Tell me that, O you of good vows!

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
yathā guhena rājendra strīpuṃsāṃ lakṣaṇāni vai .
proktāni kuruśārdūla tathā te kathayāmi vai . . 4
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
यथा गुहेन राजेन्द्र स्त्रीपुंसां लक्षणानि वै .
प्रोक्तानि कुरुशार्दूल तथा ते कथयामि वै . . 4
text_mt: Sumantu said: / As the bodily characteristics of women and men were spoken / by Guha, O king of kings, O tiger among Kurus, so I shall tell you.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktipātāddhate krauñce vyomakeśasya sūnunā .
brahmā tuṣṭo'bravīdenaṃ varaṃ varaya me'nagha . . 5
meaning:
शक्तिपाताद्धते क्रौञ्चे व्योमकेशस्य सूनुना .
ब्रह्मा तुष्टोऽब्रवीदेनं वरं वरय मेऽनघ . . 5
text_mt: When Mount Krauñca was struck down by the strike of the spear by the son of Vyomakeśa, / Brahmā, being pleased, said to him: "Choose a boon from me, sinless one!"

sanskrit_iast:
asāvapi mahātejāḥ praṇamya śirasā vibhum .
pitāmahaṃ babhāṣedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi me vibho . . 6
meaning:
असावपि महातेजाः प्रणम्य शिरसा विभुम् .
पितामहं बभाषेदं लक्षणं ब्रूहि मे विभो . . 6
text_mt: He, endowed with great splendour, bowing with his head to the lord, / spoke this to the Grandfather: "Tell me the characteristics, O lord,

sanskrit_iast:
narāṇāṃ yuvatīnāṃ ca kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama .
yanmayoktaṃ purā deva prakṣiptaṃ lavaṇārṇave . . 7
meaning:
नराणां युवतीनां च कौतुकं परमं मम .
यन्मयोक्तं पुरा देव प्रक्षिप्तं लवणार्णवे . . 7
text_mt: of men and young women; it is my supreme curiosity. / That which was spoken by me of old, O god, was cast into the salt sea."

sanskrit_iast:
matpitrā devadeveśa sakrodhena purā tathā .
prāptaṃ ca vismṛtaṃ bhūyastanme brūhi hyaśeṣataḥ . . 8
meaning:
मत्पित्रा देवदेवेश सक्रोधेन पुरा तथा .
प्राप्तं च विस्मृतं भूयस्तन्मे ब्रूहि ह्यशेषतः . . 8
text_mt: and likewise by my father, O lord of the gods of gods, in anger long ago, / and was obtained and then forgotten again—explain that to me in full.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi deveśa bhīmasyānandavardhana .
lakṣaṇāni nibodha tvaṃ puruṣāṇāmaśeṣataḥ . .
adhamottamamadhyāni yāni prāpa payonidhiḥ . . 9
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि देवेश भीमस्यानन्दवर्धन .
लक्षणानि निबोध त्वं पुरुषाणामशेषतः . .
अधमोत्तममध्यानि यानि प्राप पयोनिधिः . . 9
text_mt: Brahmā said: / I have been well questioned, O lord of gods, O increaser of the joy of Bhīma. / Learn from me the marks of men in their entirety, / the lowest, highest, and middling, which the ocean obtained.

sanskrit_iast:
śive'hani sunakṣatre grahe saumye śubhe ravau .
pūrvāhṇe maṅgalairyukte parīkṣeta vicakṣaṇaḥ . . 1.24.10
meaning:
शिवेऽहनि सुनक्षत्रे ग्रहे सौम्ये शुभे रवौ .
पूर्वाह्णे मङ्गलैर्युक्ते परीक्षेत विचक्षणः . . 1.24.10
text_mt: On an auspicious day, under an auspicious constellation, when a benefic planet rules and the sun is favorable, / in the forenoon, endowed with auspicious circumstances, an expert should examine:

sanskrit_iast:
pramāṇaṃ saṃhatiṃ chāyāṃ gatiṃ sarvāṅgalakṣaṇam .
dantakeśanakhaśmaśru etatsarvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ . . 11
meaning:
प्रमाणं संहतिं छायां गतिं सर्वाङ्गलक्षणम् .
दन्तकेशनखश्मश्रु एतत्सर्वं विचक्षणः . . 11
text_mt: measure, compactness, radiance, gait, the marks of all limbs, / teeth, hair, nails, and beard—all this the expert [should examine].

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvamāyuḥ parīkṣeta paścāllakṣaṇamādiśet .
kṣīṇe hyāyuṣi martyānāṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam . . 12
meaning:
पूर्वमायुः परीक्षेत पश्चाल्लक्षणमादिशेत् .
क्षीणे ह्यायुषि मर्त्यानां लक्षणैः किं प्रयोजनम् . . 12
text_mt: First he should examine the lifespan; afterwards he should declare the marks. / For when the lifespan of mortals is exhausted, what is the use of bodily marks?

sanskrit_iast:
jaghanyo navatiḥ prokto madhyamastu śatāḍgulaḥ .
aṣṭottaraśataṃ yasya uttamaṃ tasya lakṣaṇam . . 13
meaning:
जघन्यो नवतिः प्रोक्तो मध्यमस्तु शताड्गुलः .
अष्टोत्तरशतं यस्य उत्तमं तस्य लक्षणम् . . 13
text_mt: Ninety [aṅgulas] is said to be the lowest, and a hundred aṅgulas is middling; / one who has a hundred and eight has the highest mark.

sanskrit_iast:
pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ samudreṇa śubhāśubham .
yanme purā devavara mayā vai kathitaṃ tava . .
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dehāvayavalakṣaṇam . . 14
meaning:
प्रमाणलक्षणं प्रोक्तं समुद्रेण शुभाशुभम् .
यन्मे पुरा देववर मया वै कथितं तव . .
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि देहावयवलक्षणम् . . 14
text_mt: The auspicious and inauspicious mark of measurement was declared by the ocean, / which was told to me long ago, O best of gods, and indeed by me to you. / Hereafter I shall declare the marks of the parts of the body.

sanskrit_iast:
pādaiḥ samāṃsakaiḥ 2 snigdhai raktaṃ saumyaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ .
unnataiḥ svedarahitaiḥ śirāhīnaiśca pārthivaḥ . . 15
meaning:
पादैः समांसकैः 2 स्निग्धै रक्तं सौम्यैः सुशोभनैः .
उन्नतैः स्वेदरहितैः शिराहीनैश्च पार्थिवः . . 15
text_mt: With fleshy, smooth, red, pleasing, very handsome, / elevated, sweatless, and veinless feet, [one is] an earthly king.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya pādatale rekhā sāṃkuśeva prakāśate .
satataṃ hi sukhaṃ tasya puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 16
meaning:
यस्य पादतले रेखा सांकुशेव प्रकाशते .
सततं हि सुखं तस्य पुरुषस्य न संशयः . . 16
text_mt: A man on the sole of whose foot a line appears like an elephant goad / certainly has constant happiness; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
asvedanau mṛdutalau kamalodarasannibhau .
śliṣṭāṅgulī 1 tāmranakhau supārṣṇī vyomakeśaja . . 17
meaning:
अस्वेदनौ मृदुतलौ कमलोदरसन्निभौ .
श्लिष्टाङ्गुली 1 ताम्रनखौ सुपार्ष्णी व्योमकेशज . . 17
text_mt: Sweatless, soft-soled, resembling the interior of a lotus, / with close-set toes, copper-colored nails, and good heels, O son of Vyomakeśa,

uṣṇau śirāvirahitau gūḍhagulphau ca bhīmaja .
kūrmonnatau ca caraṇau prakhyātau pārthivasya tu . 18

कूर्मोन्नतौ च चरणौ प्रख्यातौ पार्थिवस्य तु . 18

vakrau śirāsantatau ca saṃśuṣkau viralāṅgulī . . 19

वक्रौ शिरासन्ततौ च संशुष्कौ विरलाङ्गुली . . 19
text_mt: Shaped like winnowing baskets, O mighty-armed one, rough, with white nails, / crooked, covered with veins, withered, and with widely separated toes,

brahmaghnau devaśārdūla 3 pakvamṛtsadṛśau padau . . 1.24.20

अभक्ष्यभक्षणे श्वेतौ ज्ञेयौ सेनाधिपोत्तम . . 21

अङ्गुष्ठौ पृथुलौ येषां ते नरा भाग्यवर्जिताः .
क्लिश्यन्ते विकृताङ्गुष्ठास्ते नराः पादगामिनः . . 22

sanskrit_iast:
cipiṭairvikṛtairbhagnairaṅguṣṭhairatininditāḥ .

meaning:
चिपिटैर्विकृतैर्भग्नैरङ्गुष्ठैरतिनिन्दिताः .
वक्रैर्भग्नैस्तथा ह्रस्वैरङ्गुष्ठैः क्लेशभागिनः . . 23
text_mt: Men with flat, deformed, and broken big toes are utterly contemptible; / with crooked, broken, and short big toes they share in misery.

sanskrit_iast:
śūrpākāraiśca vikṛtairbhagnarvakraiḥ śirātataiḥ .
sasvedaiḥ pāṇḍurūkṣaiśca caraṇairatininditāḥ . . 24
meaning:
शूर्पाकारैश्च विकृतैर्भग्नर्वक्रैः शिराततैः .
सस्वेदैः पाण्डुरूक्षैश्च चरणैरतिनिन्दिताः . . 24

sanskrit_iast:
yasya pradeśinī dīrghā aṅguṣṭhaṃ yā atikramet .

kaniṣṭhāyāṃ tu dīrghāyāṃ suvarṇasya tu bhāginaḥ . . 25

स्त्रीभोगं लभते नित्यं पुरुषो नात्र संशयः . .
कनिष्ठायां तु दीर्घायां सुवर्णस्य तु भागिनः . . 25

चिपिटा विरलाः शुष्का यस्याङ्गुल्यो भवन्ति वै .

sanskrit_iast:

vikṛtaiḥ sphuṭitairūkṣairnakhairdāridryabhāginaḥ . . 27

श्वेतैर्नखैर्विरूक्षैश्च पुरुषा दुःखजीविनः .

विकृतैः स्फुटितैरूक्षैर्नखैर्दारिद्र्यभागिनः . . 27

ब्रह्महत्यां च कुर्वन्ति पुरुषा हरितैर्नखैः .
बन्धुभिश्च वियुज्यन्ते कुलक्षयकराश्च ते . . 28

इन्द्रगोपकसंकाशैर्नखैर्नृपतयः स्मृताः .
शङ्खावर्तप्रतीकाशैर्नखैर्भवति पार्थिवः . . 29

रक्तैर्नखैस्तथैश्वर्यं पुष्पितैः सुभगो भवेत् . .
सूक्ष्मैरुपचितैस्ताम्रैर्नखैर्नृपतयः स्मृताः . . 1.24.30

sanskrit_iast:

केशाश्चैव महाबाहो निन्दिता पूजितास्तथा . . 36

स भवेत्पार्थिवः पूज्यः समुद्रवचनं यथा . . 39

वृषसिंहगजेन्द्राणां 6गतिर्भोगविवर्धिनी . . 1.24.40

jalormisadṛśī yā ca kākolūkasamā ca yā .
gatirdravyavihīnānāṃ duḥkhaśokabhayaṅkarā . . 41

जलोर्मिसदृशी या च काकोलूकसमा च या .
गतिर्द्रव्यविहीनानां दुःखशोकभयङ्करा . . 41
text_mt: A gait resembling a water wave, or like a crow or an owl, / belongs to those devoid of wealth, causing sorrow, grief, and fear.

sanskrit_iast:
śvānoṣṭmahiṣāṇāṃ 1kharasūkarayostathā .
gatirmeṣasamā yeṣāṃ te narā bhāgyavarjitāḥ . . 42
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanaṃ nāma caturviṃśodhyāyaḥ . 24 .
puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
meaning:
श्वानोष्ट्महिषाणां 1खरसूकरयोस्तथा .
गतिर्मेषसमा येषां ते नरा भाग्यवर्जिताः . . 42
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनं नाम चतुर्विंशोध्यायः . 24 .
पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनम्
text_mt:
Those whose gait is like that of dogs, camels, buffaloes, / donkeys, pigs, or rams are men devoid of good fortune.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Marks of Men', in the fourth kalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand [verses].
[Chapter 25:] Description of the Marks of Men

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
dakṣiṇāvartaliṅgaśca naro vai putramānbhavet .
vāmāvarte tathā liṅge naraḥ kanyāṃ prasūyate . . 1
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दक्षिणावर्तलिङ्गश्च नरो वै पुत्रमान्भवेत् .
वामावर्ते तथा लिङ्गे नरः कन्यां प्रसूयते . . 1
text_mt: Brahmā said: / A man whose penis curls to the right has sons; / when the penis curls to the left, the man father daughters.

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlaiḥ śirālairviṣamairliṅgairdāridryamādiśet .
ṛjubhirvartulākāraiḥ puruṣā putrabhāginaḥ . . 2
meaning:
स्थूलैः शिरालैर्विषमैर्लिङ्गैर्दारिद्र्यमादिशेत् .
ऋजुभिर्वर्तुलाकारैः पुरुषा पुत्रभागिनः . . 2
text_mt: One should indicate poverty from thick, veined, and uneven penises; / with straight and rounded [penises], men partake of sons.

sanskrit_iast:
nimnapādopaviṣṭasya bhūmiṃ spṛśati mehanaḥ .
duḥkhitaṃ taṃ vijānīyātpuruṣaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 3
meaning:
निम्नपादोपविष्टस्य भूमिं स्पृशति मेहनः .
दुःखितं तं विजानीयात्पुरुषं नात्र संशयः . . 3
text_mt: When a man sits with his feet lowered and his penis touches the ground, / one should know him to be miserable; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmau pādopaviṣṭasya gulphau spṛśati mehanaḥ .
īśvaraṃ taṃ vijānīyātpramadānāṃ ca vallabham2 . . 4
meaning:
भूमौ पादोपविष्टस्य गुल्फौ स्पृशति मेहनः .
ईश्वरं तं विजानीयात्प्रमदानां च वल्लभम्2 . . 4
text_mt: When a man sits with his feet on the ground and his penis touches his ankles, / one should know him to be a lord and beloved of women.

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhavyāghrasamo yasya hrasvau bhavati mehanaḥ .
bhogavānsa tu vijñeyo'śeṣabhogasamanvitaḥ . . 5
meaning:
सिंहव्याघ्रसमो यस्य ह्रस्वौ भवति मेहनः .
भोगवान्स तु विज्ञेयोऽशेषभोगसमन्वितः . . 5
text_mt: He whose short penis resembles that of a lion or tiger / is to be known as enjoying pleasures, endowed with all enjoyments.

sanskrit_iast:
rekhākṛtirmaṇiryasya mehane hi virājate .
pārthivaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā . . 6
meaning:
रेखाकृतिर्मणिर्यस्य मेहने हि विराजते .
पार्थिवः स तु विज्ञेयः समुद्रवचनं यथा . . 6
text_mt: He on whose penis the glans shines in the form of a line / is to be known as an earthly king, according to the words of the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
suvarṇarajataprakhyairmaṇimuktāsamaprabhaiḥ .
pravālasadṛśaiḥ snigdhairmaṇibhiḥ pārthivo bhavet . . 7
meaning:
सुवर्णरजतप्रख्यैर्मणिमुक्तासमप्रभैः .
प्रवालसदृशैः स्निग्धैर्मणिभिः पार्थिवो भवेत् . . 7
text_mt: With glans resembling gold and silver, shining like gems and pearls, / resembling coral and glossy, a man becomes a king.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇḍurairmalinai rūkṣairdīrghavyāsairdiśo vrajet .
samaistathonnataiścāpi susnigdhairmaṇibhirgṛhī . . 8
meaning:
पाण्डुरैर्मलिनै रूक्षैर्दीर्घव्यासैर्दिशो व्रजेत् .
समैस्तथोन्नतैश्चापि सुस्निग्धैर्मणिभिर्गृही . . 8
text_mt: With [a glans] pale, dirty, rough, or long and broad, he will wander to the quarters. / With an even, elevated, and very glossy glans, he is a householder.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanarakṣāstathā strīṇāṃ bhoktāraste bhavanti hi .
maṇibhirmadhyanimnaistu pitaraste bhavanti hi . . 9
meaning:
धनरक्षास्तथा स्त्रीणां भोक्तारस्ते भवन्ति हि .
मणिभिर्मध्यनिम्नैस्तु पितरस्ते भवन्ति हि . . 9
text_mt: They indeed become protectors of wealth and enjoyers of women. / With a glans depressed in the middle, they indeed become fathers

sanskrit_iast:
yuvatīnāṃ mahābāho niḥsvāścāpi bhavanti te .

meaning:
युवतीनां महाबाहो निःस्वाश्चापि भवन्ति ते .
नोल्बणैश्चापि धनिनो नरा वीरा भवन्ति हि . . 1.25.10
text_mt: of young women, O mighty-armed one, and they also become destitute. / Men with [a glans] that is not excessive become wealthy and heroic.

sanskrit_iast:
mūtradhārā patedekā valitā dakṣiṇā yadi .
sa bhavetpārthivaḥ pṛthvyāḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā . . 11
meaning:
मूत्रधारा पतेदेका वलिता दक्षिणा यदि .
स भवेत्पार्थिवः पृथ्व्याः समुद्रवचनं यथा . . 11
text_mt: If a single stream of urine falls, curved to the right, / he will become a ruler of the earth, according to the words of Samudra.

sanskrit_iast:
dve dhāre ca tathā snigdhe dhanavānbhogavānsmṛtaḥ .
bahudhārāstathā rūkṣāḥ saśabdāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ . . 12
meaning:
द्वे धारे च तथा स्निग्धे धनवान्भोगवान्स्मृतः .
बहुधारास्तथा रूक्षाः सशब्दाः पुरुषाधमाः . . 12
text_mt: And if two streams are glossy, he is said to be wealthy and an enjoyer of pleasures. / Those with many streams, rough, and noisy are the lowest of men.

sanskrit_iast:
mīnagandhi bhavedreto dhanavānputravānbhavet .
havigandhi bhavedyasya dhanāḍhyaḥ śrotriyaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 13
meaning:
मीनगन्धि भवेद्रेतो धनवान्पुत्रवान्भवेत् .
हविगन्धि भवेद्यस्य धनाढ्यः श्रोत्रियः स्मृतः . . 13
text_mt: If the semen smells of fish, he will be wealthy and possess sons. / He whose [semen] smells of clarified butter is said to be rich in wealth and learned in the Veda.

sanskrit_iast:
1mūṣagandhirbhavetputrī padmagandhirnṛpaḥ smṛtaḥ .
lākṣāgandhirbhavedyaśca bahukanyaḥ prajāyate . .
madyagandhirbhavedyoddhā kṣāragandhirdaridrakaḥ . . 14
meaning:
1मूषगन्धिर्भवेत्पुत्री पद्मगन्धिर्नृपः स्मृतः .
लाक्षागन्धिर्भवेद्यश्च बहुकन्यः प्रजायते . .
मद्यगन्धिर्भवेद्योद्धा क्षारगन्धिर्दरिद्रकः . . 14
text_mt: One whose [semen] smells of a mouse has sons; one whose smells of lotus is known as a king. / And one whose [semen] smells of lac begets many daughters; / one whose smells of liquor becomes a warrior; one whose smells of alkali is impoverished.

sanskrit_iast:
śīghramaithunagāmī yaḥ sa dīrghāyurato'nyathā .
alpāyurdevaśārdūla vijñeyo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 15
meaning:
शीघ्रमैथुनगामी यः स दीर्घायुरतोऽन्यथा .
अल्पायुर्देवशार्दूल विज्ञेयो नात्र संशयः . . 15
text_mt: He who finishes coitus quickly is long-lived; otherwise, / he is to be known as short-lived, O tiger among gods; there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
tanuśukraḥ strījanako māṃsagandhī ca bhogavān .
padmavarṇaṃ bhavedraktaṃ sa naro dhanavānbhavet . . 16
meaning:
तनुशुक्रः स्त्रीजनको मांसगन्धी च भोगवान् .
पद्मवर्णं भवेद्रक्तं स नरो धनवान्भवेत् . . 16
text_mt: A man of thin semen begets females, and one whose [semen] smells of flesh is an enjoyer of pleasures. / If his blood is of the colour of a lotus, that man will be wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
kiñcidraktaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ bhavedyasya tu śoṇitam .
adhamaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ sadā duḥkhaikabhājanam . . 17
meaning:
किञ्चिद्रक्तं तथा कृष्णं भवेद्यस्य तु शोणितम् .
अधमः स तु विज्ञेयः सदा दुःखैकभाजनम् . . 17
text_mt: He whose blood is slightly red and black, / is to be known as vile, forever a receptacle solely of sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
pravālasadṛśaṃ snigdhaṃ bhavedyasya ca śoṇitam .
rājānaṃ taṃ vijānīyātsaptadvīpādhipaṃ guha . . 18
meaning:
प्रवालसदृशं स्निग्धं भवेद्यस्य च शोणितम् .
राजानं तं विजानीयात्सप्तद्वीपाधिपं गुह . . 18
text_mt: And he whose blood is glossy and resembles coral, / know him to be a king, the lord of the seven continents, O Guha.

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇā māṃsalā snigdhā vastiḥ puṃsāṃ praśasyate .
nirmāṃsā vikaṭā rūkṣā bastiryeṣāṃ na te śubhāḥ . . 19
meaning:
विस्तीर्णा मांसला स्निग्धा वस्तिः पुंसां प्रशस्यते .
निर्मांसा विकटा रूक्षा बस्तिर्येषां न ते शुभाः . . 19
text_mt: A bladder of men that is broad, fleshy, and glossy is praised; / those whose bladder is fleshless, deformed, and rough are not auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
gomāyusadṛśī yasya śvānoṣṭramahiṣasya ca .
sa bhavedduḥkhito nityaṃ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 1.25.20
meaning:
गोमायुसदृशी यस्य श्वानोष्ट्रमहिषस्य च .
स भवेद्दुःखितो नित्यं पुरुषो नात्र संशयः . . 1.25.20
text_mt: He whose [bladder] resembles that of a jackal, a dog, a camel, or a buffalo, / that man will always be miserable; there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
yaścaikavṛṣaṇastāta jale prāṇānvimuñjati .
strīcañcalastu viṣamaiḥ samai rājyaṃ pracakṣate . . 21
meaning:
यश्चैकवृषणस्तात जले प्राणान्विमुञ्जति .
स्त्रीचञ्चलस्तु विषमैः समै राज्यं प्रचक्षते . . 21
text_mt: And one who has only one testicle, dear one, loses his life in water. / With uneven [testicles] he is fickle toward women; with even ones, they declare [he attains] kingship.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvagaiścāpi hrasvāyuḥ śatañjīvī pralambadhṛk .
mānavāścāpi raktaistu dhanavanto bhavanti vai . . 22
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वगैश्चापि ह्रस्वायुः शतञ्जीवी प्रलम्बधृक् .
मानवाश्चापि रक्तैस्तु धनवन्तो भवन्ति वै . . 22
text_mt: With upward-directed ones, he is short-lived; possessing hanging ones, he lives a hundred years. / And men with red [testicles] indeed become wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlasphigbhavati kṣemī dravyayuktaḥ samāṃsadhṛk .
vyāghrasphiṅmaṇḍalo rājā maṇḍūkasphiṅnarādhipaḥ . .
dvimaṇḍalo mahābāho siṃhasphiksārvabhaumatā . . 23
meaning:
स्थूलस्फिग्भवति क्षेमी द्रव्ययुक्तः समांसधृक् .
व्याघ्रस्फिङ्मण्डलो राजा मण्डूकस्फिङ्नराधिपः . .
द्विमण्डलो महाबाहो सिंहस्फिक्सार्वभौमता . . 23
text_mt: One with thick buttocks is secure; possessing even flesh, he is endowed with wealth. / One with buttocks rounded like a tiger's is a king; one with buttocks like a frog's is a lord of men; / with doubly rounded [buttocks], O mighty-armed one, [or] with buttocks like a lion's, there is universal sovereignty.

sanskrit_iast:
uṣṭravānarayoryastu dhārayetsphiṅmahāmate .
dhanadhānyavihīno'sau vijñeyo bhīmanandana . . 24
meaning:
उष्ट्रवानरयोर्यस्तु धारयेत्स्फिङ्महामते .
धनधान्यविहीनोऽसौ विज्ञेयो भीमनन्दन . . 24
text_mt: He who possesses buttocks like those of a camel or a monkey, O highly intelligent one, / is to be known as devoid of wealth and grain, O son of Bhīma.

sanskrit_iast:
pumānmṛgodaro dhanyo mayūrodara eva ca .
vyāghrodaro narapatī rājā siṃhodaro bhavet . . 25
meaning:
पुमान्मृगोदरो धन्यो मयूरोदर एव च .
व्याघ्रोदरो नरपती राजा सिंहोदरो भवेत् . . 25
text_mt: A man with a belly like a deer's is fortunate, as is one with a belly like a peacock's. / One with a belly like a tiger's is a lord of men; with a belly like a lion's, he becomes a king.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍūkasadṛśaṃ yasya puruṣasyodaraṃ bhavet .
sa bhavetpārthivaḥ puṣṭyā samudravacanaṃ yathā . . 26
meaning:
मण्डूकसदृशं यस्य पुरुषस्योदरं भवेत् .
स भवेत्पार्थिवः पुष्ट्या समुद्रवचनं यथा . . 26
text_mt: A man whose belly resembles that of a frog / becomes a ruler through nourishment, according to the words of Samudra.

sanskrit_iast:
māṃsalairṛjubhirvṛttaiḥ pārśvairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ .
īśvaro vyāghrapṛṣṭhastu senāyāścaiva nāyakaḥ . . 27
meaning:
मांसलैरृजुभिर्वृत्तैः पार्श्वैर्नृपतयः स्मृताः .
ईश्वरो व्याघ्रपृष्ठस्तु सेनायाश्चैव नायकः . . 27
text_mt: Men with fleshy, straight, and rounded flanks are known as kings. / One with a back like a tiger's is a lord and a commander of an army.

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhapṛṣṭho naro yastu bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet .
kūrmapṛṣṭhāstu rājāno dhanasaubhāgyabhāginaḥ . . 28
meaning:
सिंहपृष्ठो नरो यस्तु बन्धनं तस्य निर्दिशेत् .
कूर्मपृष्ठास्तु राजानो धनसौभाग्यभागिनः . . 28
text_mt: One should indicate captivity for a man with a back like a lion's. / But those with backs like a tortoise's are kings, enjoying wealth and good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇaṃ hadayaṃ yeṣāṃ māṃsalomacitaṃ samam .
śatāyuṣo vijānīyādbhogabhājo mahādhanān . . 29
meaning:
विस्तीर्णं हदयं येषां मांसलोमचितं समम् .
शतायुषो विजानीयाद्भोगभाजो महाधनान् . . 29
text_mt: Those whose chest is broad, fleshy, covered with hair, and even, / one should know to live a hundred years, enjoyers of pleasures and exceedingly wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
viralāḥ śuṣkāstathā rūkṣā dṛśyante'ṅgulayaḥ kare .
sa bhaved duḥkhito nityaṃ naro dāridryabhājanam . . 1.25.30
meaning:
विरलाः शुष्कास्तथा रूक्षा दृश्यन्तेऽङ्गुलयः करे .
स भवेद् दुःखितो नित्यं नरो दारिद्र्यभाजनम् . . 1.25.30
text_mt: If fingers are seen on the hand as spaced apart, withered, and rough, / that man will always be miserable, a vessel of poverty.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya mīnasamā rekhā karmasiddhibhra tasya tu .
dhanavānsa tu vijñeyo bahuputraśca mānavaḥ . . 31
meaning:
यस्य मीनसमा रेखा कर्मसिद्धिभ्र तस्य तु .
धनवान्स तु विज्ञेयो बहुपुत्रश्च मानवः . . 31
text_mt: He who has a line resembling a fish has success in his undertakings. / That man is to be known as wealthy and possessing many sons.

sanskrit_iast:
tulā yasya tu vedī vā karamadhye tu dṛśyate .
tasya sidhyati vāṇijyaṃ puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 32
meaning:
तुला यस्य तु वेदी वा करमध्ये तु दृश्यते .
तस्य सिध्यति वाणिज्यं पुरुषस्य न संशयः . . 32
text_mt: He in the middle of whose palm a balance or an altar is seen, / trade succeeds for that man; there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
saumye pāṇitale yasya dvijasya tu viśeṣataḥ .
yajñayājī bhavennityaṃ bahuvittaśca mānavaḥ . . 33
meaning:
सौम्ये पाणितले यस्य द्विजस्य तु विशेषतः .
यज्ञयाजी भवेन्नित्यं बहुवित्तश्च मानवः . . 33
text_mt: If [it is seen] especially on the left palm of a twice-born, / that man will always be a performer of sacrifices and rich in great wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
śailaṃ vāpyatha vā vṛkṣaḥ karamadhye tu dṛśyate .
acalāṃ śriyamāpnoti bahubhṛtyasamanvitaḥ . . 34
meaning:
शैलं वाप्यथ वा वृक्षः करमध्ये तु दृश्यते .
अचलां श्रियमाप्नोति बहुभृत्यसमन्वितः . . 34
text_mt: If a mountain or a tree is seen in the middle of the palm, / he attains unshakeable fortune, accompanied by many servants.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktitomarabāṇāsirekhā 1 cāpopamā tathā .
yasya haste mahābāho sa jayedvigrahe ripūn . . 35
meaning:
शक्तितोमरबाणासिरेखा 1 चापोपमा तथा .
यस्य हस्ते महाबाहो स जयेद्विग्रहे रिपून् . . 35
text_mt: He in whose hand, O mighty-armed one, there is a line resembling a spear, a javelin, an arrow, a sword, / or a bow, will conquer his enemies in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
dhvajabhrāpyatha vā śaṃkhaḥ karamadhye tu dṛśyate .
samudrayāyī sa bhaveddhanī ca satataṃ guha . . 36
meaning:
ध्वजभ्राप्यथ वा शंखः करमध्ये तु दृश्यते .
समुद्रयायी स भवेद्धनी च सततं गुह . . 36
text_mt: If a banner or a conch is seen in the middle of the palm, / he will travel by sea and be continually rich, O Guha.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīvatsamatha vā padmaṃ vajraṃ vā cakameva ca .
ratho vāpyatha vā kumbho yasya haste prakāśate . .
rājānaṃ taṃ vijānīyātparasainyavidāraṇam . . 37
meaning:
श्रीवत्समथ वा पद्मं वज्रं वा चकमेव च .
रथो वाप्यथ वा कुम्भो यस्य हस्ते प्रकाशते . .
राजानं तं विजानीयात्परसैन्यविदारणम् . . 37
text_mt: He in whose hand shines a śrīvatsa, or a lotus, a thunderbolt, or a discus, / or a chariot, or a water-jar, / know him to be a king who tears through enemy armies.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇe tu karāṅguṣṭhe yavo yasya tu dṛśyate .
sarvavidyāpravaktā ca bhavedvai nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 38
meaning:
दक्षिणे तु कराङ्गुष्ठे यवो यस्य तु दृश्यते .
सर्वविद्याप्रवक्ता च भवेद्वै नात्र संशयः . . 38
text_mt: He on whose right thumb a barley-grain mark is seen, / will indeed be an expounder of all sciences; there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya pāṇitale rekhā kaniṣṭhāmūlamutthitā2 .
gatā madhyaṃ pradeśinyāḥ sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam . . 39
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārdhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 25 .
puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
meaning:
यस्य पाणितले रेखा कनिष्ठामूलमुत्थिता2 .
गता मध्यं प्रदेशिन्याः स जीवेच्छरदः शतम् . . 39
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनं नाम पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः . 25 .
पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनम्
text_mt:
He on whose palm a line, rising from the base of the little finger, / goes to the middle of the forefinger, will live for a hundred autumns.
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Caturthīkalpa, the twenty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Marks of Men.'
Description of the Marks of Men

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
samakukṣirbhavedbhogī nimnakukṣirdhanāpahaḥ .
māyāvī viṣamā 1 kukṣistathā kuhakakṛtsadā . . 1
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
समकुक्षिर्भवेद्भोगी निम्नकुक्षिर्धनापहः .
मायावी विषमा 1 कुक्षिस्तथा कुहककृत्सदा . . 1
text_mt: Brahmā said: / One with an even belly will be an enjoyer of pleasures; one with a depressed belly takes away wealth. / One with an uneven belly is deceitful and always a practitioner of trickery.
title: Puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
rājā syānnimnakukṣistu sārvabhaumo mahābalaḥ .
sarpodarā daridrāḥ syurbahubhakṣāśca suvrata . . 2
meaning:
राजा स्यान्निम्नकुक्षिस्तु सार्वभौमो महाबलः .
सर्पोदरा दरिद्राः स्युर्बहुभक्षाश्च सुव्रत . . 2
text_mt: One with a depressed belly may be a king, a universal sovereign of great might. / Those with bellies like serpents are poor and gluttonous, O you of noble vows.

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇābhirmaṇḍalābhirunnatābhiśca nābhibhiḥ .
bhavanti sukhino vīrā dhanadhānyasamanvitāḥ . . 3
meaning:
विस्तीर्णाभिर्मण्डलाभिरुन्नताभिश्च नाभिभिः .
भवन्ति सुखिनो वीरा धनधान्यसमन्विताः . . 3
text_mt: With navels that are broad, circular, and elevated, / men become happy heroes, endowed with wealth and grain.

sanskrit_iast:
nimnābhiratha svalpābhiḥ kleśabhājo bhavanti hi .
valirmadhyaṅgatā vīrā viṣamā ca viśeṣataḥ . .
dhanahāniṃ tathā śūlaṃ nityaṃ janayate vibho . . 4
meaning:
निम्नाभिरथ स्वल्पाभिः क्लेशभाजो भवन्ति हि .
वलिर्मध्यङ्गता वीरा विषमा च विशेषतः . .
धनहानिं तथा शूलं नित्यं जनयते विभो . . 4
text_mt: With [navels] that are deep and very small, they indeed partake in suffering. / A fold [of the abdomen] that runs into the middle and is especially uneven, / always produces loss of wealth and abdominal pain, O lord.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmāvārtā sadā śāntiṃ karotīti vidurbudhāḥ .
karoti medhāṃ dakṣiṇena saṃpravṛttā divaspate . . 5
meaning:
वामावार्ता सदा शान्तिं करोतीति विदुर्बुधाः .
करोति मेधां दक्षिणेन संप्रवृत्ता दिवस्पते . . 5
text_mt: Wise men know that one curling to the left always produces peace. / Turning toward the right, it produces intelligence, O lord of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
pārśvāyatā dīrghamāyuraiśvaryamūrdhvataḥ smṛtam .
gavāḍhyatāmadhastāttu karotīti vidurbudhāḥ . . 6
meaning:
पार्श्वायता दीर्घमायुरैश्वर्यमूर्ध्वतः स्मृतम् .
गवाढ्यतामधस्तात्तु करोतीति विदुर्बुधाः . . 6
text_mt: Extended to the sides, [it indicates] long life; upward, sovereignty is remembered; / downward, the wise know that it brings abundance of cattle.

sanskrit_iast:
śatapatrakarṇikābhā nābhiryasya mahāmate .
bhūpatvaṃ kurute sā tu puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 7
meaning:
शतपत्रकर्णिकाभा नाभिर्यस्य महामते .
भूपत्वं कुरुते सा तु पुरुषस्य न संशयः . . 7
text_mt: A navel that resembles the pericarp of a lotus, O highly intelligent one, / makes a man a ruler of the earth; there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
samodaro bhavedbhogī nisvaḥ syādviṣamodaraḥ .
sūkṣmodaro bhavedvāgmī bahusampatsamanvitaḥ . . 8
meaning:
समोदरो भवेद्भोगी निस्वः स्याद्विषमोदरः .
सूक्ष्मोदरो भवेद्वाग्मी बहुसम्पत्समन्वितः . . 8
text_mt: One with an even abdomen will be an enjoyer of pleasures; one with an uneven abdomen will be destitute. / One with a slender abdomen will be eloquent and endowed with much prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
śastreṇāntaṃ vrajedvīra strībhogaṃ cāpnuyāttathā .
ācāryo bahuputraśca yathāsaṅkhyaṃ vinirdiśet . . 9
meaning:
शस्त्रेणान्तं व्रजेद्वीर स्त्रीभोगं चाप्नुयात्तथा .
आचार्यो बहुपुत्रश्च यथासङ्ख्यं विनिर्दिशेत् . . 9
text_mt: He will meet his end by a weapon, O hero, and likewise obtain the enjoyment of women; / he becomes a teacher and has many sons: one should declare [these results] respectively,

sanskrit_iast:
valibhirdevaśārdūla ityāha sa payonidhiḥ .
agamyāgāmino jñeyā viṣamābhirna saṃśayaḥ . . 1.26.10
meaning:
वलिभिर्देवशार्दूल इत्याह स पयोनिधिः .
अगम्यागामिनो ज्ञेया विषमाभिर्न संशयः . . 1.26.10
text_mt: by means of the skin-folds, O tiger among gods; so said the ocean. / Those who have irregular folds are known as having intercourse with forbidden women, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛjubhirvasubhogī syātparadāravinindakaḥ .
māṃsalairmṛdubhiḥ pārśvai rājā syānnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 11
meaning:
ऋजुभिर्वसुभोगी स्यात्परदारविनिन्दकः .
मांसलैर्मृदुभिः पार्श्वै राजा स्यान्नात्र संशयः . . 11
text_mt: With straight folds, he will enjoy wealth and condemn another's wife. / With fleshy, soft flanks, one becomes a king; there is no doubt in this.

sanskrit_iast:
anūrdhvacibukā ye tu subhagāste bhavanti vai .
nirdhanā viṣamairdīrghairbhavantīha suvīraja . . 12
meaning:
अनूर्ध्वचिबुका ये तु सुभगास्ते भवन्ति वै .
निर्धना विषमैर्दीर्घैर्भवन्तीह सुवीरज . . 12
text_mt: Those whose chins are not raised are indeed fortunate. / With irregular, long chins, they become destitute here, O son of Suvīra.

sanskrit_iast:
pīnaiścopacitairnimnaiḥ 1 skandhairbhīmāṅgasambhava .
rājānaḥ sukhinaścāpi bhavantīha na saṃśayaḥ . . 13
meaning:
पीनैश्चोपचितैर्निम्नैः 1 स्कन्धैर्भीमाङ्गसम्भव .
राजानः सुखिनश्चापि भवन्तीह न संशयः . . 13
text_mt: With shoulders that are plump, well-developed, and low, O son of Bhīmāṅga, / men become kings and happy here; there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
samonnataṃ tu hṛdayaṃ samaṃ ca pṛthu caiva hi .
avepanaṃ māṃsalaṃ ca pārthivānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ . . 14
meaning:
समोन्नतं तु हृदयं समं च पृथु चैव हि .
अवेपनं मांसलं च पार्थिवानां न संशयः . . 14
text_mt: A chest that is symmetrical and elevated, even, broad, / unquivering, and fleshy belongs to rulers of the earth, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
khararomacitaṃ vīraśirālaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
adhanānāṃ bhavedeva hṛdayaṃ ṛbhavottama . .
samavakṣaso'rthayutāḥ pīnaiḥ śūrāḥ smṛtā budhaiḥ . . 15
meaning:
खररोमचितं वीरशिरालं च विशेषतः .
अधनानां भवेदेव हृदयं ऋभवोत्तम . .
समवक्षसोऽर्थयुताः पीनैः शूराः स्मृता बुधैः . . 15
text_mt: Covered with rough hair, O hero, and especially veiny, / such a chest belongs indeed to the poor, O best of Ṛbhus. / Those with symmetrical chests possess wealth; with plump chests, they are considered by the wise to be heroes.

sanskrit_iast:
tanubhirdravyahīnāḥ syurasamaiścāpyakiñcanāḥ .
vadhyante cāpi śastreṇa nātra kāryā vicāraṇā . . 16
meaning:
तनुभिर्द्रव्यहीनाः स्युरसमैश्चाप्यकिञ्चनाः .
वध्यन्ते चापि शस्त्रेण नात्र कार्या विचारणा . . 16
text_mt: With thin [chests] they are devoid of wealth, and with uneven ones they are impoverished; / they are also killed by a weapon: no doubt should be entertained here.

sanskrit_iast:
hanubhirviṣamairvīra janmahīno bhavennaraḥ .
yasyonnato bhaveddhanuḥ sa bhogī syānna saṃśayaḥ . . 17
meaning:
हनुभिर्विषमैर्वीर जन्महीनो भवेन्नरः .
यस्योन्नतो भवेद्धनुः स भोगी स्यान्न संशयः . . 17
text_mt: With uneven jaws, O hero, a man becomes base-born. / One whose jaw is prominent will be an enjoyer, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
nirmāṃsairviṣamairvīra niḥsvo nimnaiḥ pracakṣyate .
dhanavāṃśca bhavetpīnaiḥ sukhabhogasamanvitaḥ . .
viṣamairarthahīnaḥ syādduḥkhabhāgī sadā naraḥ . . 18
meaning:
निर्मांसैर्विषमैर्वीर निःस्वो निम्नैः प्रचक्ष्यते .
धनवांश्च भवेत्पीनैः सुखभोगसमन्वितः . .
विषमैरर्थहीनः स्याद्दुःखभागी सदा नरः . . 18
text_mt: With fleshless and uneven [jaws], O hero, [and] with sunken ones, he is declared destitute; / with plump ones, he will be wealthy and endowed with pleasure and enjoyment; / with uneven ones, a man is devoid of wealth and always shares in suffering.

sanskrit_iast:
cipiṭagrīvako duṣṭo mato loke sa vai guha .
śūraḥ syānmahiṣagrīvo mṛgagrīvo bhayāturaḥ . . 19
meaning:
चिपिटग्रीवको दुष्टो मतो लोके स वै गुह .
शूरः स्यान्महिषग्रीवो मृगग्रीवो भयातुरः . . 19
text_mt: One with a flat neck is regarded in the world as wicked, O Guha. / One with a buffalo-neck is a hero; one with a deer-neck is stricken with fear.

sanskrit_iast:
kambugrīvo bhavedrājā lambakaṇṭho'gralakṣaṇaḥ .
hrasvagrīvastu dhanavānsusukhī bhogavāṃstathā . . 1.26.20
meaning:
कम्बुग्रीवो भवेद्राजा लम्बकण्ठोऽग्रलक्षणः .
ह्रस्वग्रीवस्तु धनवान्सुसुखी भोगवांस्तथा . . 1.26.20
text_mt: One with a conch-neck becomes a king; one with a dangling throat has prominent features; / but one with a short neck is wealthy, very happy, and an enjoyer.

sanskrit_iast:
nimāṃsau romaśau bhagnāvalpau vāpi viśeṣataḥ .
nirdhanasyedṛśāvaṃsau prakhyātau vyomakeśaja . . 21
meaning:
निमांसौ रोमशौ भग्नावल्पौ वापि विशेषतः .
निर्धनस्येदृशावंसौ प्रख्यातौ व्योमकेशज . . 21
text_mt: Fleshless, hairy, broken, or especially small: / such are the shoulders celebrated for an impoverished person, O son of Vyomakeśa.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavedaromaśaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ dhanināṃ bhīmasambhava .
salomaśaṃ tathā vakraṃ nirdhanānāṃ balādhipa . . 22
meaning:
भवेदरोमशं पृष्ठं धनिनां भीमसम्भव .
सलोमशं तथा वक्रं निर्धनानां बलाधिप . . 22
text_mt: The back of the wealthy is hairless, O son of Bhīma; / hairy and crooked, [it belongs] to the destitute, O lord of the army.

sanskrit_iast:
asvedanāvunnatau ca tathā pīnau ṣaḍānana .
samaromasugandhau ca kakṣau jñeyau dhanānvitau . . 23
meaning:
अस्वेदनावुन्नतौ च तथा पीनौ षडानन .
समरोमसुगन्धौ च कक्षौ ज्ञेयौ धनान्वितौ . . 23
text_mt: Free from sweat, elevated, and likewise fleshy, O six-faced one, / with even hair and fragrant: such armpits should be known as belonging to the wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
avyucchinnau tathā śliṣṭau vipulau ca surādhipa .
śūrāṇāmīdṛśāvaṃsau nagajānandavardhana . . 24
meaning:
अव्युच्छिन्नौ तथा श्लिष्टौ विपुलौ च सुराधिप .
शूराणामीदृशावंसौ नगजानन्दवर्धन . . 24
text_mt: Unbroken, closely joined, and broad, O lord of the gods: / such shoulders belong to heroes, O increaser of the joy of the mountain-born [goddess].

sanskrit_iast:
udvṛddhabāhuko yastu vadhabandhanamāpnuyāt .
dīrghabāhurbhavedrājā samudravacanaṃ yathā . . 25
meaning:
उद्वृद्धबाहुको यस्तु वधबन्धनमाप्नुयात् .
दीर्घबाहुर्भवेद्राजा समुद्रवचनं यथा . . 25
text_mt: One who has overgrown arms meets with execution and bondage. / One with long arms becomes a king, according to the words of the Ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
pralambabāhurvijñeyo naraḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ .
hrasvabāhurbhaveddāsaḥ parapreṣyakaro'pi vā . . 26
meaning:
प्रलम्बबाहुर्विज्ञेयो नरः सर्वगुणान्वितः .
ह्रस्वबाहुर्भवेद्दासः परप्रेष्यकरोऽपि वा . . 26
text_mt: A man with long-hanging arms should be known as endowed with all good qualities. / One with short arms becomes a servant or even one who carries out tasks for others.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmāvartabhujā ye tu dīrghāyatabhujāśca ye .
sampūrṇabāhū rājā syādityāha sa payonidhiḥ . . 27
meaning:
वामावर्तभुजा ये तु दीर्घायतभुजाश्च ये .
सम्पूर्णबाहू राजा स्यादित्याह स पयोनिधिः . . 27
text_mt: Those whose arms curl to the left, and those whose arms are long and extended, / having well-rounded arms, will become kings; so said the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
grīvā ca 1vartulākārā kamburekhāsamāvṛtā .
sa bhavetpārthivo bhūmau sarvaduṣṭanibarhaṇaḥ . . 28
meaning:
ग्रीवा च 1वर्तुलाकारा कम्बुरेखासमावृता .
स भवेत्पार्थिवो भूमौ सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हणः . . 28
text_mt: And a neck that is circular in shape and marked with lines like a conch: / he will become a ruler on earth who destroys all wicked men.

sanskrit_iast:
dīrghagrīvā bakagrīvā śukagrīvāśca ye narāḥ .
uṣṭragrīvāḥ karigrīvāḥ sarve te nirdhanāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 29
meaning:
दीर्घग्रीवा बकग्रीवा शुकग्रीवाश्च ये नराः .
उष्ट्रग्रीवाः करिग्रीवाः सर्वे ते निर्धनाः स्मृताः . . 29
text_mt: Men with long necks, heron-necks, parrot-necks, / camel-necks, and elephant-necks: all these are remembered as destitute.

sanskrit_iast:
ibhāṅgasadṛśau2 vṛttau samau pīnau ca suvrata .
ājānulambinau bāhū pārthivānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ . . 1.26.30
meaning:
इभाङ्गसदृशौ2 वृत्तौ समौ पीनौ च सुव्रत .
आजानुलम्बिनौ बाहू पार्थिवानां न संशयः . . 1.26.30
text_mt: Resembling an elephant's trunk, rounded, even, and plump, O you of good vows, / reaching down to the knees: such arms belong to rulers of the earth, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
daridrāṇāṃ lomaśau hrasvau bāhū jñeyau surottama .
taskarāṇāṃ ca viṣamau sthūlau sūkṣmau ca suvrata . . 31
meaning:
दरिद्राणां लोमशौ ह्रस्वौ बाहू ज्ञेयौ सुरोत्तम .
तस्कराणां च विषमौ स्थूलौ सूक्ष्मौ च सुव्रत . . 31
text_mt: Hairy and short arms should be known as belonging to the poor, O best of the gods; / and uneven, thick, and thin [arms belong] to thieves, O you of good vows.

sanskrit_iast:
nimnaṃ karatalaṃ yasya pitṛvittaṃ na tasya vai .
bhavedārbhavaśārdūla tathā bhīruśca mānavaḥ . . 32
meaning:
निम्नं करतलं यस्य पितृवित्तं न तस्य वै .
भवेदार्भवशार्दूल तथा भीरुश्च मानवः . . 32
text_mt: One whose palm is depressed does not possess ancestral wealth, / O tiger among the descendants of Ṛbhu, and that man is timid.

sanskrit_iast:
suvṛttatanunimnena dhanavānkaratalena tu .
uttānakaratalo dātā bhavatīti na saṃśayaḥ . . 33
meaning:
सुवृत्ततनुनिम्नेन धनवान्करतलेन तु .
उत्तानकरतलो दाता भवतीति न संशयः . . 33
text_mt: With a well-rounded, thin, and slightly sunken palm, one is wealthy; / one whose palm is upturned becomes a generous giver: there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣamā bhavanti viṣamairnimnāścāpi viśeṣataḥ .
karatalairdevaśārdūla lākṣābhairīśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 34
meaning:
विषमा भवन्ति विषमैर्निम्नाश्चापि विशेषतः .
करतलैर्देवशार्दूल लाक्षाभैरीश्वराः स्मृताः . . 34
text_mt: They become irregular with irregular [palms], and especially depressed ones; / with palms resembling red lac, O tiger among gods, they are remembered as lords.

sanskrit_iast:
agamyāgamanaṃ pītai rūkṣairnirdhanatā smṛtā .
apeyapānaṃ kurvanti nīlakṛṣṇaiḥ sadaiva hi . . 35
meaning:
अगम्यागमनं पीतै रूक्षैर्निर्धनता स्मृता .
अपेयपानं कुर्वन्ति नीलकृष्णैः सदैव हि . . 35
text_mt: With yellow [palms], there is intercourse with forbidden women; with rough ones, poverty is remembered; / with dark-blue ones, they always engage in drinking forbidden drink.

sanskrit_iast:
nimnāḥ snigdhā bhavennṛṇāṃ rekhā karatale guha .
dhanināṃ na daridrāṇāmityāha sa payonidhiḥ . . 36
meaning:
निम्नाः स्निग्धा भवेन्नृणां रेखा करतले गुह .
धनिनां न दरिद्राणामित्याह स पयोनिधिः . . 36
text_mt: Depressed and glossy are the lines on men's palms, O Guha, / of the rich, not of the poor; so said the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
viralāṅgulayo ye tu te daridrāḥ pracakṣate .
dhaninastu mahābāho ye ghanāṅgulayo narāḥ . . 37
meaning:
विरलाङ्गुलयो ये तु ते दरिद्राः प्रचक्षते .
धनिनस्तु महाबाहो ये घनाङ्गुलयो नराः . . 37
text_mt: Those whose fingers are spaced apart are declared poor; / but those men whose fingers are closely set are wealthy, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit_iast:
vadanaṃ maṇḍalaṃ yasya dharmaśīlaṃ tamādiśet .
śuṇḍavaktrā narā ye tu durbhagāste na saṃśayaḥ . . 38
meaning:
वदनं मण्डलं यस्य धर्मशीलं तमादिशेत् .
शुण्डवक्त्रा नरा ये तु दुर्भगास्ते न संशयः . . 38
