text_mt: One whose face is circular should be declared righteous; / but men whose faces are like a trunk are unfortunate, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
harivaktrā jihmavaktrā vikṛtāsyāstathā narāḥ .
bhagnavatrāḥ karālāsyā sarve te taskarāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 39
meaning:
हरिवक्त्रा जिह्मवक्त्रा विकृतास्यास्तथा नराः .
भग्नवत्राः करालास्या सर्वे ते तस्कराः स्मृताः . . 39
text_mt: Men with monkey-faces, crooked faces, and deformed faces, / broken faces, and dreadful faces: all these are remembered as thieves.

sanskrit_iast:
sampūrṇavaktrā rājāno gajasiṃhānanāstathā .
chāgavānaravaktrāśca dhaninaḥ parikīrtitāḥ . . 1.26.40
meaning:
सम्पूर्णवक्त्रा राजानो गजसिंहाननास्तथा .
छागवानरवक्त्राश्च धनिनः परिकीर्तिताः . . 1.26.40
text_mt: Those with full faces are kings, as are those with elephant- and lion-faces; / and those with goat- and monkey-faces are celebrated as wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya gaṇḍau susampūrṇau padmapatrasamaprabhau .
kṛṣibhāgī bhavennityaṃ bahuvittaśca mānavaḥ . . 41
meaning:
यस्य गण्डौ सुसम्पूर्णौ पद्मपत्रसमप्रभौ .
कृषिभागी भवेन्नित्यं बहुवित्तश्च मानवः . . 41
text_mt: A man whose cheeks are completely full and have the luster of a lotus petal / is constantly blessed with agriculture and possesses much wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhavyāghragajendrāṇāṃ kapolaḥ sadṛśo yadi .
mahābhogī sa vijñeyaḥ senāyāścaiva nāyakaḥ . . 42
meaning:
सिंहव्याघ्रगजेन्द्राणां कपोलः सदृशो यदि .
महाभोगी स विज्ञेयः सेनायाश्चैव नायकः . . 42
text_mt: If a cheek is like those of lions, tigers, and lordly elephants, / he should be known as a great enjoyer and a commander of an army.

sanskrit_iast:
vadanaṃ tu samaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ saumyaṃ saṃvṛtameva hi .
pārthivānāṃ mahābāho viparītantu duḥkhadam . . 43
meaning:
वदनं तु समं श्लक्ष्णं सौम्यं संवृतमेव हि .
पार्थिवानां महाबाहो विपरीतन्तु दुःखदम् . . 43
text_mt: A face that is symmetrical, smooth, pleasant, and well-covered / belongs to rulers of the earth, O mighty-armed one; the opposite brings suffering.

sanskrit_iast:
mahāmukhaṃ tu deveśa durbhagatvaṃ prayacchati .
strīmukhaṃ putranāśāya maṇḍalaṃ sukhitāṃ vrajet . . 44
meaning:
महामुखं तु देवेश दुर्भगत्वं प्रयच्छति .
स्त्रीमुखं पुत्रनाशाय मण्डलं सुखितां व्रजेत् . . 44
text_mt: A huge face, O lord of the gods, bestows misfortune; / a woman-like face leads to the destruction of sons; a circular [face] attains happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
dravyanāśāya vai dīrghaṃ pāpadaṃ bhayadaṃ tathā .
dhūrtānāṃ caturasraṃ syātputrahānikaraṃ śṛṇu . . 45
meaning:
द्रव्यनाशाय वै दीर्घं पापदं भयदं तथा .
धूर्तानां चतुरस्रं स्यात्पुत्रहानिकरं शृणु . . 45
text_mt: A long face brings loss of wealth, produces sin, and produces fear; / a square face belongs to rogues and causes loss of sons: listen!

sanskrit_iast:
nimnavaktraṃ ca devendra putrahānikaraṃ bhavet .
hrasvaṃ bhatati kīnāśe pūrṇakāntaṃ ca bhoginām . . 46
meaning:
निम्नवक्त्रं च देवेन्द्र पुत्रहानिकरं भवेत् .
ह्रस्वं भतति कीनाशे पूर्णकान्तं च भोगिनाम् . . 46
text_mt: A depressed face, O lord of the gods, causes loss of sons; / a short one belongs to a miser, and one full and pleasing belongs to enjoyers.

sanskrit_iast:
raktādharo narapatirdhanavānkamalādharaḥ .
sthūloṣṭhā hanumūlāśca śuṣkaistīkṣṇaiśca duḥkhitāḥ . .47
meaning:
रक्ताधरो नरपतिर्धनवान्कमलाधरः .
स्थूलोष्ठा हनुमूलाश्च शुष्कैस्तीक्ष्णैश्च दुःखिताः . .47
text_mt: One with red lower lip is a lord of men; one with lotus-like lower lip is wealthy; / those with thick lips and jaws [are miserable], and with dry and sharp ones they are sorrowful.

sanskrit_iast:
asphoṭitāgraṃ snigdhaṃ ca nataṃ mṛdu tathā guha .
sampūrṇaṃ ca sadā śastaṃ śmaśru bhūmipaterguha . . 48
meaning:
अस्फोटिताग्रं स्निग्धं च नतं मृदु तथा गुह .
सम्पूर्णं च सदा शस्तं श्मश्रु भूमिपतेर्गुह . . 48
text_mt: With unspilt ends, glossy, downward-curving, soft, O Guha, / and full: such a beard is always praised for a ruler of the earth, O Guha.

sanskrit_iast:
raktaiścālpaistathā rūkṣaiḥ śmaśrubhirbhīmanandana .
narāścaurā bhavantyeva paradāraratāstathā . .49
meaning:
रक्तैश्चाल्पैस्तथा रूक्षैः श्मश्रुभिर्भीमनन्दन .
नराश्चौरा भवन्त्येव परदाररतास्तथा . .49
text_mt: With reddish, sparse, and rough beards, O delight of Bhīma, / men indeed become thieves and devoted to others' wives.

sanskrit_iast:
nirmāṃsau yasya vai karṇau saṃgrāmānnāśamṛcchati 1 .
cipiṭābhyāṃ bhavedrogī hrasvau ca kṛpaṇasya ca . . 1.26.50
meaning:
निर्मांसौ यस्य वै कर्णौ संग्रामान्नाशमृच्छति 1 .
चिपिटाभ्यां भवेद्रोगी ह्रस्वौ च कृपणस्य च . . 1.26.50
text_mt: One whose ears are fleshless goes to destruction from battle; / with flat ears, one becomes diseased; and short ears belong to a miser.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkukarṇaśca bhūnāthaḥ sarvaśatrubhayaṅkaraḥ .
dīrghāyū romaśābhyāṃ tu vipulābhyāṃ narādhipaḥ . .
bhogī ca sa bhavennityaṃ devabrāhmaṇapūjakaḥ . . 51
meaning:
शङ्कुकर्णश्च भूनाथः सर्वशत्रुभयङ्करः .
दीर्घायू रोमशाभ्यां तु विपुलाभ्यां नराधिपः . .
भोगी च स भवेन्नित्यं देवब्राह्मणपूजकः . . 51
text_mt: One with peg-shaped ears is a lord of the earth who strikes fear into all enemies; / with hairy [ears] he is long-lived; with broad ones he is a ruler of men, / and he is always an enjoyer, worshipping the gods and brahmins.

sanskrit_iast:
śirāvabaddhau krūrasya vyālambau ca viśeṣataḥ .
māṃsalau sukhadau jñeyau śravaṇau vyomakeśaja . . 52
meaning:
शिरावबद्धौ क्रूरस्य व्यालम्बौ च विशेषतः .
मांसलौ सुखदौ ज्ञेयौ श्रवणौ व्योमकेशज . . 52
text_mt: Encompassed with veins, and especially pendulous, [ears] belong to a cruel man; / fleshy ears should be known as granting happiness, O son of Vyomakeśa.

sanskrit_iast:
bhogī syānnigaṇḍo vai mantrī sampūrṇagaṇḍakaḥ .
śubhabhākchukanāsastu cirajīvī śuṣkanāsikaḥ . . 53
meaning:
भोगी स्यान्निगण्डो वै मन्त्री सम्पूर्णगण्डकः .
शुभभाक्छुकनासस्तु चिरजीवी शुष्कनासिकः . . 53
text_mt: One with fleshy cheeks will enjoy pleasures, while one with full cheeks will become a minister. / One with a nose like a parrot's beak attains good fortune, but one with a dry nose lives long.

sanskrit_iast:
kundakuṇḍalasaṅkāśaiḥ prakāśairdaśanairnṛpaḥ .
ṛkṣavānaradantāśca nityaṃ kṣutparipīḍitāḥ . . 54
meaning:
कुन्दकुण्डलसङ्काशैः प्रकाशैर्दशनैर्नृपः .
ऋक्षवानरदन्ताश्च नित्यं क्षुत्परिपीडिताः . . 54
text_mt: A king has bright teeth resembling jasmine buds and earrings. / Those with teeth like bears or monkeys are constantly afflicted with hunger.

sanskrit_iast:
hastidantāḥ kharadantāḥ snigdhadantā guṇānvitāḥ .
karālairviralai rūkṣairdaśanairduḥkhajīvinaḥ . . 55
meaning:
हस्तिदन्ताः खरदन्ताः स्निग्धदन्ता गुणान्विताः .
करालैर्विरलै रूक्षैर्दशनैर्दुःखजीविनः . . 55
text_mt: Those with elephant-like teeth, donkey-like teeth, and glossy teeth are endowed with virtues. / With dreadful, sparse, and rough teeth, men live in misery.

sanskrit_iast:
dvātriṃśaddantā rājāna ekatriṃśacca bhogavān .
triṃśaddantā narā nityaṃ sukhaduḥkhitvabhāgina . .
ūnatriṃśacya daśanaiḥ puruṣāḥ duḥkhabhāginaḥ . . 56
meaning:
द्वात्रिंशद्दन्ता राजान एकत्रिंशच्च भोगवान् .
त्रिंशद्दन्ता नरा नित्यं सुखदुःखित्वभागिन . .
ऊनत्रिंशच्य दशनैः पुरुषाः दुःखभागिनः . . 56
text_mt: Those with thirty-two teeth are kings, and with thirty-one, one enjoys pleasures; / men with thirty teeth constantly partake in pleasure and pain, / and men with fewer than thirty teeth partake in sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇajihvo bhavetpreṣyaḥ savalayā tu jihvayā .
bhavetkopasya kartā vai sthūlarūkṣaśca jihvayā . . 57
meaning:
कृष्णजिह्वो भवेत्प्रेष्यः सवलया तु जिह्वया .
भवेत्कोपस्य कर्ता वै स्थूलरूक्षश्च जिह्वया . . 57
text_mt: One with a black tongue will be a servant; with a ringed tongue, / he will surely be prone to anger; and with a thick and rough tongue, [he will be the same].

sanskrit_iast:
śvetajihvā narā jñeyāḥ śaucācārasamanvitāḥ .
padmapatrasamā jihvā sūkṣmā dīrghā suśobhanā . .
sthūlā ca na ca vistīrṇā yeṣāṃ te manujādhipāḥ . . 58
meaning:
श्वेतजिह्वा नरा ज्ञेयाः शौचाचारसमन्विताः .
पद्मपत्रसमा जिह्वा सूक्ष्मा दीर्घा सुशोभना . .
स्थूला च न च विस्तीर्णा येषां ते मनुजाधिपाः . . 58
text_mt: Men with white tongues are to be known as endowed with purity and good conduct. / Those whose tongue is like a lotus petal, thin, long, very handsome, / thick and yet not [overly] broad, are rulers of men.

sanskrit_iast:
nimnā snigdhā ca hrasvā ca raktāgrā rasanā yadi .
sarvavidyāpravaktāraste bhavanti na saṃśayaḥ . . 59
meaning:
निम्ना स्निग्धा च ह्रस्वा च रक्ताग्रा रसना यदि .
सर्वविद्याप्रवक्तारस्ते भवन्ति न संशयः . . 59
text_mt: If the tongue is concave, glossy, short, and red-tipped, / they become expounders of all branches of knowledge, without a doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇatālurnaro yastu sa bhavetkulanāśanaḥ .
sukhabhāgī duḥkhabhāgī pītatālurnarādhipaḥ . . 1.26.60
meaning:
कृष्णतालुर्नरो यस्तु स भवेत्कुलनाशनः .
सुखभागी दुःखभागी पीततालुर्नराधिपः . . 1.26.60
text_mt: A man whose palate is black will be a destroyer of his family. / A king whose palate is yellow partakes in both pleasure and sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
vikṛtaṃ sphuṭitaṃ rūkṣaṃ tālukaṃ na praśasyate .
siṃhatālurnarapatirgajatālustathaiva ca . .
padmatālurbhavedrājā śvetatālurdhaneśvaraḥ . . 61
meaning:
विकृतं स्फुटितं रूक्षं तालुकं न प्रशस्यते .
सिंहतालुर्नरपतिर्गजतालुस्तथैव च . .
पद्मतालुर्भवेद्राजा श्वेततालुर्धनेश्वरः . . 61
text_mt: A palate that is deformed, cracked, or rough is not praised. / One with a lion-like palate is a lord of men, and likewise one with an elephant-like palate; / one with a lotus-like palate will be a king, and one with a white palate is a master of wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsasvarā narā dhanyā meghagambhīraniḥsvanāḥ .
krauṃcasvanāśca rājāno bhogavanto mahādhanāḥ . . 62
meaning:
हंसस्वरा नरा धन्या मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनाः .
क्रौंचस्वनाश्च राजानो भोगवन्तो महाधनाः . . 62
text_mt: Blessed are men with voices like swans or with sounds deep like a thundercloud. / Kings with voices like krauñca birds are prosperous and very wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
cakravākasvanā dhanyā rājāno dharmavatsalāḥ .
kumbhasvano narapatirdundubhisvana eva ca . .
rūkṣadīrghasvarāḥ krūrāḥ paśūnāṃ sadṛśā na tu . . 63
meaning:
चक्रवाकस्वना धन्या राजानो धर्मवत्सलाः .
कुम्भस्वनो नरपतिर्दुन्दुभिस्वन एव च . .
रूक्षदीर्घस्वराः क्रूराः पशूनां सदृशा न तु . . 63
text_mt: Blessed are kings with voices like cakravāka birds, devoted to righteousness. / A lord of men has a voice like a pot or a voice like a war drum. / Those with harsh and elongated voices are cruel, yet not like beasts.

sanskrit_iast:
2gurgurasvarasaṃyuktāḥ puruṣāḥ kleśabhāginaḥ .
cāṣasvanā bhāgyayutā bhinnakāṃsyasvarāśca ye . .
kṣīṇabhinnasvarā ye syuradhamāste prakīrtitāḥ . . 64
meaning:
2गुर्गुरस्वरसंयुक्ताः पुरुषाः क्लेशभागिनः .
चाषस्वना भाग्ययुता भिन्नकांस्यस्वराश्च ये . .
क्षीणभिन्नस्वरा ये स्युरधमास्ते प्रकीर्तिताः . . 64
text_mt: Men endowed with a rumbling voice partake in misery. / Those with voices like the cāṣa bird are fortunate, as are those with voices like cracked brass; / those who have faint and cracked voices are declared to be vile.

sanskrit_iast:
pārthivāstanunāsāśca dīrghanāsāśca bhoginaḥ .
hrasvanāsā narā ye tu dharmaśīlāstu te matāḥ . . 65
meaning:
पार्थिवास्तनुनासाश्च दीर्घनासाश्च भोगिनः .
ह्रस्वनासा नरा ये तु धर्मशीलास्तु ते मताः . . 65
text_mt: Rulers of the earth have slender noses, and those with long noses enjoy pleasures; / but those men who have short noses are regarded as righteous in nature.

sanskrit_iast:
hastyaśvasiṃhanāsāśca sūcīnāsāśca ye narāḥ .
teṣāṃ sidhyati vāṇijyaṃ hayānāṃ caiva vikrayaḥ . . 66
meaning:
हस्त्यश्वसिंहनासाश्च सूचीनासाश्च ये नराः .
तेषां सिध्यति वाणिज्यं हयानां चैव विक्रयः . . 66
text_mt: Men who have noses like elephants, horses, or lions, or needle-like noses— / for them trade succeeds, as does the selling of horses.

sanskrit_iast:
vikṛtā nāsikā yasya 3sthūlāgrā rūpavarjitā .
pāpakarmā sa vijñeyaḥ sāmudravacanaṃ yathā . . 67
meaning:
विकृता नासिका यस्य 3स्थूलाग्रा रूपवर्जिता .
पापकर्मा स विज्ञेयः सामुद्रवचनं यथा . . 67
text_mt: He whose nose is deformed, thick-tipped, and devoid of beauty / should be known as an evildoer, according to the words of Sāmudra.

sanskrit_iast:
dāḍimīpuṣpasaṃkāśe bhavetāṃ yasya locane .
4 bhūpatiḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ saptadvīpādhipo guha . . 68
meaning:
दाडिमीपुष्पसंकाशे भवेतां यस्य लोचने .
4 भूपतिः स तु विज्ञेयः सप्तद्वीपाधिपो गुह . . 68
text_mt: He whose two eyes resemble the flower of a pomegranate / is to be known, O Guha, as a king, ruler of the seven continents.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāghrākṣāḥ kopanā jñeyāḥ ka5rkaṭākṣāḥ kalipriyāḥ .
biḍālahaṃsanetrāśca bhavanti puruṣādhamāḥ . . 69
meaning:
व्याघ्राक्षाः कोपना ज्ञेयाः क5र्कटाक्षाः कलिप्रियाः .
बिडालहंसनेत्राश्च भवन्ति पुरुषाधमाः . . 69
text_mt: Those with tiger-like eyes are to be known as irritable; those with crab-like eyes are fond of strife; / and men with cat-like or swan-like eyes become vile.

sanskrit_iast:
mapūranakulākṣāśca narāste madhyamāḥ smṛtāḥ .
na 1śrīstyajati sarvajña puruṣaṃ madhupiṅgalam . . 1.26.70
meaning:
मपूरनकुलाक्षाश्च नरास्ते मध्यमाः स्मृताः .
न 1श्रीस्त्यजति सर्वज्ञ पुरुषं मधुपिङ्गलम् . . 1.26.70
text_mt: Men with eyes like peacocks or mongooses are remembered as middling. / Fortune does not abandon a man with honey-tawny eyes, O all-knowing one.

sanskrit_iast:
āpiṅgalākṣā rājānaḥ sarvabhogasamanvitāḥ .
rocanā haritālākṣā guñjāpiṅgā dhaneśvarāḥ . .
balasattvaguṇopetāḥ pṛthivīcakravartinaḥ . . 71
meaning:
आपिङ्गलाक्षा राजानः सर्वभोगसमन्विताः .
रोचना हरितालाक्षा गुञ्जापिङ्गा धनेश्वराः . .
बलसत्त्वगुणोपेताः पृथिवीचक्रवर्तिनः . . 71
text_mt: Kings with reddish-brown eyes are endowed with all pleasures. / Those with eyes like yellow pigment or orpiment, or tawny like guñjā berries, are lords of wealth, / endowed with strength, vigour, and virtues, and are universal emperors over the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
dvimātrāvīkṣaṇā nityaṃ jīvanti paramāśritāḥ .
trimātrāsyandino jñeyāḥ puruṣāḥ sukhabhāginaḥ . . 72
meaning:
द्विमात्रावीक्षणा नित्यं जीवन्ति परमाश्रिताः .
त्रिमात्रास्यन्दिनो ज्ञेयाः पुरुषाः सुखभागिनः . . 72
text_mt: Those whose gaze lasts two mātrās constantly live dependent on others. / Men whose flow of tears lasts three mātrās are known to partake in happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
caturmātrānimeṣaiśca nayanairīśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ .
dīrghāyuṣo dharmaratāḥ pañcamātrānimeṣiṇaḥ . . 73
meaning:
चतुर्मात्रानिमेषैश्च नयनैरीश्वराः स्मृताः .
दीर्घायुषो धर्मरताः पञ्चमात्रानिमेषिणः . . 73
text_mt: With eyes blinking every four mātrās, they are remembered as lords. / Those blinking every five mātrās live long and are devoted to righteousness.

sanskrit_iast:
hrasvakarṇā mahābhāgā mahākarṇāśca ye narāḥ .
āvartakarṇā dhaninaḥ snigdhakarṇāstathaiva ca . . 74
meaning:
ह्रस्वकर्णा महाभागा महाकर्णाश्च ये नराः .
आवर्तकर्णा धनिनः स्निग्धकर्णास्तथैव च . . 74
text_mt: Men who have short ears are highly fortunate, as are those with large ears. / Those with coiled ears are wealthy, as are those with glossy ears.

sanskrit_iast:
dīrghāyuṣaḥ śuktikarṇāḥ śaṅkhakarṇā mahādhanāḥ .
dīrghāyuṣo dīrghakarṇā lambakarṇāstapasvinaḥ . . 75
meaning:
दीर्घायुषः शुक्तिकर्णाः शङ्खकर्णा महाधनाः .
दीर्घायुषो दीर्घकर्णा लम्बकर्णास्तपस्विनः . . 75
text_mt: Those with pearl-oyster-shaped ears are long-lived; those with conch-shaped ears are very wealthy. / Those with long ears are long-lived; those with pendulous ears are ascetics.

sanskrit_iast:
lalāṭenārdhacandreṇa bhavanti pṛthivīśvarāḥ .
vipulena lalāṭena mahādhanapatiḥ smṛtaḥ . .
svalpena tu lalāṭena naro dharmarataḥ smṛtaḥ . . 76
meaning:
ललाटेनार्धचन्द्रेण भवन्ति पृथिवीश्वराः .
विपुलेन ललाटेन महाधनपतिः स्मृतः . .
स्वल्पेन तु ललाटेन नरो धर्मरतः स्मृतः . . 76
text_mt: By a crescent-shaped forehead men become lords of the earth. / By a broad forehead one is remembered as a master of great wealth; / but by a small forehead a man is remembered as devoted to righteousness.

sanskrit_iast:
rekhā pañca lalāṭe tu striyā vā puruṣasya vā .
śataṃ jīvati varṣāṇāmaiśvaryaṃ cādhigacchati . . 77
meaning:
रेखा पञ्च ललाटे तु स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा .
शतं जीवति वर्षाणामैश्वर्यं चाधिगच्छति . . 77
text_mt: If there are five lines on the forehead of a woman or a man, / that person lives for a hundred years and attains sovereignty.

sanskrit_iast:
catūrekhāmaśītiṃ tu tribhiḥ saptatimeva ca .
dvābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ tu rekhābhyāṃ catvāriṃśattathaikayā . .
arekhena lalāṭena vijñeyā pañcaviṃśatiḥ . . 78
meaning:
चतूरेखामशीतिं तु त्रिभिः सप्ततिमेव च .
द्वाभ्यां षष्टिं तु रेखाभ्यां चत्वारिंशत्तथैकया . .
अरेखेन ललाटेन विज्ञेया पञ्चविंशतिः . . 78
text_mt: With four lines, [one lives] eighty [years]; with three, seventy; / with two lines, sixty; and with one, forty. / With a forehead devoid of lines, twenty-five is to be known.

sanskrit_iast:
rekhācchedaistu vijñeyā hīnamadhyottamā narāḥ .
alpāyuṣastathālpābhirvyādhibhiḥ paripīḍitāḥ . . 79
meaning:
रेखाच्छेदैस्तु विज्ञेया हीनमध्योत्तमा नराः .
अल्पायुषस्तथाल्पाभिर्व्याधिभिः परिपीडिताः . . 79
text_mt: By breaks in the lines, men are to be known as low, middling, or superior. / Those with few [lines] are short-lived and afflicted by diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
triśūlaṃ paṭṭiśaṃ vāpi lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate .
īśvaraṃ taṃ vijānīyādbhoginaṃ kīrtimāśritam . . 1.26.80
meaning:
त्रिशूलं पट्टिशं वापि ललाटे यस्य दृश्यते .
ईश्वरं तं विजानीयाद्भोगिनं कीर्तिमाश्रितम् . . 1.26.80
text_mt: On whose forehead a trident or a spear is seen, / one should recognise him as a lord, an enjoyer of pleasures, endowed with renown.

sanskrit_iast:
utkrāntanimnaṃ tu śiraḥ svalpopahatameva ca .
candrākāraṃ1 narendrāṇāṃ gavāḍhyaṃ maṅgalaṃ smṛtam . . 81
meaning:
उत्क्रान्तनिम्नं तु शिरः स्वल्पोपहतमेव च .
चन्द्राकारं1 नरेन्द्राणां गवाढ्यं मङ्गलं स्मृतम् . . 81
text_mt: A head that is elevated and sunken, and slightly defective, / shaped like the moon, of kings, rich in cattle, is remembered as auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣamaṃ tu daridrāṇāṃ śiro dīrghaṃ tu duḥkhinām .
nāgakumbhanibhaṃ rājñaḥ samaṃ sarvatra bhoginaḥ . . 82
meaning:
विषमं तु दरिद्राणां शिरो दीर्घं तु दुःखिनाम् .
नागकुम्भनिभं राज्ञः समं सर्वत्र भोगिनः . . 82
text_mt: An uneven head belongs to the poor, while a long head belongs to the miserable. / A king's head resembles the frontal globes of an elephant; an enjoyer of pleasures has a head even everywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
kapilaḥ sphuṭitai rūkṣaiḥ sthūlaiśva śikhareśayaiḥ .
duḥkhitā puruṣā jñeyā romaśmaśrubhireva ca . . 83
meaning:
कपिलः स्फुटितै रूक्षैः स्थूलैश्व शिखरेशयैः .
दुःखिता पुरुषा ज्ञेया रोमश्मश्रुभिरेव च . . 83
text_mt: With tawny, split, rough, thick hairs resting on the crest, / as well as body-hair and beards [of that kind], men are to be known as miserable.

sanskrit_iast:
rūkṣā vivarṇā nistejāḥ kharāḥ sthūlāśca mūrdhajāḥ .
nātistokā na bahuśo mūrdhajā duḥkhabhāginaḥ . . 84
meaning:
रूक्षा विवर्णा निस्तेजाः खराः स्थूलाश्च मूर्धजाः .
नातिस्तोका न बहुशो मूर्धजा दुःखभागिनः . . 84
text_mt: Rough, discoloured, lustreless, harsh, and coarse head-hairs— / head-hairs that are neither too few nor very abundant—partake in sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
viralāśca mṛdusnigdhā bhramarāñjanasaprabhāḥ .
kacā yasya tu dṛśyante sa bhavetpṛthivīpatiḥ . . 85
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaḍviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 26 .
puruṣalakṣaṇa-varṇanam
meaning:
विरलाश्च मृदुस्निग्धा भ्रमराञ्जनसप्रभाः .
कचा यस्य तु दृश्यन्ते स भवेत्पृथिवीपतिः . . 85
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनं नाम षड्विंशोऽध्यायः . 26 .
पुरुषलक्षण-वर्णनम्
text_mt:
He whose hair is seen to be sparse, soft, glossy, and shining like a black bee or collyrium, / he will become a ruler of the earth.
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the fourth Kalpa, the twenty-sixth chapter, named "Description of the Marks of a Man."
Description of the Marks of a Man

sanskrit_iast:
kārtikeya uvāca
saṃkṣepato mama vibho lakṣaṇāni nṛpasya tu .
śubhāni cāṅgajātāni brūhi me vadatāṃ vara . . 1
meaning:
कार्तिकेय उवाच
संक्षेपतो मम विभो लक्षणानि नृपस्य तु .
शुभानि चाङ्गजातानि ब्रूहि मे वदतां वर . . 1
text_mt: Kārtikeya said: / In brief, O lord, best among speakers, / tell me the auspicious bodily marks of a king.
title: Puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
śṛṇu vakṣyeṅgajātāni pārthivasya śubhāni ca .
pārthivo jñāyate yaistu narāṇāṃ madhyabhāgataḥ . . 2
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणु वक्ष्येङ्गजातानि पार्थिवस्य शुभानि च .
पार्थिवो ज्ञायते यैस्तु नराणां मध्यभागतः . . 2
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Listen, I shall declare the auspicious bodily [marks] of an earthly king, / by which an earthly ruler is recognised from among men.

sanskrit_iast:
trīṇi yasya mahābāho vipulāni narasya tu .
udyatāni tathā ṣaḍ vai gambhīrāṇi ca trīṇi vai . . 3
meaning:
त्रीणि यस्य महाबाहो विपुलानि नरस्य तु .
उद्यतानि तथा षड् वै गम्भीराणि च त्रीणि वै . . 3
text_mt: A man whose three [parts] are broad, O mighty-armed one, / whose six are elevated, and whose three are deep;

sanskrit_iast:
catvāri cāpi hrasvāni sapta raktāni vā vibho .
dīrghāṇi cāpi sūkṣmāṇi bhavanti yasya pañca vā . . 4
meaning:
चत्वारि चापि ह्रस्वानि सप्त रक्तानि वा विभो .
दीर्घाणि चापि सूक्ष्माणि भवन्ति यस्य पञ्च वा . . 4
text_mt: and whose four are short, or whose seven are red, O lord, / and whose five are long and slender—

sanskrit_iast:
nābhiḥ saṃdhiḥ svanaśceti gambhīrāṇi ca trīṇi vai .
vadanaṃ ca lalāṭaṃ ca dantottama urastathā . . 5
meaning:
नाभिः संधिः स्वनश्चेति गम्भीराणि च त्रीणि वै .
वदनं च ललाटं च दन्तोत्तम उरस्तथा . . 5
text_mt: the navel, the voice, and the joints: these three are deep. / The face, the forehead, excellent teeth, and the chest—

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇametastritayaṃ vīra yasya narasya tu .
sa rājā nātra sandehaḥ śṛṇuṣvevonnatāni ca . . 6
meaning:
विस्तीर्णमेतस्त्रितयं वीर यस्य नरस्य तु .
स राजा नात्र सन्देहः शृणुष्वेवोन्नतानि च . . 6
text_mt: the man for whom these [are] broad, O hero, / is a king, there is no doubt here. And listen indeed to the elevated ones:

sanskrit_iast:
kṛkāṭikā tadhā cāsyaṃ nakhā vakṣo'tha nāsikā .
kakṣe cāpi mahābāho ṣaḍetāni vidurbudhāḥ . . 7
meaning:
कृकाटिका तधा चास्यं नखा वक्षोऽथ नासिका .
कक्षे चापि महाबाहो षडेतानि विदुर्बुधाः . . 7
text_mt: the nape of the neck, and the mouth, the nails, the chest, then the nose, / and also the armpits, O mighty-armed one: the wise know these six [to be elevated].

sanskrit_iast:
liṅgaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ tathā grīvā jaṅghā hrasvāni suvrata .
netrānte hastapādau tu tālvoṣṭhau ca surottama . .
jihvā raktā nakhāścaiva saptaitāni mahāmate . . 8
meaning:
लिङ्गं पृष्ठं तथा ग्रीवा जङ्घा ह्रस्वानि सुव्रत .
नेत्रान्ते हस्तपादौ तु ताल्वोष्ठौ च सुरोत्तम . .
जिह्वा रक्ता नखाश्चैव सप्तैतानि महामते . . 8
text_mt: The penis, back, neck, and shanks should be short, O you of noble vows. / The outer corners of the eyes, hands and feet, palate and lips, O best of gods, / tongue, and nails are red—these seven, O you of great intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
tvacaḥ kararuhāḥ keśā daśanā ṛbhavottama .
sūkṣmāṇyetāni ca guha pañca cāpi vidurbudhāḥ . . 9
meaning:
त्वचः कररुहाः केशा दशना ऋभवोत्तम .
सूक्ष्माण्येतानि च गुह पञ्च चापि विदुर्बुधाः . . 9
text_mt: Skin, nails, hair, and teeth, O best among the gods, / are fine; the wise know these five [to be so], O Guha.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsikālocane bāhū stanayorantaraṃ hanuḥ .
iti dīrghamidaṃ proktaṃ pañcakaṃ bhūbhujāṃ nṛpa . . 1.27.10
meaning:
नासिकालोचने बाहू स्तनयोरन्तरं हनुः .
इति दीर्घमिदं प्रोक्तं पञ्चकं भूभुजां नृप . . 1.27.10
text_mt: Nose, eyes, arms, the space between the breasts, and chin— / this group of five is declared long for monarchs, O prince.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣutaṃ rājñāṃ sakṛddvistrirnāditaṃ hrāditaṃ tathā .
dīrghāyuṣāṃ prayuktaṃ te hasitaṃ ca vidurbudhāḥ . . 11
meaning:
क्षुतं राज्ञां सकृद्द्विस्त्रिर्नादितं ह्रादितं तथा .
दीर्घायुषां प्रयुक्तं ते हसितं च विदुर्बुधाः . . 11
text_mt: The sneeze of kings is once, twice, or thrice, resonant and loud; / and the wise know such laughter as belonging to those of long life.

sanskrit_iast:
padmapatranibhe netre dhanināṃ śivanandana .
bhārgavīmāpnuyātso'pi raktānte yasya locane . . 12
meaning:
पद्मपत्रनिभे नेत्रे धनिनां शिवनन्दन .
भार्गवीमाप्नुयात्सोऽपि रक्तान्ते यस्य लोचने . . 12
text_mt: Eyes resembling lotus petals belong to the wealthy, O son of Śiva; / he also attains Lakṣmī whose eyes have red outer corners.

sanskrit_iast:
madhupiṅgairmahātmāno narā jñeyāḥ surādhipa .
bhīravo hi kṛśākṣāstu caurā maṇḍalacakrakaiḥ . . 13
meaning:
मधुपिङ्गैर्महात्मानो नरा ज्ञेयाः सुराधिप .
भीरवो हि कृशाक्षास्तु चौरा मण्डलचक्रकैः . . 13
text_mt: Men with honey-tawny eyes are to be known as noble-minded, O ruler of gods; / those with small eyes are indeed timid, while thieves have round, circular eyes.

sanskrit_iast:
hayaḥ kekaranetrāstu gambhīrairarthasampadaḥ .
nīlotpalābhairvedavido bhṛśaṃ kṛṣṇaistathārthitā . .
mantritvaṃ sthūlasudṛśo vadanti bhuvi tadvidaḥ . . 14
meaning:
हयः केकरनेत्रास्तु गम्भीरैरर्थसम्पदः .
नीलोत्पलाभैर्वेदविदो भृशं कृष्णैस्तथार्थिता . .
मन्त्रित्वं स्थूलसुदृशो वदन्ति भुवि तद्विदः . . 14
text_mt: Those with squinting eyes are swift as horses, and through deep eyes comes wealth of riches. / With eyes resembling blue water lilies they know the Vedas; through exceedingly black ones, wealth is acquired; / those who know this on earth declare that those with large, fine eyes attain ministership.

sanskrit_iast:
śyāmākṣāḥ subhagā jñeyā dīnākṣaibhra daridratā .
vistīrṇairbhogino śreyā vipulaiśca tathā guha . . 15
meaning:
श्यामाक्षाः सुभगा ज्ञेया दीनाक्षैभ्र दरिद्रता .
विस्तीर्णैर्भोगिनो श्रेया विपुलैश्च तथा गुह . . 15
text_mt: Those with dark eyes are to be known as fortunate; with miserable eyes comes poverty. / Those with broad and large eyes, O Guha, are to be known as enjoyers [of pleasure].

sanskrit_iast:
abhyunnatābhirhrasvāyurviśālābhiḥ sukhī bhavet .
daridro viṣamābhistu tato jñeyaḥ surottama . . 16
meaning:
अभ्युन्नताभिर्ह्रस्वायुर्विशालाभिः सुखी भवेत् .
दरिद्रो विषमाभिस्तु ततो ज्ञेयः सुरोत्तम . . 16
text_mt: With elevated eyebrows one has a short life; with wide ones, one becomes happy. / But with uneven eyebrows, one should then be known as poor, O best of gods.

sanskrit_iast:
bhruvo bālendusadṛśā dhanināmārbhavottama .
dīrghābhirnirdhano jñeyaḥ saṃsaktābhistu suvrata . . 17
meaning:
भ्रुवो बालेन्दुसदृशा धनिनामार्भवोत्तम .
दीर्घाभिर्निर्धनो ज्ञेयः संसक्ताभिस्तु सुव्रत . . 17
text_mt: Eyebrows resembling the crescent moon belong to the wealthy, O best among gods. / With long eyebrows, one should be known as destitute; with joined eyebrows, O you of noble vows,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīṇābhirarthahīnāḥ syurnarā jñeyāḥ surottama .
madhye natabhruvo ye ca paradāraratāstu te . . 18
meaning:
क्षीणाभिरर्थहीनाः स्युर्नरा ज्ञेयाः सुरोत्तम .
मध्ये नतभ्रुवो ये च परदाररतास्तु ते . . 18
text_mt: and with thin eyebrows, men are destitute of wealth, O best of gods. / And those whose eyebrows are bent downward in the middle are devoted to the wives of others.

sanskrit_iast:
viralairunnataiḥ śaṃkhairdhanyāḥ1 syurnātra saṃśayaḥ .
nimnaiḥ stutyarthasaṃsaktā2 unnataiśca janādhipāḥ . . 19
meaning:
विरलैरुन्नतैः शंखैर्धन्याः1 स्युर्नात्र संशयः .
निम्नैः स्तुत्यर्थसंसक्ता2 उन्नतैश्च जनाधिपाः . . 19
text_mt: Those with thin, elevated temples are fortunate, of this there is no doubt. / With sunken temples they are intent upon seeking praise, and with elevated ones they become lords of men.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣamalalāṭā vidhanāḥ sadā syurdevasattama .
ācāryāḥ śuktisadṛśairnarāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 1.27.20
meaning:
विषमललाटा विधनाः सदा स्युर्देवसत्तम .
आचार्याः शुक्तिसदृशैर्नराः स्युर्नात्र संशयः . . 1.27.20
text_mt: Those with uneven foreheads are always destitute, O best of gods. / Men with foreheads resembling oyster shells are teachers, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
unnataśirobhirāḍhyā narā jñeyāḥ sadā guha .
vadhabandhabhāgino vīrā narā ninnalalāṭinaḥ . .
bhṛśamunnataiśca mūrkhāśca kṛpaṇāśca tathā nataiḥ . . 21
meaning:
उन्नतशिरोभिराढ्या नरा ज्ञेयाः सदा गुह .
वधबन्धभागिनो वीरा नरा निन्नललाटिनः . .
भृशमुन्नतैश्च मूर्खाश्च कृपणाश्च तथा नतैः . . 21
text_mt: Men with elevated heads are always to be known as wealthy, O Guha. / Men with sunken foreheads partake of killing and bondage, O hero; / with excessively high foreheads they are fools, and with low ones, wretched.

sanskrit_iast:
śubhāvahaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vadanaṃ syādyathā śṛṇu .
adīnamānanaṃ snigdhaṃ sasmitaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ . . 22
meaning:
शुभावहं मनुष्याणां वदनं स्याद्यथा शृणु .
अदीनमाननं स्निग्धं सस्मितं च विशेषतः . . 22
text_mt: Hear how the face of men brings auspiciousness: / a face that is not downcast, glossy, and especially smiling.

sanskrit_iast:
sāśrudīnaṃ tathā rūkṣamasnigdhaṃ ninditaṃ4 guha .
asambhāvyaṃ mukhaṃ jñeyaṃ narāṇāṃ nagadāraṇa . . 23
meaning:
साश्रुदीनं तथा रूक्षमस्निग्धं निन्दितं4 गुह .
असम्भाव्यं मुखं ज्ञेयं नराणां नगदारण . . 23
text_mt: A face with tears, downcast, rough, and lacklustre is condemned, O Guha; / such a face of men is to be known as wretched, O cleaver of mountains.

sanskrit_iast:
akampaṃ gubhadaṃ jñeyaṃ narāṇāṃ hasitaṃ guha .
nimīlitākṣaṃ pāpasya hasitaṃ cārbhavottama . . 24
meaning:
अकम्पं गुभदं ज्ञेयं नराणां हसितं गुह .
निमीलिताक्षं पापस्य हसितं चार्भवोत्तम . . 24
text_mt: The laughter of men without trembling is to be known as auspicious, O Guha. / And the laughter of a wicked man has closed eyes, O best among gods.

sanskrit_iast:
āmaṇḍalaṃ śiro yasya sa gavāḍhyo naro bhavet .
chatrākṛti śiro yasya sa bhavennṛpatirnaraḥ . . 25
meaning:
आमण्डलं शिरो यस्य स गवाढ्यो नरो भवेत् .
छत्राकृति शिरो यस्य स भवेन्नृपतिर्नरः . . 25
text_mt: A man whose head is rounded becomes rich in cattle. / A man whose head has the shape of a royal parasol becomes a king.

sanskrit_iast:
cipiṭākāritaśirā hanyādvai pitarau naraḥ .
ghaṇṭākṛti śirodhvānamasakṛtsevate naraḥ . .
nimnaṃ śironarthadaṃ syānnarāṇāmarbhavottama . . 26
meaning:
चिपिटाकारितशिरा हन्याद्वै पितरौ नरः .
घण्टाकृति शिरोध्वानमसकृत्सेवते नरः . .
निम्नं शिरोनर्थदं स्यान्नराणामर्भवोत्तम . . 26
text_mt: A man with a flattened head slays his own parents. / A man with a bell-shaped head repeatedly takes to the road. / A sunken head brings misfortune to men, O best among gods.

sanskrit_iast:
guḍaiḥ snigdhaistathā kṛṣṇairabhinnāgraistathaiva hi .
keśairna cātibahulairmṛdubhiḥ pārthivo bhavet . . 27
meaning:
गुडैः स्निग्धैस्तथा कृष्णैरभिन्नाग्रैस्तथैव हि .
केशैर्न चातिबहुलैर्मृदुभिः पार्थिवो भवेत् . . 27
text_mt: With hair that is curled, glossy, black, not split at the ends, / not overly thick, and soft, one becomes a king.

sanskrit_iast:
bahulāḥ kapilāḥ sthūlā viṣamāḥ sphuṭitāstathā .
paruṣā hrasvātikuṭilā daridrāṇāṃ kacāḥ ghanāḥ . . 28
meaning:
बहुलाः कपिलाः स्थूला विषमाः स्फुटितास्तथा .
परुषा ह्रस्वातिकुटिला दरिद्राणां कचाः घनाः . . 28
text_mt: Hair that is thick, tawny, coarse, uneven, split, / rough, short, excessively curly, and dense belongs to the poor.

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ śubhaṃ vāśubhameva ca .
yoṣitāṃ tadidānīṃ te lakṣaṇaṃ vacmi bhīmaja . . 29
strīlakṣaṇavarṇanam
meaning:
इत्युक्तं लक्षणं नॄणां शुभं वाशुभमेव च .
योषितां तदिदानीं ते लक्षणं वच्मि भीमज . . 29
स्त्रीलक्षणवर्णनम्
text_mt:
Thus has been spoken the auspicious and inauspicious bodily sign of men. / Now I will tell you the bodily sign of women, O son of Bhīma.
Description of the Bodily Signs of Women

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
śṛṇvidānīṃ mahābāho strīlakṣaṇamanuttamam .
yanmayoktaṃ purā vīra nāradasya mahātmanaḥ . . 1
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृण्विदानीं महाबाहो स्त्रीलक्षणमनुत्तमम् .
यन्मयोक्तं पुरा वीर नारदस्य महात्मनः . . 1
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Hear now, O mighty-armed hero, the unsurpassed bodily signs of women, / which was spoken by me of old to the great-souled Nārada,
title: adhyāyaḥ 028

sanskrit_iast:
tattvaṃ vijñāyate yena śubhāśubhamavasthitam .
ninditaṃ ca praśastaṃ ca strīṇāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam . . 2
meaning:
तत्त्वं विज्ञायते येन शुभाशुभमवस्थितम् .
निन्दितं च प्रशस्तं च स्त्रीणां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् . . 2
text_mt: by which the true nature, resting in the auspicious and inauspicious, is understood. / I shall declare the condemned and the praiseworthy bodily signs of women.

sanskrit_iast:
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva bhrātaraṃ mātulaṃ tathā .
dvau tu bimbau parīkṣeta samudrasya vaco yathā . . 3
meaning:
मातरं पितरं चैव भ्रातरं मातुलं तथा .
द्वौ तु बिम्बौ परीक्षेत समुद्रस्य वचो यथा . . 3
text_mt: One should examine the mother, the father, the brother, and the maternal uncle— / the two lineages, according to the word of Samudra.

sanskrit_iast:
muhūrte tithisampanne nakṣatre cābhipūjite .
dvijaistu saha vāgamya kanyāṃ vīkṣeta śāstravit . . 4
meaning:
मुहूर्ते तिथिसम्पन्ने नक्षत्रे चाभिपूजिते .
द्विजैस्तु सह वागम्य कन्यां वीक्षेत शास्त्रवित् . . 4
text_mt: At an auspicious hour, on an auspicious lunar day, under a revered constellation, / coming together with Brahmins, one skilled in the scriptures should examine the maiden.

sanskrit_iast:
hastau pādau parīkṣeta aṅgulīrnakhameva ca .
1pāṇimeva ca jaṅghe ca kaṭināsoru eva ca . . 5
meaning:
हस्तौ पादौ परीक्षेत अङ्गुलीर्नखमेव च .
1पाणिमेव च जङ्घे च कटिनासोरु एव च . . 5
text_mt: One should examine the hands, feet, fingers, and nails, / the palms, shanks, hips, and thighs,

sanskrit_iast:
jaghanodarapṛṣṭhaṃ ca stanau karṇau bhujau tathā .
jihvāṃ coṣṭhau ca dantāśca kapolaṃ galakaṃ tathā . . 6
meaning:
जघनोदरपृष्ठं च स्तनौ कर्णौ भुजौ तथा .
जिह्वां चोष्ठौ च दन्ताश्च कपोलं गलकं तथा . . 6
text_mt: the buttocks, belly, back, breasts, ears, and arms, / the tongue, lips, teeth, cheeks, and neck,

sanskrit_iast:
cakṣurnāsā lalāṭaṃ ca śiraḥ keśāṃstathaiva ca .
romarājiṃ1 svaraṃ varṇamāvartāni tu vā punaḥ . . 7
meaning:
चक्षुर्नासा ललाटं च शिरः केशांस्तथैव च .
रोमराजिं1 स्वरं वर्णमावर्तानि तु वा पुनः . . 7
text_mt: the eyes, nose, forehead, head, and hair, / the line of hair [on the abdomen], voice, complexion, and the whorls of hair.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāstu rekhāgrīvāyāṃ yā2 ca raktāntalocanā .
yasya sā gṛhamāgacchettadgṛhaṃ sukhamedhate . . 8
meaning:
यस्यास्तु रेखाग्रीवायां या2 च रक्तान्तलोचना .
यस्य सा गृहमागच्छेत्तद्गृहं सुखमेधते . . 8
text_mt: She on whose neck there are lines and whose eyes have red outer corners, / into whose house she enters, that house flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
lalāṭe dṛśyate yasyāstriśūlaṃ devanirmitam .
bahūnāṃ strīsahasrāṇāṃ svāminīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet . . 9
meaning:
ललाटे दृश्यते यस्यास्त्रिशूलं देवनिर्मितम् .
बहूनां स्त्रीसहस्राणां स्वामिनीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् . . 9
text_mt: She on whose forehead is seen a trident fashioned by the gods, / one should designate her as the mistress of many thousands of women.

sanskrit_iast:
rājahaṃsagatiryasyā mṛgākṣī mṛgavarṇikā .
samaśuklāgradantā ca kanyāṃ tāmuttamāṃ viduḥ . . 1.28.10
meaning:
राजहंसगतिर्यस्या मृगाक्षी मृगवर्णिका .
समशुक्लाग्रदन्ता च कन्यां तामुत्तमां विदुः . . 1.28.10
text_mt: She whose gait is like that of a royal swan, deer-eyed, having the complexion of a deer, / and with even teeth with white tips—they know such a maiden to be the best.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍūkakukṣī yā kanyā nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalā .
ekaṃ janayate putraṃ so'pi rājā bhaviṣyati . . 11
meaning:
मण्डूककुक्षी या कन्या न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डला .
एकं जनयते पुत्रं सोऽपि राजा भविष्यति . . 11
text_mt: A maiden whose belly is like that of a frog and whose proportions are like a banyan tree / gives birth to a single son, and he too will become a king.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsasvarā mṛduvacā yā kanyā madhupiṅgalā .
aṣṭau janayate putrāndhanadhānyavivardhinī . . 12
meaning:
हंसस्वरा मृदुवचा या कन्या मधुपिङ्गला .
अष्टौ जनयते पुत्रान्धनधान्यविवर्धिनी . . 12
text_mt: A maiden with a swan-like voice, gentle words, and honey-tawny [eyes], / brings increase of wealth and grain, and gives birth to eight sons.

sanskrit_iast:
āyatau śravaṇau yasyāḥ surūpā cāpi nāsikā .
bhruvau cendrāyudhākārau sātyantaṃ sukhabhāginī . . 13
meaning:
आयतौ श्रवणौ यस्याः सुरूपा चापि नासिका .
भ्रुवौ चेन्द्रायुधाकारौ सात्यन्तं सुखभागिनी . . 13
text_mt: She whose ears are long, whose nose is well-formed, / and whose eyebrows are shaped like Indra's bow partakes of supreme happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
tanvī śyāmā tathā kṛṣṇā snigdhāṅgī mṛdubhāṣiṇī .
śaṅkhakundendudaśanā bhavedaiśvaryabhāginī . . 14
meaning:
तन्वी श्यामा तथा कृष्णा स्निग्धाङ्गी मृदुभाषिणी .
शङ्खकुन्देन्दुदशना भवेदैश्वर्यभागिनी . . 14
text_mt: Slender, fair-complexioned or dark, with glossy limbs, speaking gently, / with teeth like a conch, jasmine, or the moon, she becomes a possessor of sovereignty.

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyā vedimadhyā tu yā bhavet .
āyate vipule netre rājapatnī tu sā bhavet . . 15
meaning:
विस्तीर्णं जघनं यस्या वेदिमध्या तु या भवेत् .
आयते विपुले नेत्रे राजपत्नी तु सा भवेत् . . 15
text_mt: She whose hips are broad, whose waist is like an altar, / and whose eyes are long and wide becomes the wife of a king.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāḥ payodhare vāme hastekarṇe gale'pi vā .
maśakaṃ tilakaṃ vāpi sā pūrvaṃ janayetsutam . . 16
meaning:
यस्याः पयोधरे वामे हस्तेकर्णे गलेऽपि वा .
मशकं तिलकं वापि सा पूर्वं जनयेत्सुतम् . . 16
text_mt: She on whose left breast, hand, ear, or throat / there is a mole or a birthmark gives birth to a son first.

sanskrit_iast:
gūḍhagulphāṅguliśirā alpapārṣṇiḥ sumadhyamā .
raktākṣī raktacaraṇā sātyantaṃ sukhabhāginī . . 17
meaning:
गूढगुल्फाङ्गुलिशिरा अल्पपार्ष्णिः सुमध्यमा .
रक्ताक्षी रक्तचरणा सात्यन्तं सुखभागिनी . . 17
text_mt: With ankles and veins of the fingers hidden, small heels, a slender waist, / red corners of the eyes, and red feet, she partakes of supreme happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
kūrmapṛṣṭhāyatanakhau snigdhabhāvavivarjitau .
vakrāṅgulitalau pādau kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet . . 18
meaning:
कूर्मपृष्ठायतनखौ स्निग्धभावविवर्जितौ .
वक्राङ्गुलितलौ पादौ कन्यां तां परिवर्जयेत् . . 18
text_mt: With nails long like a tortoise's shell, devoid of glossiness, / and feet with crooked toes and soles—such a maiden one should avoid.

sanskrit_iast:
yena kenacidaṃśena māṃsaṃ yasyā vivardhate .
rāsabhīṃ tādṛśīṃ vidyānna sā kalyāṇamarhati . . 19
meaning:
येन केनचिदंशेन मांसं यस्या विवर्धते .
रासभीं तादृशीं विद्यान्न सा कल्याणमर्हति . . 19
text_mt: She in whom flesh increases disproportionately in any part, / one should know her to be like a she-ass; she is not worthy of good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
pāde pradeśinī yasyā aṅguṣṭhaṃ samatikramet .
duḥśīlā durbhagā jñeyā kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet . . 1.28.20
meaning:
पादे प्रदेशिनी यस्या अङ्गुष्ठं समतिक्रमेत् .
दुःशीला दुर्भगा ज्ञेया कन्यां तां परिवर्जयेत् . . 1.28.20
text_mt: She whose second toe surpasses the big toe on her foot / is to be known as ill-behaved and unfortunate; one should avoid such a maiden.

sanskrit_iast:
pāde madhyamikā yasyāḥ kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi .
ramate sā na kaumāre svacchandā1 kāmacāriṇī . . 21
meaning:
पादे मध्यमिका यस्याः क्षितिं न स्पृशते यदि .
रमते सा न कौमारे स्वच्छन्दा1 कामचारिणी . . 21
text_mt: If the middle toe of her foot does not touch the ground, / she does not delight in marriage, being self-willed and promiscuous.

sanskrit_iast:
pāde anāmikā yasyāḥ kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi .
dvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ hatvā tṛtīye sā pratiṣṭhitā . . 22
meaning:
पादे अनामिका यस्याः क्षितिं न स्पृशते यदि .
द्वितीयं पुरुषं हत्वा तृतीये सा प्रतिष्ठिता . . 22
text_mt: If the ring toe of her foot does not touch the ground, / having killed a second husband she is established with a third.

sanskrit_iast:
pāde kaniṣṭhā yasyāstu kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi .
dvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ hatvā tṛtīye sā pratiṣṭhitā . . 23
meaning:
पादे कनिष्ठा यस्यास्तु क्षितिं न स्पृशते यदि .
द्वितीयं पुरुषं हत्वा तृतीये सा प्रतिष्ठिता . . 23
text_mt: If the little toe of her foot does not touch the ground, / having killed a second husband she is established with a third.

sanskrit_iast:
na devikā na dhanikā na dhānyapratināmikā .
gulmavṛkṣasanāmnī ca kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet . . 24
meaning:
न देविका न धनिका न धान्यप्रतिनामिका .
गुल्मवृक्षसनाम्नी च कन्यां तां परिवर्जयेत् . . 24
text_mt: Neither [named] Devikā, nor Dhanikā, nor bearing a name corresponding to grain, / nor having the name of a shrub or tree: one should avoid such a maiden.

sanskrit_iast:
indracandrādipuruṣasanāmnī ca yadā bhavet .
naitāḥ patiṣu rajyante yāśca nakṣatranāmikāḥ . . 25
meaning:
इन्द्रचन्द्रादिपुरुषसनाम्नी च यदा भवेत् .
नैताः पतिषु रज्यन्ते याश्च नक्षत्रनामिकाः . . 25
text_mt: And when she has the name of a male such as Indra or Candra, / these do not find pleasure in husbands, nor those named after lunar mansions.

sanskrit_iast:
āvartaḥ pṛṣṭhato yasyā nābhiṃ samanuvindati .
tadapatyaṃ bhaved dhrasvaṃ hrasvāyuśca vinirdiśet . . 26
meaning:
आवर्तः पृष्ठतो यस्या नाभिं समनुविन्दति .
तदपत्यं भवेद् ध्रस्वं ह्रस्वायुश्च विनिर्दिशेत् . . 26
text_mt: She whose hair-whorl on the back matches that on her navel, / her offspring will be short, and one should predict a short life for it.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣṭhāvartā patiṃ hanti nābhyāvartā pativratā .
kaṭyāvartā tu svacchandā na kadācidvirajyate . . 27
meaning:
पृष्ठावर्ता पतिं हन्ति नाभ्यावर्ता पतिव्रता .
कट्यावर्ता तु स्वच्छन्दा न कदाचिद्विरज्यते . . 27
text_mt: A woman with a whorl on her back slays her husband; a woman with a whorl on her navel is devoted to her husband; / a woman with a whorl on her waist is self-willed and never falls out of love.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāstu hasamānāyā gaṇḍe jāyet kūpakam .
ramate sā na kaumāre svacchandā kāryakāriṇī . . 28
meaning:
यस्यास्तु हसमानाया गण्डे जायेत् कूपकम् .
रमते सा न कौमारे स्वच्छन्दा कार्यकारिणी . . 28
text_mt: She on whose cheek a dimple appears when laughing / does not delight in marriage, being self-willed and doing as she pleases.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāstu gacchamānāyāṣṭiṭṭīkāyati jaṅghikā .
putraṃ vyavasyetsā kartuṃ patitve nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 29
meaning:
यस्यास्तु गच्छमानायाष्टिट्टीकायति जङ्घिका .
पुत्रं व्यवस्येत्सा कर्तुं पतित्वे नात्र संशयः . . 29
text_mt: She whose calf makes a tiṭ-tiṭ sound while walking / will undertake to make a son in the place of a husband; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlapādā ca yā kanyā sarvāṃgeṣu ca lomaśā .
sthūlahastā ca yā syādvai dāsīṃ tāṃ nirdiśedbudhaḥ . . 1.28.30
meaning:
स्थूलपादा च या कन्या सर्वांगेषु च लोमशा .
स्थूलहस्ता च या स्याद्वै दासीं तां निर्दिशेद्बुधः . . 1.28.30
text_mt: And the maiden who has thick feet, is hairy on all her limbs, / and has thick hands, the wise man should designate as a female servant.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāścotkaṭakau2 pādau mukhaṃ ca vikṛtaṃ bhavet .
uttaroṣṭhe ca romāṇi sā kṣipraṃ bhakṣayetpatim . . 31
meaning:
यस्याश्चोत्कटकौ2 पादौ मुखं च विकृतं भवेत् .
उत्तरोष्ठे च रोमाणि सा क्षिप्रं भक्षयेत्पतिम् . . 31
text_mt: And she whose feet are high-arched, whose face is deformed, / and who has hair on her upper lip, will quickly devour her husband.

sanskrit_iast:
trīṇi yasyāḥ pralambante lalāṭamudaraṃ sphicau .
trīṇi bhakṣayate sā tu devaraṃ śvasuraṃ patim . . 32
meaning:
त्रीणि यस्याः प्रलम्बन्ते ललाटमुदरं स्फिचौ .
त्रीणि भक्षयते सा तु देवरं श्वसुरं पतिम् . . 32
text_mt: She whose three—forehead, belly, and buttocks—hang down, / she indeed devours three: husband's brother, father-in-law, and husband.

sanskrit_iast:
samudbhūṣitacāritrā gurubhaktā pativratā .
devabrāhmaṇabhaktā ca mānuṣīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..3 3
nityaṃ snātā sugandhā ca nityaṃ ca priyavādinī .
alpāśinyalparoṣā ca devatāṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet .. 34
meaning:
समुद्भूषितचारित्रा गुरुभक्ता पतिव्रता .
देवब्राह्मणभक्ता च मानुषीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..3 3
नित्यं स्नाता सुगन्धा च नित्यं च प्रियवादिनी .
अल्पाशिन्यल्परोषा च देवतां तां विनिर्दिशेत् .. 34
text_mt: Adorned with good conduct, devoted to elders, devoted to her husband, / and devoted to gods and Brahmins: one should designate her as human. / Constantly bathed, sweet-smelling, constantly speaking affectionately, / eating little, and bearing little anger: one should designate her as divine.

sanskrit_iast:
pracchannaṃ kurute pāpamapavādaṃ ca rakṣati .
hadayaṃ syācca durgrāhyaṃ mārjārī tāṃ vinirdiśet ..35
meaning:
प्रच्छन्नं कुरुते पापमपवादं च रक्षति .
हदयं स्याच्च दुर्ग्राह्यं मार्जारी तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..35
text_mt: She does evil secretly, yet guards against reproach; / her heart is hard to grasp: one should designate her as feline.

sanskrit_iast:
hasate krīḍate caiva kruddhā caiva prasīdati .
nīceṣu ramate nityaṃ rāsabhī tāṃ vinirdiśet .. 36
meaning:
हसते क्रीडते चैव क्रुद्धा चैव प्रसीदति .
नीचेषु रमते नित्यं रासभी तां विनिर्दिशेत् .. 36
text_mt: She laughs and plays, and even when angered she becomes pleased; / she constantly delights in base men: one should designate her as a she-ass.

sanskrit_iast:
pratikūlakarī nityaṃ bandhūnāṃ bhartureva ca .
svacchande lalitāṃ caiva āsurīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..37
meaning:
प्रतिकूलकरी नित्यं बन्धूनां भर्तुरेव च .
स्वच्छन्दे ललितां चैव आसुरीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..37
text_mt: Constantly causing hostility to relatives and to her husband, / and taking pleasure in self-willed ways: one should designate her as demonic.

sanskrit_iast:
1bahvāśī bahuvākyā ca nityaṃ cāpriyavādinī .
hinasti svapatiṃ yā tu rākṣasīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet .. 38
meaning:
1बह्वाशी बहुवाक्या च नित्यं चाप्रियवादिनी .
हिनस्ति स्वपतिं या तु राक्षसीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् .. 38
text_mt: Eating much, speaking much, and constantly speaking unkindly, / she who harms her own husband: one should designate her as a rākṣasī.

sanskrit_iast:
śaucācāraparibhraṣṭā rūpabhraṣṭā bhayaṅkarā .
prasvedamalapaṅkā ca piśācīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..39
meaning:
शौचाचारपरिभ्रष्टा रूपभ्रष्टा भयङ्करा .
प्रस्वेदमलपङ्का च पिशाचीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..39
text_mt: Fallen from purity and good conduct, ruined in beauty, terrifying, / and covered with the mire of sweat and dirt: one should designate her as a piśācī.

sanskrit_iast:
nityaṃ snātāṃ sugandhāṃ ca māṃsamadyapriyādinīm .
vṛkṣodyānaprasaktā ca gāndharvīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..1.28.40
meaning:
नित्यं स्नातां सुगन्धां च मांसमद्यप्रियादिनीम् .
वृक्षोद्यानप्रसक्ता च गान्धर्वीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..1.28.40
text_mt: Constantly bathed and sweet-smelling, fond of meat and wine, / and attached to trees and pleasure-gardens: one should designate her as a gāndharvī.

sanskrit_iast:
capalā cañcalā caiva nityaṃ paśyeddiśastathā .
calasvabhāvā lubdhā ca vānarīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..4 1
candrānanāṃ śubhāṅgīṃ tu mattavāraṇagāminīm .
āraktanakhahastāṃ tu vidyādvidyādharīṃ budhaḥ ..42
meaning:
चपला चञ्चला चैव नित्यं पश्येद्दिशस्तथा .
चलस्वभावा लुब्धा च वानरीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..4 1
चन्द्राननां शुभाङ्गीं तु मत्तवारणगामिनीम् .
आरक्तनखहस्तां तु विद्याद्विद्याधरीं बुधः ..42
text_mt: Fickle and unsteady, constantly gazing at the directions, / of an unsteady nature, and greedy: one should designate her as a female monkey. / Moon-faced, with auspicious limbs, walking like an elephant in rut, / and with slightly red nails and hands: the wise man should know her as a vidyādharī.

sanskrit_iast:
vīṇāvāditraśabdena vaṃśagītaraveṇa ca .
puṣpadhūpaprasaktāṃ ca gāndharvīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet ..43
meaning:
वीणावादित्रशब्देन वंशगीतरवेण च .
पुष्पधूपप्रसक्तां च गान्धर्वीं तां विनिर्दिशेत् ..43
text_mt: Fond of the sound of lute and musical instruments, the noise of flute and song, / and fond of flowers and incense: one should designate her as a gāndharvī.

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
ityevamuktvā sa mahānubhāvo jagāma vedhā nijamandiraṃ vai .
strīṇāṃ tathā puṃstvavatāṃ ca vīra yallakṣaṇaṃ pārthiva lokapūjyam . . 44
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthī kalpe
strīlakṣaṇavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 28 .
gaṇapatikalpavarṇanam
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स महानुभावो जगाम वेधा निजमन्दिरं वै .
स्त्रीणां तथा पुंस्त्ववतां च वीर यल्लक्षणं पार्थिव लोकपूज्यम् . . 44
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थी कल्पे
स्त्रीलक्षणवर्णनं नामाष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः . 28 .
गणपतिकल्पवर्णनम्
text_mt:
Sumantu said: / Having spoken thus, O king, that exalted Creator indeed went to his own abode; / such is the characteristic, worshipped by the world, of women and of men, O hero.
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, called 'Description of the Characteristics of Women', in the Fourth Period of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, an exposition of fifty-thousand verses.
Description of the ritual procedure for Gaṇapati

sanskrit_iast:
śatānīka uvāca
gakārākṣaradevasya gaṇeśasya mahātmanaḥ .
ārādhanavidhiṃ brūhi sāṅgaṃ mantrasamanvitam . . 1
meaning:
शतानीक उवाच
गकाराक्षरदेवस्य गणेशस्य महात्मनः .
आराधनविधिं ब्रूहि साङ्गं मन्त्रसमन्वितम् . . 1
text_mt: Śatānīka said: / Speak of the rite of worship, complete with limbs and accompanied by mantras, / of the great-souled Gaṇeśa, the deity of the letter 'ga'.
title: Gaṇapatikalpavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
na tithirna ca nakṣatraṃ nopavāso vidhīyate .
yatheṣṭaṃ1 ceṣṭataḥ siddhiḥ sadā bhavati kāmikā . . 2
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
न तिथिर्न च नक्षत्रं नोपवासो विधीयते .
यथेष्टं1 चेष्टतः सिद्धिः सदा भवति कामिका . . 2
text_mt: Sumantu said: / Neither a lunar day nor a lunar mansion nor fasting is prescribed; / through effort according to one's desire, desired success always comes about.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetārkamūlaṃ saṅgṛhya kuryādgaṇapatiṃ budhaḥ .
aṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ tu padmāsanagataṃ tathā . . 3
meaning:
श्वेतार्कमूलं सङ्गृह्य कुर्याद्गणपतिं बुधः .
अङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं तु पद्मासनगतं तथा . . 3
text_mt: Taking the root of the white arka plant, the wise man should fashion Gaṇapati, / merely the size of the thumb's joint, seated upon a lotus seat,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhujaṃ trinetraṃ ca sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam .
nāgayajñopavītāṅgaṃ śaśāṅkakṛtaśekharam . . 4
meaning:
चतुर्भुजं त्रिनेत्रं च सर्वाभरणभूषितम् .
नागयज्ञोपवीताङ्गं शशाङ्ककृतशेखरम् . . 4
text_mt: having four arms, three eyes, adorned with all ornaments, / his body possessing the sacred thread of a serpent, crested with the moon.

sanskrit_iast:
dantaṃ savye kare dadyāddvitīye cākṣasūtrakam .
tṛtīye paraśuṃ dadyāccaturthe modakaṃ nyaset . . 5
meaning:
दन्तं सव्ये करे दद्याद्द्वितीये चाक्षसूत्रकम् .
तृतीये परशुं दद्याच्चतुर्थे मोदकं न्यसेत् . . 5
text_mt: He should place the tusk in the right hand, and the rosary in the second; / in the third he should place the axe, and in the fourth he should set the modaka.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṅkumaṃ candanaṃ cāpi samālambhanamucyate .
vāsobhirbhūṣaṇai raktairmālyaiścārādhayedgaṇam . . 6
meaning:
कुङ्कुमं चन्दनं चापि समालम्भनमुच्यते .
वासोभिर्भूषणै रक्तैर्माल्यैश्चाराधयेद्गणम् . . 6
text_mt: Saffron and sandalwood paste are spoken of as the unguent; / one should worship Gaṇa with garments, red ornaments, and garlands,

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpena ca sugandhena modakaiścāpi pūjayet .
evaṃ pūjyāgratastasya bhojayedbrāhmaṇaṃ budhaḥ . . 7
meaning:
धूपेन च सुगन्धेन मोदकैश्चापि पूजयेत् .
एवं पूज्याग्रतस्तस्य भोजयेद्ब्राह्मणं बुधः . . 7
text_mt: and with fragrant incense, and one should also worship him with modakas. / Having worshipped thus, before him the wise man should feed a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmanaṃ kubjakaṃ cāpi bhojayetpurato dvijam .
āśīrvādaṃ tatastasmātprāpya siddhimavāpnuyāt . . 8
meaning:
वामनं कुब्जकं चापि भोजयेत्पुरतो द्विजम् .
आशीर्वादं ततस्तस्मात्प्राप्य सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् . . 8
text_mt: He should also feed a dwarf and a hunchbacked twice-born man before him; / then, receiving a blessing from him, he will attain success.

sanskrit_iast:
bhaktyā kurukulaśreṣṭha 1śṛṇu mantrapadāni vai .
gaṃ svāhā mūlamantro'yaṃ praṇavena samanvitaḥ . . 9
meaning:
भक्त्या कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ 1शृणु मन्त्रपदानि वै .
गं स्वाहा मूलमन्त्रोऽयं प्रणवेन समन्वितः . . 9
text_mt: With devotion, O best of the Kuru lineage, listen to the words of the mantras: / 'Gaṃ svāhā' is this root mantra, accompanied by the praṇava.

sanskrit_iast:
gāṃ namo hadayaṃ jñeyaṃ gīṃ śiraḥ parikīrtitam .
śikhā ca gūṃ namo jñeyo gaiṃ namaḥ kavacaṃ smṛtam . . 1.29.10
meaning:
गां नमो हदयं ज्ञेयं गीं शिरः परिकीर्तितम् .
शिखा च गूं नमो ज्ञेयो गैं नमः कवचं स्मृतम् . . 1.29.10
text_mt: 'Gāṃ namaḥ' is to be known as the heart; 'gīṃ' is proclaimed as the head; / the crest is to be known as 'gūṃ namaḥ'; 'gaiṃ namaḥ' is held to be the armour;

sanskrit_iast:
gauṃ namo netramuddiṣṭaṃ gaḥ phaṭ kāmāstramucyate .
āgaccholkāmukhāyeti mantra āvāhane hyayam . . 11
meaning:
गौं नमो नेत्रमुद्दिष्टं गः फट् कामास्त्रमुच्यते .
आगच्छोल्कामुखायेति मन्त्र आवाहने ह्ययम् . . 11
text_mt: 'Gauṃ namaḥ' is declared as the eye; 'gaḥ phaṭ' is spoken of as the desire-weapon; / and this mantra, 'Come, O you whose face is a meteor!', is for the invocation.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṃ gaṇeśāya namo gandhamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
puṣpolkāya namaḥ puṣpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ . . 12
meaning:
गं गणेशाय नमो गन्धमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः .
पुष्पोल्काय नमः पुष्पमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः . . 12
text_mt: 'Gaṃ, homage to Gaṇeśa' is proclaimed as the incense/fragrance mantra; / 'Homage to Puṣpolka' is proclaimed as this flower mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpolkāya namo dhūpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ .
dīpolkāya namo dīpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ . . 13
meaning:
धूपोल्काय नमो धूपमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः .
दीपोल्काय नमो दीपमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः . . 13
text_mt: 'Homage to Dhūpolka' is proclaimed as this incense mantra; / 'Homage to Dīpolka' is proclaimed as this lamp mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ gaṃ maholkāya namo balimantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
oṃ saṃsiddholkāya namo mantraścāyaṃ visarjane . . 14
meaning:
ओं गं महोल्काय नमो बलिमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः .
ओं संसिद्धोल्काय नमो मन्त्रश्चायं विसर्जने . . 14
text_mt: 'Oṃ gaṃ, homage to Maholka' is proclaimed as the offering mantra; / and this mantra, 'Oṃ, homage to Saṃsiddholka', is used in dismissal.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ mahākarṇāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi .
tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt gāyatrī japaḥ pūrvataḥ . . 15
meaning:
ओं महाकर्णाय विद्महे वक्रतुण्डाय धीमहि .
तन्नो दन्तिः प्रचोदयात् गायत्री जपः पूर्वतः . . 15
text_mt: 'Oṃ, we know the large-eared one; we meditate upon the one with the curved trunk; / may that tusker inspire us': this Gāyatrī is the recitation in the east.

sanskrit_iast:
mahāgaṇapataye vīra1 svāhā dakṣiṇataḥ sadā .
maholkāya paścimataḥ kūśmāṇḍāyottareṇa tu . .
ekadantatripurāntakāya āgneyyāṃ vīra nirdiśet . . 16
meaning:
महागणपतये वीर1 स्वाहा दक्षिणतः सदा .
महोल्काय पश्चिमतः कूश्माण्डायोत्तरेण तु . .
एकदन्तत्रिपुरान्तकाय आग्नेय्यां वीर निर्दिशेत् . . 16
text_mt: 'To Mahāgaṇapati, svāhā', O hero, always in the south; / 'To Maholka' in the west; and 'To Kūśmāṇḍa' in the north; / 'To the one-tusked destroyer of Tripura' one should designate in the southeast, O hero.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ śivadatta vikaṭaharahāsa prāṇāya svā nairṛtyām .
2tulambanātyacaladantakāya svāhā vāyavyām . . 17
meaning:
ओं शिवदत्त विकटहरहास प्राणाय स्वा नैरृत्याम् .
2तुलम्बनात्यचलदन्तकाय स्वाहा वायव्याम् . . 17
text_mt: 'Oṃ, O Śivadatta, whose laugh is the dread laughter of Hara, svāhā to the breath' in the southwest; / 'To the one with suspended, unmoving teeth, svāhā' in the northwest.

sanskrit_iast:
padmadaṃṣṭrāya narāyeti aiśānyāṃ homayedbudhaḥ .
huṃ phaṭ hum̐ phaṭ hastatāladhvanirhasanakūrdanaḥ . . 18
meaning:
पद्मदंष्ट्राय नरायेति ऐशान्यां होमयेद्बुधः .
हुं फट् हुम्̐ फट् हस्ततालध्वनिर्हसनकूर्दनः . . 18
text_mt:
In the north-east, the wise man should offer oblations with: 'To Padmadaṃṣṭra, to Nara, svāhā.'
With clapping of hands uttering 'huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ', laughing and leaping,

sanskrit_iast:
mṛdanartanagaṇapatirdevasya mudrāṃ tato homaṃ samācaret .
na yadā vaśyā bhavati . .
kṛṣṇatilāhutimaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāttrirātreṇa rājā vaśyo bhavati . . 19
meaning:
मृदनर्तनगणपतिर्देवस्य मुद्रां ततो होमं समाचरेत् .
न यदा वश्या भवति . .
कृष्णतिलाहुतिमष्टसहस्रं जुहुयात्त्रिरात्रेण राजा वश्यो भवति . . 19
text_mt:
[and] the hand gesture of the god Gaṇapati, dancer of the mṛdaṅga, he should then perform the homa.
When [a person] is not subdued,
one should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame seeds; within three nights the king becomes subdued.

sanskrit_iast:
tilayavahomena sarve janapadā vaśyā bhavanti .
ati rūpavatī kanyā gacchantamanu(?)cchati . . 1.29.20
meaning:
तिलयवहोमेन सर्वे जनपदा वश्या भवन्ति .
अति रूपवती कन्या गच्छन्तमनु(?)च्छति . . 1.29.20
text_mt:
Through homa of sesame seeds and barley, all subjects of the realm become subdued.
An exceedingly beautiful maiden pursues [him] as he walks.

sanskrit_iast:
caṇatandulahomenājito bhavet .
nimbapatrasamaistailairvidveṣaṇaṃ karoti . .
somagrahaṇe udakamadhye avatīrya aṣṭasahasraṃ japet .
saṅgrāme aparājito bhavati . . 21
meaning:
चणतन्दुलहोमेनाजितो भवेत् .
निम्बपत्रसमैस्तैलैर्विद्वेषणं करोति . .
सोमग्रहणे उदकमध्ये अवतीर्य अष्टसहस्रं जपेत् .
सङ्ग्रामे अपराजितो भवति . . 21
text_mt:
Through homa of chickpeas and rice grains, he becomes invincible.
With oils mixed equally with nimba leaves, he causes enmity.
Descending into water during a lunar eclipse, he should mutter [the mantra] eight thousand times;
he becomes undefeated in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
( oṃ lambarājñe namaḥ .)
ādityābhimukho bhūtvā aṣṭasahasraṃ japet .
ādityo varado bhavati . . 22
meaning:
( ओं लम्बराज्ञे नमः .)
आदित्याभिमुखो भूत्वा अष्टसहस्रं जपेत् .
आदित्यो वरदो भवति . . 22

sanskrit_iast:
śuklacaturthyāmupoṣya gandhapuṣpādibhirarcanaṃ kṛtvā tilatandulāñjuhuyāt .
śirasā dhārayaṃstairaparājito bhavati . . 23
meaning:
शुक्लचतुर्थ्यामुपोष्य गन्धपुष्पादिभिरर्चनं कृत्वा तिलतन्दुलाञ्जुहुयात् .
शिरसा धारयंस्तैरपराजितो भवति . . 23
text_mt:
Having fasted on the fourth day of the bright fortnight and worshipped with perfumes, flowers, and the like, he should offer sesame seeds and rice grains.
Bearing them on his head, he becomes undefeated by them.

sanskrit_iast:
apāmārgasamidbhiragniṃ prajvālya ekaviṃśatyāhutīryo juhuyāt .
trirātrācchatruṃ vyāpādayati . . 24
meaning:
अपामार्गसमिद्भिरग्निं प्रज्वाल्य एकविंशत्याहुतीर्यो जुहुयात् .
त्रिरात्राच्छत्रुं व्यापादयति . . 24
text_mt:
Having kindled the fire with kindling sticks of apāmārga, he who offers twenty-one oblations
kills his enemy within three nights.

sanskrit_iast:
athottareṇa mantraṃ vyākhyāsye .
vṛkṣamūle kajjalaṃ saṅgṛhya saptabhirmantritaṃ kṛtvā netrāṇyañjayedyaṃ paśyati sa vaśī bhavati . . 25
meaning:
अथोत्तरेण मन्त्रं व्याख्यास्ये .
वृक्षमूले कज्जलं सङ्गृह्य सप्तभिर्मन्त्रितं कृत्वा नेत्राण्यञ्जयेद्यं पश्यति स वशी भवति . . 25
text_mt:
Now I shall explain the subsequent mantra:
Gathering collyrium at the root of a tree, empowering it seven times [with the mantra], one should anoint one's eyes; whomever he beholds becomes subjugated.

Sumantu said:
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati made of neem wood the size of a thumb-joint, worshipped [him] daily with incense, perfume, and the like, and bound [him] concealed on one's head, one should go forth.
He becomes dear to all people. Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb from white arka root and worshipped [him] with incense and the like, he brings all castes under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb from white sandalwood, worshipped [him] with flowers, perfume, and the like, and made an offering on the bright fourth or eighth [lunar day], he should offer eight thousand oblations with curd and milk-rice; he brings the king under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb made of red sandalwood, he should give an offering to the ghosts; having made eight thousand oblations of curd, honey, and ghee to Gaṇapati, he brings the subjects born to himself under subjugation. One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint from the root of red oleander.
He should give an offering with red flowers, perfumes, and presents. He should offer eight thousand oblations with sesame, salt, and ghee; he brings ten villages under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from white oleander, he should offer eight thousand oblations with sesame paste, curd, ghee, milk, and turmeric mixed together; he brings a courtesan under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from the root of an aśvattha tree, given an offering of perfume, flowers, and incense, and offered one hundred oblations, he brings an enemy under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from arka root, he should give offerings of perfume, flowers, and incense.
He should offer one hundred and eight [oblations] of tinduka; he brings an enemy under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint made of bilva root, worshipped [him] with perfume, flowers, and incense, and offered eight thousand oblations smeared with the three sweets, he brings royal ministers under subjugation.
Carrying the incense on one's head, one should go to the king's gate; victory occurs in battle.
One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint made of elephant-tusk earth.
Having worshipped [him] with perfume, flowers, and incense, he should worship [him] becoming naked on the dark fourth [tithi].
He should recite [the mantra] seven times daily; he becomes attractive to women.
One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb from bull-horn earth.
Having worshipped [him] with perfume and flowers, he should give bdellium incense; he brings the lord of the cowherds' settlement under subjugation.
Or else one should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint from anthill earth.
He should smear the image with pungent oil.
Having kindled a fire with datura wood, he should offer eight thousand oblations; he should give all kinds of incense mixed with sesame and mustard; he should smear [the image] with the three pungents.
He should give eaglewood incense; he brings the king under subjugation, and he becomes beloved to others. He should fumigate himself with red sandalwood; he becomes fortunate.
'Oṃ, to Gaṇapati, the crooked-trunked, elephant-tusked, who roars with a gurgling sound, the four-armed, three-eyed, who holds a pestle, noose, and thunderbolt in his hands, tamer of all beings, subjugator of all worlds, causer of injury to all the wicked, crusher of all enemies, desirer of all kingdoms: bring the king here under subjugation! Strike, strike! Cook, cook, with the thunderbolt-goad, Gaṇeśa! Phaṭ! Svāhā!'
'Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ svāhā namaḥ' is the heart of the root mantra.
'Oṃ kaḥ' is the head, 'oṃ khaḥ' is the crest, 'oṃ gaḥ' is the heart, 'oṃ guḥ' is the mouth, 'oṃ gaiṃ' is the eye, 'oṃ ghaḥ' is the armour, 'oṃ ṅa' is the invocation of the heart. The limbs of invocation are: 'oṃ namaḥ' is the heart of the root mantra, 'oṃ gāḥ' is the head, 'oṃ gaiḥ namaḥ' is the crest, 'oṃ gauḥ namaḥ' is the armour, 'oṃ gaṃ namaḥ' is the two eyes, 'oṃ gaḥ phaṭ' is the weapon.
'Oṃ to the thumb-torch svāhā' is the invocation of the heart; 'svāhā' is the dismissal of the heart. 'Oṃ to the perfume-torch svāhā' is the perfume mantra. 'Oṃ to the righteous-being-torch svāhā' is the flower mantra. 'To the unconquerable' on the east; 'oṃ to Dhūrjaṭi' on the south;
'oṃ to the pot-bellied one' on the west; 'oṃ to Gaṇapati' on the north; 'oṃ to the lord of the gaṇas' in the north-east; 'oṃ to Mahāgaṇapati' in the south-east; 'oṃ to Kūśmāṇḍa' in the south-west;
'oṃ to the one-tusked destroyer of Tripura, the three-eyed one' in the north-west. 'Oṃ, we know Mahāgaṇapati, we meditate upon the crooked-trunked one;
may that tusked one impel us!' This is the Gāyatrī.
Having shown the eight hand-gestures—lotus, tusk, rosary, attractor, axe, goad, noose, and kettle-drum—he should then perform the rites.
He should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame; he would bring a king under subjugation.
He should display in sequence the eleven hand-gestures from invocation up to the food offering.
By whatever procedure one should worship Hara, the three-eyed wielder of the trident,
by that very procedure one should worship the divine Vighneśa, the lord of the gaṇas, O king. 1
title: Vināyakapūjāvidhinirūpaṇam

sanskrit_iast:
tadeva maṇḍalaṃ cāsya aṅganyāsastathaiva ca .
ṛte mantrapadānīha samānaṃ sarvameva hi . . 2
meaning:
तदेव मण्डलं चास्य अङ्गन्यासस्तथैव च .
ऋते मन्त्रपदानीह समानं सर्वमेव हि . . 2
text_mt:
His diagram is the very same, and likewise the placement on the limbs;
except for the words of the mantra, everything indeed is the same here. 2

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayedyastu vighneśamekadantamumāsutam .
naśyanti tasya vighnāni na cāriṣṭaṃ kadācana . . 3
meaning:
पूजयेद्यस्तु विघ्नेशमेकदन्तमुमासुतम् .
नश्यन्ति तस्य विघ्नानि न चारिष्टं कदाचन . . 3
text_mt:
Whoever worships Vighneśa, the one-tusked son of Umā,
his obstacles are destroyed, and no calamity ever befalls him. 3

sanskrit_iast:
yaścopavāsaṃ kṛtvā tu caturthyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ .
sarve tasya samārambhāḥ sidhyeyurnātra saṃśayaḥ . .4
meaning:
यश्चोपवासं कृत्वा तु चतुर्थ्यां पूजयेन्नरः .
सर्वे तस्य समारम्भाः सिध्येयुर्नात्र संशयः . .4
text_mt:
And whatever man worships on the fourth [tithi] having fasted,
all his undertakings succeed; there is no doubt about this. 4

sanskrit_iast:
yasyānukūlo vighneśaḥ śivayoḥ kulanandana .
tasyānukūlaṃ sarvaṃ syājjagadvai sarvakarmasu . . 5
meaning:
यस्यानुकूलो विघ्नेशः शिवयोः कुलनन्दन .
तस्यानुकूलं सर्वं स्याज्जगद्वै सर्वकर्मसु . . 5
text_mt:
To whom Vighneśa is favorable, O delighter of the race of Śiva,
to him the entire world becomes favorable in all undertakings. 5

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādārādhayedenaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
kuṅkumāgurudhūpena tathaivoṇḍīrakasrajā . .
3palalollāpikābhiśca jātikonmattakaistathā . . 6
meaning:
तस्मादाराधयेदेनं भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितः .
कुङ्कुमागुरुधूपेन तथैवोण्डीरकस्रजा . .
3पललोल्लापिकाभिश्च जातिकोन्मत्तकैस्तथा . . 6
text_mt:
Therefore, one should worship him endowed with devotion and faith,
with saffron, eaglewood incense, and likewise with a garland of uṇḍīraka,
with sesame sweets and pastries, and likewise with jasmine and datura flowers. 6

sanskrit_iast:
śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vidhinānena pūjayet .
tasya sidhyati nirvighnaṃ sarvakarma na saṃśayaḥ . .7
meaning:
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्थ्यां तु विधिनानेन पूजयेत् .
तस्य सिध्यति निर्विघ्नं सर्वकर्म न संशयः . .7
text_mt:
He should worship on the fourth [tithi] in the bright fortnight according to this procedure;
his every undertaking succeeds without obstacles; there is no doubt. 7

sanskrit_iast:
ekadante jagannāthe gaṇeśe tuṣṭimāgate .
pitṛdevamanuṣyādyāḥ sarve tuṣyanti bhārata . . 8
meaning:
एकदन्ते जगन्नाथे गणेशे तुष्टिमागते .
पितृदेवमनुष्याद्याः सर्वे तुष्यन्ति भारत . . 8
text_mt:
When the one-tusked lord of the world, Gaṇeśa, is pleased,
ancestors, gods, humans, and others are all pleased, O descendant of Bharata. 8

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādārādhayedenaṃ sadā bhaktipuraḥsaram .
karṇalepaistuṇḍikābhirmodakaiśca1 mahīpate . .
pūjayetsatataṃ devaṃ vighnavināśāya dantinam . . 9
meaning:
तस्मादाराधयेदेनं सदा भक्तिपुरःसरम् .
कर्णलेपैस्तुण्डिकाभिर्मोदकैश्च1 महीपते . .
पूजयेत्सततं देवं विघ्नविनाशाय दन्तिनम् . . 9

iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
vināyakapūjāvidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 30 .
śivācaturthī pūjanam

विनायकपूजाविधिनिरूपणं नाम त्रिंशोऽध्यायः . 30 .

text_mt:
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, named 'Description of the Procedure for the Worship of Vināyaka', in the section on the fourth [tithi] in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand [verses]. 30.
Worship on the Śivācaturthī

sanskrit_iast:
sumanturuvāca
śivā śāntā sukhā rājaṃścaturthī trividhā smṛtā .
māsi bhādrapade śuklā śivā lokeṣu pūjitā . . 1
meaning:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
शिवा शान्ता सुखा राजंश्चतुर्थी त्रिविधा स्मृता .
मासि भाद्रपदे शुक्ला शिवा लोकेषु पूजिता . . 1
text_mt:
Sumantu said:
Śivā, Śāntā, and Sukhā: the fourth [tithi] is traditionally declared to be threefold, O king.
The bright [fourth] in the month of Bhādrapada, named Śivā, is worshipped in the worlds. 1
title: Sukhāvahāṅgārakacaturthīvratanirūpaṇam

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāṃ snānaṃ tathā dānamupavāso japastathā .
kriyamāṇaṃ śataguṇaṃ prasādāddantino nṛpa . . 2
meaning:
तस्यां स्नानं तथा दानमुपवासो जपस्तथा .
क्रियमाणं शतगुणं प्रसादाद्दन्तिनो नृप . . 2
text_mt: Bathing, giving gifts, fasting, and recitation of mantras performed on it, / O king, become a hundredfold [more fruitful] through the grace of the Tusked One.

sanskrit_iast:
guḍalavaṇaghṛtānāṃ tu dānaṃ śubhakaraṃ smṛtam .
guḍāpūpaistathā vīra puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇabhojanam . . 3
meaning:
गुडलवणघृतानां तु दानं शुभकरं स्मृतम् .
गुडापूपैस्तथा वीर पुण्यं ब्राह्मणभोजनम् . . 3
text_mt: The gift of jaggery, salt, and clarified butter is considered auspicious; / likewise, O hero, feeding Brahmins with sweet jaggery cakes brings great merit.

sanskrit_iast:
yāstasyāṃ naraśārdūla pūjayanti sadā striyaḥ .
guḍalavaṇapūpaiśca śvaśrūṃ śvasurameva ca . .4
meaning:
यास्तस्यां नरशार्दूल पूजयन्ति सदा स्त्रियः .
गुडलवणपूपैश्च श्वश्रूं श्वसुरमेव च . .4
text_mt: The women who always worship on it, O tiger among men, / their mother-in-law and father-in-law with jaggery, salt, and cakes,

sanskrit_iast:
tāḥ sarvāḥ subhagāḥ syurve1 vighreśasyānumodanāt .
kanyakā tu viśeṣeṇa vidhinānena pūjayet . . 5
meaning:
ताः सर्वाः सुभगाः स्युर्वे1 विघ्रेशस्यानुमोदनात् .
कन्यका तु विशेषेण विधिनानेन पूजयेत् . . 5
text_mt: all of them shall indeed be fortunate through the grace of the Lord of Obstacles. / An unmarried maiden especially should worship according to this procedure.

sanskrit_iast:
( iti śivākalpaḥ)
sumanturuvāca
māghe māsi tathā śuklā yā caturthī mahīpate .
sā śāntā śāntidā nityaṃ śāntiṃ kuryātsadaiva hi . . 6
meaning:
( इति शिवाकल्पः)
सुमन्तुरुवाच
माघे मासि तथा शुक्ला या चतुर्थी महीपते .
सा शान्ता शान्तिदा नित्यं शान्तिं कुर्यात्सदैव हि . . 6
text_mt: (Thus ends the Śivā ritual.) / Sumantu said: / The fourth lunar day in the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, O lord of the earth, / is the Śāntā, the peace-bestower; it always brings peace.

sanskrit_iast:
snānadānādikaṃ karma sarvamasyāṃ kṛtaṃ vibho .
bhavetsahasraguṇitaṃ prasādāttasya2 dantinaḥ . . 7
meaning:
स्नानदानादिकं कर्म सर्वमस्यां कृतं विभो .
भवेत्सहस्रगुणितं प्रसादात्तस्य2 दन्तिनः . . 7
text_mt: Bathing, giving gifts, and all such rites performed on it, O lord, / become multiplied a thousandfold through the grace of that Tusked One.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtopavāso yastasyāṃ pūjayedvi ghnanāyakam .
tasya homādikaṃ karma bhavetsāhasrikaṃ nṛpa . . 8
meaning:
कृतोपवासो यस्तस्यां पूजयेद्वि घ्ननायकम् .
तस्य होमादिकं कर्म भवेत्साहस्रिकं नृप . . 8
text_mt: Whoever, having fasted, worships the Lord of Obstacles on it, / his rites of fire offerings and the like become a thousandfold [more fruitful], O king.

sanskrit_iast:
lavaṇaṃ ca guḍaṃ śākaṃ guḍapūpāṃśca bhārata .
dattvā bhaktyā tu viprebhyaḥ phalaṃ sāhasrikaṃ bhajet3 . . 9
meaning:
लवणं च गुडं शाकं गुडपूपांश्च भारत .
दत्त्वा भक्त्या तु विप्रेभ्यः फलं साहस्रिकं भजेत्3 . . 9
text_mt: Offering salt, jaggery, vegetables, and sweet jaggery cakes / with devotion to Brahmins, O Bhārata, one obtains a thousandfold fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣataḥ striyo rājanpūjayanto guruṃ nṛpa .
guḍalavaṇaghṛtairvīra sadā syurbhāgyasaṃyutāḥ4 . . 1.31.10
meaning:
विशेषतः स्त्रियो राजन्पूजयन्तो गुरुं नृप .
गुडलवणघृतैर्वीर सदा स्युर्भाग्यसंयुताः4 . . 1.31.10
text_mt: Especially women, O king, who worship the elder / with jaggery, salt, and clarified butter, O hero, will always be endowed with good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
( iti śāntākalpaḥ)
sumanturuvāca
sukhāvahā ca susukhā saubhāgyakaraṇī param . . 11
meaning:
( इति शान्ताकल्पः)
सुमन्तुरुवाच
सुखावहा च सुसुखा सौभाग्यकरणी परम् . . 11
text_mt: (Thus ends the Śāntā ritual.) / Sumantu said: / It brings happiness, is very pleasant, and is supreme in creating good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
caturthī kuruśārdūla rūpasaubhāgyadā śubhā .
sukhāvrataṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ rūpadaṃ bhāgyadaṃ tathā . . 12
meaning:
चतुर्थी कुरुशार्दूल रूपसौभाग्यदा शुभा .
सुखाव्रतं महापुण्यं रूपदं भाग्यदं तथा . . 12
text_mt: The fourth lunar day, O tiger of the Kurus, bestows beauty, good fortune, and auspiciousness. / The Sukhā observance brings great merit, conferring beauty and good fortune;

sanskrit_iast:
susūkṣmaṃ sukaraṃ dhanyamiha puṇyasukhāvaham .
paratra phaladaṃ vīra divyarūpapradāyakam . . 13
meaning:
सुसूक्ष्मं सुकरं धन्यमिह पुण्यसुखावहम् .
परत्र फलदं वीर दिव्यरूपप्रदायकम् . . 13
text_mt: it is subtle, easy to perform, praiseworthy, bringing meritorious happiness here [in this world], / and granting fruit in the next world, O hero, bestowing a celestial form.

sanskrit_iast:
hasitaṃ lalitaṃ coktaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ ca sukhāvaham .
savilāsabhujakṣepaścaṃkramaśceṣṭitaṃ śubham . . 14
meaning:
हसितं ललितं चोक्तं चेष्टितं च सुखावहम् .
सविलासभुजक्षेपश्चंक्रमश्चेष्टितं शुभम् . . 14
text_mt: Laughter, grace, and movements are said to bring happiness; / graceful swinging of the arms and elegant walking are auspicious movements.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhāvratena sarveṣāṃ sukhaṃ kurukulodvaha .

meaning:
सुखाव्रतेन सर्वेषां सुखं कुरुकुलोद्वह .
कृत्येन पूजिते चेशे विघ्रेशे शिवयोः सुते . . 15
text_mt: Through the Sukhā observance, happiness comes to all, O scion of the Kuru race, / when the Lord, the Lord of Obstacles, the son of Śiva and Pārvatī, is worshipped according to the rite.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā śuklacaturthyāṃ tu vāro bhaumasya vai bhavet .
tadā sā sukhadā jñeyā caturthī vai sukheti ca . . 16
meaning:
यदा शुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु वारो भौमस्य वै भवेत् .
तदा सा सुखदा ज्ञेया चतुर्थी वै सुखेति च . . 16
text_mt: When a Tuesday coincides with the fourth lunar day of the bright fortnight, / then that fourth lunar day is known as bestowing happiness, and indeed as Sukhā.

sanskrit_iast:
purā maithunamāśritya sthitābhyāṃ tu himācale .

meaning:
पुरा मैथुनमाश्रित्य स्थिताभ्यां तु हिमाचले .
भीमोमाभ्यां महाबाहो रक्तबिन्दुश्च्युतः क्षितौ . . 17
text_mt: Long ago, as Śiva and Umā were engaged in union upon the Himālayas, / O mighty-armed one, a drop of blood fell upon the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
medinyāṃ sa prayatnena sukhe vidhṛto'nayā .
jātosyāḥ sa kujo vīra rakto raktasamudbhavaḥ . . 18
meaning:
मेदिन्यां स प्रयत्नेन सुखे विधृतोऽनया .
जातोस्याः स कुजो वीर रक्तो रक्तसमुद्भवः . . 18
text_mt: She carefully held it in comfort upon the earth; / from her Kuja was born, O hero, red, born from blood.

sanskrit_iast:
mamāṅgato yathotpannastasmādaṅgārako hyayam .
aṅgadoṅgopakāraśca aṅgānāṃ tu prado nṛṇām . . 19
meaning:
ममाङ्गतो यथोत्पन्नस्तस्मादङ्गारको ह्ययम् .
अङ्गदोङ्गोपकारश्च अङ्गानां तु प्रदो नृणाम् . . 19
text_mt: Since he was born from my limb, he is indeed called Aṅgāraka. / He gives limbs, benefits the limbs, and bestows limbs upon men;

sanskrit_iast:
saubhāgyādikaro yasmāttasmādaṅgārako mataḥ .
bhaktyā caturthyāṃ naktena yo vai śraddhāsamanvitaḥ . . 1.31.20
meaning:
सौभाग्यादिकरो यस्मात्तस्मादङ्गारको मतः .
भक्त्या चतुर्थ्यां नक्तेन यो वै श्रद्धासमन्वितः . . 1.31.20
text_mt: because he brings good fortune and other blessings, he is regarded as Aṅgāraka. / Whoever with devotion, fasting during the day and eating at night on the fourth lunar day, endowed with faith,

sanskrit_iast:
upavatsyati nā rājannārī vā nānyamānasā .
pūjayecca kujaṃ bhaktayā raktapuṣpavilepanaiḥ . . 21
meaning:
उपवत्स्यति ना राजन्नारी वा नान्यमानसा .
पूजयेच्च कुजं भक्तया रक्तपुष्पविलेपनैः . . 21
text_mt: a man or a woman, O king, with an undistracted mind, / should worship Kuja with devotion, using red flowers and unguents.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇeśaṃ prathamaṃ bhaktyā yojayecchaddhayānvitaḥ .
yasya tuṣṭaḥ prayacchetsa saubhāgyaṃ rūpasampadam . . 22
meaning:
गणेशं प्रथमं भक्त्या योजयेच्छद्धयान्वितः .
यस्य तुष्टः प्रयच्छेत्स सौभाग्यं रूपसम्पदम् . . 22
text_mt: First, one endowed with faith should worship Gaṇeśa with devotion; / pleased with him, he will bestow good fortune and the wealth of beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvaṃ ca kṛtasaṅkalpaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .
gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ vandenmantreṇānena bhārata . . 23
meaning:
पूर्वं च कृतसङ्कल्पः स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि .
गृहीत्वा मृत्तिकां वन्देन्मन्त्रेणानेन भारत . . 23
text_mt: Having first made the solemn vow and bathed according to rule, / taking up clay, one should salute it with this mantra, O Bhārata:

sanskrit_iast:
iha tvaṃ vanditā pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇenoddharatā kila .
tasmānme daha pāpmānaṃ yanmayā pūrvasañcitam . . 24
meaning:
इह त्वं वन्दिता पूर्वं कृष्णेनोद्धरता किल .
तस्मान्मे दह पाप्मानं यन्मया पूर्वसञ्चितम् . . 24
text_mt: ‘Here you were praised long ago by Kṛṣṇa as he lifted you up; / therefore, burn away the sin accumulated by me in the past.’

sanskrit_iast:
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra ādityāya pradarśayet .
ādityaraśmisampūtāṃ gaṅgājalakaṇokṣitām . . 25
meaning:
इमं मन्त्रं पठन्वीर आदित्याय प्रदर्शयेत् .
आदित्यरश्मिसम्पूतां गङ्गाजलकणोक्षिताम् . . 25
text_mt: Reciting this mantra, O hero, one should show [the clay] to the Sun, / purified by the rays of the Sun and sprinkled with drops of Gaṅgā water.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā mṛdaṃ śirasi tāṃ sarvāṅgeṣu ca yojayet .
tataḥ snānaṃ prakurvīta mantrayeta jalaṃ punaḥ . . 26
meaning:
दत्त्वा मृदं शिरसि तां सर्वाङ्गेषु च योजयेत् .
ततः स्नानं प्रकुर्वीत मन्त्रयेत जलं पुनः . . 26
text_mt: Placing that clay on the head, one should apply it to all one's limbs. / Then one should bathe and again consecrate the water with mantras:

sanskrit_iast:
tvamāpo yoniḥ sarveṣāṃ daityadānavadyaukasām .
svedāṇḍajodbhidāṃ caiva rasānāṃ pataye namaḥ . . 27
meaning:
त्वमापो योनिः सर्वेषां दैत्यदानवद्यौकसाम् .
स्वेदाण्डजोद्भिदां चैव रसानां पतये नमः . . 27
text_mt: ‘You, O waters, are the source of all—of Daityas, Dānavas, and celestials, / and of the sweat-born, egg-born, and sprouting beings. Homage to the Lord of juices!’

sanskrit_iast:
snāto'haṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvaprasravaṇeṣu ca .
taḍāgeṣu ca sarveṣu mānasādisaraḥsu ca . . 28
meaning:
स्नातोऽहं सर्वतीर्थेषु सर्वप्रस्रवणेषु च .
तडागेषु च सर्वेषु मानसादिसरःसु च . . 28
text_mt: ‘I have bathed in all sacred water sites, in all waterfalls, / in all ponds, and in lakes such as Mānasa;

sanskrit_iast:
nadīṣu devakhāteṣu sutīrtheṣu hradeṣu vai .
dhyāyanyaṭhannimaṃ mantraṃ tataḥ snānaṃ samācaret . . 29
meaning:
नदीषु देवखातेषु सुतीर्थेषु ह्रदेषु वै .
ध्यायन्यठन्निमं मन्त्रं ततः स्नानं समाचरेत् . . 29
text_mt: in rivers, in divine excavations, in sacred fords, and in deep pools.’ / Meditating and reciting this mantra, one should then perform the bath.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā gṛhamāgatya vai spṛśet .
dūrvāśvatthau śamīṃ spṛṣṭvā gāṃ ca mantreṇa mantravit . . 1.31.30
meaning:
ततः स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा गृहमागत्य वै स्पृशेत् .
दूर्वाश्वत्थौ शमीं स्पृष्ट्वा गां च मन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् . . 1.31.30
text_mt: Then, having bathed and become pure, one should come home and touch; / having touched dūrvā grass, an aśvattha tree, and a śamī tree, the knower of mantras should touch a cow with the mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
dūrvā namasya mantreṇa śucau bhūmau samutthitām .
tvaṃ dūrve'mṛtanāmāsi sarvadevaistu vanditā . . 31
meaning:
दूर्वा नमस्य मन्त्रेण शुचौ भूमौ समुत्थिताम् .
त्वं दूर्वेऽमृतनामासि सर्वदेवैस्तु वन्दिता . . 31
text_mt: One should salute the dūrvā grass growing on pure ground with the mantra: / ‘O dūrvā, you are named nectar, praised by all the gods;

sanskrit_iast: vanditā daha tatsarvaṃ duritaṃ yanmayā1 kṛtam . . 32
meaning: वन्दिता दह तत्सर्वं दुरितं यन्मया1 कृतम् . . 32
text_mt: praised [by me], burn away all that evil which was done by me.’

sanskrit_iast:
śamīmantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tannibodha mahīpate .
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitrāṃ tvaṃ kāśyapī prathitā śrutau . .
śamī śamaya me pāpaṃ nūnaṃ vetsi dharādharān . . 33
meaning:
शमीमन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्निबोध महीपते .
पवित्राणां पवित्रां त्वं काश्यपी प्रथिता श्रुतौ . .
शमी शमय मे पापं नूनं वेत्सि धराधरान् . . 33
text_mt: I shall state the śamī mantra; listen to it, O lord of the earth: / ‘You are the purest of pure things, renowned as Kāśyapī in sacred tradition; / O śamī, pacify my sin; surely you know the mountains.’

sanskrit_iast:
aśvatthālambhane vīra mantrametaṃ nibodha me .
netraspandādijaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥsvapnaṃ durvicintanam . .
śaktānāṃ ca samudyogamaśvattha tvaṃ kṣamasva me . . 34
meaning:
अश्वत्थालम्भने वीर मन्त्रमेतं निबोध मे .
नेत्रस्पन्दादिजं दुःखं दुःस्वप्नं दुर्विचिन्तनम् . .
शक्तानां च समुद्योगमश्वत्थ त्वं क्षमस्व मे . . 34
text_mt: In touching the aśvattha tree, O hero, learn this mantra from me: / ‘The distress born from eye-twitching and the like, bad dreams, evil thoughts, / and the enterprise of powerful enemies—O aśvattha, forgive it for me.’

sanskrit_iast:
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra kuryādvai sparśanaṃ budhaḥ .
tato devyai tu gāṃ dadyādvīraṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇām . .
samālabhya tu hastena tato mantramudīrayet . . 35
meaning:
इमं मन्त्रं पठन्वीर कुर्याद्वै स्पर्शनं बुधः .
ततो देव्यै तु गां दद्याद्वीरं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणाम् . .
समालभ्य तु हस्तेन ततो मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् . . 35
text_mt: Reciting this mantra, O hero, the wise person should touch [it]. / Then, having circumambulated a white cow clockwise, / and touching it with the hand, one should recite the mantra:

sanskrit_iast:
sarvadevamayī devi munibhistu supūjitā .
tasmātspṛśāmi vande tvāṃ vanditā pāpahā bhava . . 36
meaning:
सर्वदेवमयी देवि मुनिभिस्तु सुपूजिता .
